proofs.title: Reachable-state invariant preservation
proofs.statement: Every permitted transition preserves a meaningful invariant from valid initial/reachable states.
proofs.progress_note: Actual finite node traces preserve state and prior bindings; mixed live file/node traces including refusal, known abort and recovery preserve the phase/history relation. The host-called store prepare projection now preserves that relation after observed open across the actual post-open mutators without replaying the appended history per prepare. Provenance, complete runtime guards and physical refinement remain open. BP joint durable/pending sender binding and fixed-Store receiver state/context/decision invariants now hold through actual transitions and arbitrary finite replay; changing-Store composition remains open. CHANGED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-snt-relation` (books/store-node-traces) now covers the two publications whose node effect is deferred to `fn-sn-finish` -- `fn-sn-prepare-retention` (`6ab2c783`) and `fn-sn-prepare-identity` (`4bb7bb3d`) -- and the fault arm `fn-sn-recover` grew in `40bb3f74`. Before this it was false of every state those three transitions produce, so `fn-snrt-step-preserves-relation`, `fn-own-step-preserves-relation` and `fn-opc-configured-step-preserves-owner-relation` above it were false with it and no run had said so. What the deferred arm says is weaker than the article arm by design: it carries the replayed node at the reservation's transaction id and the equation between the applied event and the replay of the extended history, and no proposal standing on the live node, because there is none until the directory barrier.

proofs.title: Atomic allocation and stable numbering
proofs.statement: Acceptance publishes all intended local memberships together and never reuses an allocated number for another article.
proofs.progress_note: Atomic logical publication and stable number/binding lemmas; persistent/reclamation integration remains open. OVER THE SERVED PATH (books/owner-numbering.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-own-served-watermarks-never-decrease -- under fn-own-relation of the configured owner, for any group, any sequence of writer events ((:take), (:begin id), (:store e), (:complete)) through fn-ocfg-step (fn-owner-step, host/owner-host.lisp:209) followed by any connection's outcome installed with fn-ocfg-with-owner (fn-owner-replace-core) leaves the committed view's next local number for that group at least what it was; fn-own-served-local-number-is-never-reassigned -- over the same calls, a (group . number) that names an article of the committed view names an article with the same Message-ID afterwards. The committed view is the archive every reader pins when it opens or advances and reads through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix (owner-host.lisp:1240). Proof: the view is the replay of a prefix of the durable records and the records only grow (fn-own-step-records-prefix); replaying a longer prefix only conses articles on the front and only raises watermarks; the Message-ID half cites fn-state-has-fresh-local-numbers on the new view. Teeth (tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests.lisp): witness of two POSTs in fn.letters across a completion (numbers 3 and 4, watermark 3 to 5, 1 and 2 keep their Message-IDs, the advanced reader's GROUP 211 4 1 4 and STAT 3/4 name the new articles); must-fail for the relation on both keystones (the store node's archive wound back to empty: the 240 is still answered, fn.letters 1 is given again and the watermark falls from 3 to 2) and for the holder hypothesis (fn.letters 3 unheld before, held after). The writer-events hypothesis has no tooth: no violating value was found (every other fn-ocfg-step arm keeps the view or refreshes it from an extension of the records), and redundancy is not proved; it is the statement's scope. SCOPE of fn-own-pinned-view-survives-other-post (T6): reader connections only, by design -- a peer connection answers IHAVE/CHECK from the live node (fn-own-conn-live-session), so a POST by another connection correctly changes its 335 to 435; tests/acl2/owner-served-invariants-tests shows it. No peer-connection variant is owed. EVIDENCE: persvati run-20260924T152353Z-e987, manifest planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260924T152452Z-1758763.json: books/owner-numbering 4.1 s, tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests 4.3 s, both passed. RESTATED BY control-c3b (2026-09-25), when the committed view began serving the visible state (a cancel withdraws its target from what readers see, books/control-visible.lisp): fn-own-raw-local-number-is-never-reassigned is the former statement over the view's raw list (fn-own-view-raw, the acceptance articles, withdrawn ones included): a (group . number) held there names the same Message-ID after the same calls. fn-own-served-local-number-is-never-reassigned now says a number held in the served (visible) list is held afterwards by the same Message-ID or by nothing (withdrawn); it is never given to another article. The former equality over the served list is false once a cancel executes. fn-own-served-watermarks-never-decrease is unchanged (the visible state keeps the acceptance watermarks). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests.lisp, both holder keystones with the relation and the held-before must-fails; the fixture has no cancel, so the served keystone's nothing arm has no witness there. Record: planning/evidence/control-c3b-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.title: Identity and idempotent acceptance
proofs.statement: Retrying an accepted identity preserves its binding and introduces no duplicate allocation or obligation.
proofs.progress_note: Exact logical identity bindings and retries covered; native identities, signatures, and durable protocol retry path remain open. T3 places the duplicate/conflict/missing branch decision in fn-sn-existing-action, the function all four host prepare/query sites call, with exact case theorems and reachable teeth in store-node-existing-invariants/tests. Those direct case equations are not counted here as keystones for the broader no-allocation/no-obligation property; composed native retry qualification remains open. Since D25 (2026-09-24) the host calls fn-pb-existing-action (books/poster-bytes.lisp), which keys on the poster's bytes and refines fn-sn-existing-action; the case theorems of the host-called decision are in books/poster-bytes-invariants.lisp.

proofs.title: Reservation and release safety
proofs.statement: Accepted obligations are accounted for and discharge requires the specified predicate over committed authorized evidence.
proofs.progress_note: Finite abstract admission and general release preserve valid ledgers; release preserves independent pins and known identities. P9 over the host-called functions (books/store-node-retention.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-spc-prepare (host/store-node-host.lisp:472, answered :refused at :475 when it returns its input) returns the live store state unchanged whenever the record's charge exceeds the room the node's retention capacity leaves, with that comparison its only hypothesis; fn-node-prepare does the same; fn-node-prepare-refuses-whatever-retain-admit-refuses is the named equation that makes RET-002's fn-retain-admit-refuses-unaffordable-obligation a statement about the called function (fn-retain-admit's no-op is exactly the inadmissible case, and in that case prepare refuses). fn-sn-finish (store-node-host.lisp:546): every article accepted before a completion is accepted after it on every arm (no hypothesis beyond membership), and an obligation leaves the ledger only when the completed record is a retention release, not an undertaking, matching its id, subject, kind and evidence; Store releases name kind :forward, so no arm releases an article's :archive pin (corollary fn-sn-finish-keeps-every-archive-obligation). Teeth: tests/acl2/store-node-retention-tests.lisp, reachable witnesses from fn-sn-initial through the host's io/prepare/finish (capacity 10, 2 reserved, charge 9 refused and 8 staged; article, undertaking and release arms) and one must-fail per hypothesis; the identity, consumer and topic arms have no concrete witness. Scope: charges are abstract units, not physical bytes; there is no archive-release event in v0, so 'until explicit release' is 'kept' for articles; crash/recover and sweep are not covered here. Authorized/committed evidence validation remains open. M5 transaction budget over the called prepare (books/owner-store-budget.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-sbud-prepare, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare installs, is the identity when the budget is at most the owner Store's committed record count and is fn-opc-prepare below it; its refusal word is :unaffordable; the budget is the persisted profile's admissibility (fn-sbud-budget-is-the-profile-admissibility) and is fixed at init. Teeth in tests/acl2/owner-store-budget-tests.lisp and tests/acl2/store-budget-tests.lisp; farm manifest certify-20260924T161235Z-2188032. Second count and payload constant removed (books/store-budget-naming.lisp, 2026-09-24): the host names each transaction file from the staged candidate's sequence, fn-sbud-pending-sequence (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-pending-sequence, host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-pending-sequence), through fn-sbud-txn-name, the scan's fn-bs-txn-name; in a record phase of a well-formed kernel that sequence is the committed count (fn-sbud-pending-sequence-is-used) and the name extends the committed namespace to one fn-bs-txn-observation-pairs accepts at sequence used (fn-sbud-pending-name-is-the-scans-next-name). The POST boundary both entries call is fn-sbud-post-boundary over the persisted profile, admitting exactly the payloads at or under the profile's payload field (fn-sbud-post-boundary-refuses-exactly-past-the-profile-bound); the served owner relays :payload-bound as the Store word :refused, whose 441 line is W3's. Teeth in tests/acl2/store-budget-naming-tests.lisp over an owner reached by its own transitions; farm manifest certify-20260924T182844Z-3383029.

proofs.title: Codec and identity preimages
proofs.statement: Accepted values round-trip; deterministic encodings and domain-separated preimages have the specified uniqueness and version boundaries.
proofs.progress_note: The record codec now supports schema 0 (:legacy) and schema 1 (bounded acceptance stamp), with round-trip, canonicality and legacy-byte witnesses certified in the T2a lane. The combined native image and migration witness remain open. The codec evidence is scoped to its admitted grammars; unknown-record opaque preservation and complete native signature/Store integration are not established by it. The separate hybrid-carrier evidence describes exact-source serialization and its remaining universal round-trip obligation. D27 codec ceilings (packet P2, lane/bounds-p2-ceilings, 2026-09-25): the record codec writes and reads every byte string through the CBOR bounded API at the record width (fn-record-item-encode, fn-record-item-decode, books/records.lisp), so the record is no longer capped by the generic entry's 65,535-octet item; fn-record-impl-round-trip and fn-record-impl-accepted-input-is-canonical keep their statements over it, fn-record-item-stream-bytes-round-trip is the item round trip at any length up to the u32 record width, fn-record-item-encode-is-cbor-encode keeps every record of at most 65,535-octet items byte-identical (the schema-0 golden vector is unchanged), and the seam constraint fn-record-encode-length-bound bounds a record's encoding by fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count. Teeth: tests/acl2/records-ceiling-tests.lisp (a 70,000-octet payload and a 460-octet group name round-trip; the generic decoder refuses the u32-headed item; a must-fail per round-trip hypothesis). Scope: the codec ceilings (record 2^32-1, payload 2^32-2^25, 65,535 groups, 460-octet names) are widths, not the operator's bounds; until packet P1 the served bound is the profile's payload field (32,768 in every named profile). Evidence: planning/evidence/bounds-p2-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.progress_note: Fixed-mode framing composition, production event-yield preservation and exact consumed-prefix/suffix accounting are certified. Wildmat DP matches independent anchored semantics. Session-sensitive mode changes and complete protocol/effect refinement remain open. The served path is now the subject: books/served states partition independence of fn-served-step and of the whole reply stream, which is the function tools/run_reader.py calls once per socket read, so the wire pending_subject note is closed for framing. The owner book now certifies in the merged feed/transit batch recorded by planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260921T051833Z-3941584.json. This does not extend these framing theorems to an unproved owner composition or to Python outbound article rendering; W12 wire-block owns that running-path extension. The W14 cumulative byte-feeder induction now proves successful outbound block source preservation through fn-wire-drive and the actual fn-wire-render-feed-command article arm under the exact served article-start profile. Its hypotheses require positive command profile, the nonempty article arm excluding CHECK/IHAVE/TAKETHIS command prefixes, renderer success, and the article limit no greater than receiver body limit; tests separate each premise. This is not a new proof of later authentication/injection dispatch or durable acceptance. The native counted fast transition is now integrated: fn-served-step-counted-fast-is-reference is certified under the maintained full wire invariant, with a malformed-retained-byte separating witness. Per-read entry checks only the fixed wire spine and scalars. The changed outer fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read correspondence is pending current-source certification; the focused served closure excludes that owner book. See planning/evidence/native-served-fast-path-w26-2026-09-21.md. CLOSED AS STATED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read` now certifies with the premise `fn-served-step-counted-fast-is-reference` asks for -- `fn-wire-statep` of the found connection's wire. The configured owner does not carry it: `fn-own-conn-okp` (books/owner-invariants) requires a shape, a bounded session and a pinned archive and says nothing about the wire recognizer, while `fn-served-connp` is the predicate that does. The two transitions agree on every wire the full recognizer accepts and may differ on one the fast spine accepts and it does not. proofs.title: Conditional crash recovery
proofs.statement: Under the disk model, recovery retains acknowledged commits, may retain complete unacknowledged commits, and exposes no partial transaction.
proofs.progress_note: Arbitrary mixed live/file traces including refusal/abort preserve exact ready-state replay and prior acknowledged records, conditional on the kernel crash model. Observed-image opening uses actual recovery with no fabricated acknowledgements or barriers; zero through four barriers remain gated, the fifth opens ready. Host adoption passed the integrated suite; physical byte correspondence, freshness and platform qualification remain separate from these targeted proofs. Receiver logical replay now preserves exact contexts and committed receipt ADUs against a fixed Store. Five actual receiver process-death cuts passed in the 133-test suite; process death is separate from power loss and general FNWF/FNRJ byte/live/replay refinement. Fencing, barrier and retention keystones are unchanged in statement and now run with the whole-state recognizers off the executable path (24 calls to 0 in the store cluster, 10 to 0 in core), carried under mbe instead. Real process evidence: the deploy gate SIGKILLed the server inside an open POST and the acknowledged article reread byte-for-byte after recovery. Byte-level torn writes remain the DESIGN-crash-model-v2 design, which is review finding D4. OPEN AND CHANGED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-snrt-new-success-is-actual-matching-durable-completion` keeps its safety conjuncts at full strength for all three arms of `fn-sn-finish` -- a new acknowledgement comes only from `:finish` and only under an enabled completion -- and makes its article-specific conclusions (the bound record, the `fn-node-complete` equation, the committed record) conditional on the acceptance arm, as the keystone it uses already does since `6ab2c783` and `4bb7bb3d` gave the completion record a retention and an identity kind whose node transition is not a completion and whose article accessors name nothing. `fn-sn-known-abort` CHANGED BEHAVIOUR in the same lane: `6ab2c783` gave it a retention arm that left the live node alone, so an aborted retention publication returned a `:ready` state whose node sat one transaction id behind its own durable frontier, which `fn-snt-relation` forbids and `fn-own-idle-node-is-replay` relies on; the arm now advances the node over the id the abort consumes, exactly as `fn-sn-refuse-reservation` does over a refused reservation, and `tests/acl2/store-identity-traces-tests` carries the witness. RESTATED 2026-09-23 (red/bpre): `fn-bprv-history-record-is-node-committed-when-idle` now carries `(fn-record-p record)`: since `6ab2c783` and `346a8f99` a Store history holds retention and statement events beside article records, those install no article under their own name, and `tests/acl2/bp-receiver-evolving-tests` commits a retention undertake on a related `:ready` Store where the old statement is false; the loop keystone `fn-bprv-apply-store-event-keeps-committed` now covers every arm of `fn-replay-apply-record`. `fn-bprv-evolving-invariant-survives-observed-reopen` and `fn-bpr-live-receipt-regenerated-after-restart` now carry `fn-sn-observed-identity-okp` of the image's records, the kernel's own reopen hypothesis since `4857c648`; OPEN: no ground witness separates it under `fn-snt-relation` plus `fn-sf-crash-imagep` (the live prepare checks the identity step, so it may be derivable there), so that hypothesis has no must-fail tooth, and deriving it from the relation would lift it from every kernel reopen guarantee at once. INTERIM 2026-09-24 (BP observed reopen): fn-bprv-observed-reopen-facts, fn-bprv-evolving-invariant-survives-observed-reopen, and fn-bpr-live-receipt-regenerated-after-restart now require fn-sn-observed-topic-okp(records), matching the actual Store observed opener after topic events were added. The existing consumer relation and identity premises do not establish the independent topic replay check; Store tests exhibit structurally valid topic-invalid records, while a counterexample under the full crash-image hypothesis and a reachable-state derivation remain separate obligations. The conditional BP book and dependent test certify at manifests 050516 and 050842. A maintained Store topic/crash relation deriving this premise on reachable images is still open in this packet; these conditional theorems do not establish full BP reopen. Host tie (books/store-open-bridge.lisp, k4-bridges lane): the cited keystones stay the registry events; fn-cpo-open-observed-is-sn-open-observed-on-the-kernel and fn-cpo-open-observed-succeeds-exactly are the named theorems relating them to fn-cpo-open-observed, which host/store-node-host.lisp:159 and host/owner-host.lisp:193 call. Corollaries (the host's subject, not registry events): fn-sn-open-observed-success-exact-history -> fn-sn-open-observed-success-exact-history-of-host-open (kernel conjuncts only; the node conjunct does not transfer); fn-sn-open-observed-not-ready-before-five-barriers and fn-sn-open-observed-five-barriers-open-ready -> their -of-host-open corollaries (over fn-cpo-open-observed success alone, from the bridge kernel fact and the same generic barrier lemmas); fn-sn-acknowledged-record-survives-observed-reopen -> -of-host-open (added hypothesis fn-sob-configured-openp); fn-bprv-evolving-invariant-survives-observed-reopen -> -of-host-open (the fn-bprv-evolving-invariantp conjunct; fn-snt-relation does not transfer); fn-sn-open-observed-success-has-live-history-relation and fn-bpr-live-receipt-regenerated-after-restart: NOT transferred (both state fn-snt-relation or a run from the opened node, and the host's node is the configured replay's); the host-side relation is fn-cpo-open-observed-success-has-history-relation. K4 NODE CORRESPONDENCE (k0-steps, books/store-open-node-bridge.lisp): when every configuration record names txid 0 (fn-sonb-configured-before-eventsp: configured before the first Store event, never reconfigured after one), fn-sonb-configured-replay-is-fixed-table-replay shows the configured replay is the fixed-table replay under the final domain and capacity, and so fn-snt-relation holds of the host's opened state (fn-sn-open-observed-success-has-live-history-relation-of-host-open), the node conjunct holds at the host's open (fn-sn-open-observed-success-exact-history-node-of-host-open), and the receipt theorem holds with the restart through fn-cpo-open-observed (fn-bpr-live-receipt-regenerated-after-restart-of-host-open). Without that hypothesis the opened node is fn-cst-replay-node (fn-sn-open-observed-success-configured-node-of-host-open) and fn-snt-relation can fail: a release followed by a capacity reduction at txid 7 opens on the host and is refused by the final-table replay (store-open-node-bridge-tests, config-observed-tests). A reconfigured store's live relation is fn-cst-relation; the BP receipt theorem is not stated over it.

proofs.title: Checkpoint equivalence
proofs.statement: Checkpoint plus suffix recovery preserves the required logical state of full committed-history replay.
proofs.progress_note: Logical capture preserves the exact prefix node; general admissible-split restore equivalence includes allocator gaps and frontier normalization. Native capture/select/reopen runs after authoritative full journal replay and compares checkpoint restoration in private state. The W15 namespace successor moves canonical names, bounded observation, allocation and selection limits into ACL2, reports every differential mismatch as corruption, and preserves Store fencing after ambiguous publication/replacement. Source-pinned native and development-adapter tests cover named corruption, cross-open and crash cases. Suffix-only recovery, shared-owner/index composition, every-cut physical correspondence and freshness/platform qualification remain open. The version-two auxiliary checker compares a reopened Store, including topic projection and the rebuilt consumer sequence index, to an independent full exact-history replay after the selected node-checkpoint differential. Its ACL2 book and witness certify, but this runtime equality check is not a general checkpoint-plus-suffix theorem for auxiliary fields; the existing exact-prefix pack theorem supplies the byte-history preservation premise. Native combined-image and clone-activation evidence remain open.

proofs.title: Compaction and protected closure
proofs.statement: Reclamation and crash-interrupted compaction preserve every dependency rooted by policy and obligations.
proofs.progress_note: The implemented physical tranche retains exact canonical event bytes in one immutable selected pack, validates every surviving covered record, accepts only missing files within the covered prefix, requires a contiguous uncovered suffix, and resumes exact prefix unlink under the writer lease. fn-cc-partial-deletion-preserves-exact-history covers arbitrary missing subsets of that prefix under summary, suffix and exact-observation hypotheses; its test has a non-degenerate middle deletion and one must-fail event per hypothesis. The aggregate parser refuses above 4 MiB before header parsing and its focused test round-trips a valid pack larger than the generic 65538-octet CBOR input cap. Selected namespace and exact-overlap helper guards are verified; guard closure of the actual framed coverage/observation caller remains open on the shared unverified Store-event decoder chain. The definition-unfolding prefix-plus-suffix equality is deliberately not a registry event. One pack is limited to 4096 events and 4 MiB, so this exact-history representation cannot compact arbitrarily large stores. Open: a general crash correspondence theorem, active-reader coordination, protected article-object closure, filesystem qualification, and integrated native-image execution. The byte crash correspondence now transcribes the actual native reclaim plan as repeated transaction-directory unlinks with a post-unlink cut and a closing directory fence with a post-barrier cut. Executable witnesses show arbitrary covered-name survival before the fence, no restoration after it, exact suffix retention, and conflict refusal. The native caller now invokes the logical plan subject directly; recovery continues through fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe. Source mapping and model witnesses are not integrated native-image evidence; source-matched process-death execution and filesystem qualification remain open. The actual reclaim planner now uses total nested-pair accessors and has explicit guard events, with source-LD evidence and malformed-input witnesses. The modeled crash examples execute the actual planner through a test helper; no hand-written substitute program supplies their run. These source checks do not certify the complete dependency closure or establish general suffix preservation under all physical crashes. No event yet; T12d (009 stays v1). The scoped ACL2 pack-retirement book proves the selected generation survives every modeled issued-unlink cut under plan-prefix and selected-membership premises, and that a valid gap-aware next generation exceeds the selected name when not exhausted. Its test book supplies a multi-generation deletion witness and counterexamples to the keystone premises. The native caller uses the proved plan under the exclusive Store lock, with one cut after each unlink and one after the packs-directory barrier; an empty plan returns without a cut. The follow-up count theorems state that surviving unlinks reduce bounded pack namespace occupancy, without authorizing retained-history or article-object deletion. Native image execution and syscall/power-loss correspondence remain open.

proofs.title: Guard and execution correspondence
proofs.statement: Guard-verified concrete operations used by the host implement their logical counterparts on the stated domains.
proofs.progress_note: The standalone native store wrapper calls fn-spc-prepare, and the shared native owner now calls fn-opc-prepare from fn-owner-prepare. The two registered equality keystones connect those exact host-called subjects to fn-sn-prepare and to the former configured-owner prepare event under the maintained store and owner relations. Observed recovery establishes the owner premise through fn-own-start and fn-own-configure; configured-owner steps and direct socket entries preserve it. The executable path retains candidate and pending binding checks while omitting appended-history replay and all relation/whole-state recognizers. Exact owner/configuration context and pending bytes are preserved. Full physical byte/effect correspondence, a saved-image native-owner gate for this revision, and platform qualification remain open. OCL at open (2026-09-24): fn-orec-recover-installs-ocl-relation (books/owner-recover-ocl) proves, over the composition fn-owner-recover calls (host/owner-host.lisp:186 fn-cpr-replay, :191 fn-cpo-open-observed, :195-201 fn-ocfg-make of fn-own-configure of fn-own-start with fn-oag-post-config), that the installed owner satisfies fn-ocl-relation and fn-scar-view-indexedp under (natp max-conns) and the open's kind :ok, both checked by the host before it installs; the remaining host checks are implied. It is the first link of the carried served keystones stated under fn-ocl-relation (fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-reference-under-ocl-relation, fn-acar-own-outcome-is-reference-under-ocl-relation). Certified on persvati run-20260924T221249Z-f2d3, manifest certify-20260924T221303Z-1169743 (owner-recover-ocl 4.3 s, its tests 4.1 s). Representation, first boundary (2026-09-25): fn-rcon-record-p-is-record-p (books/records-concrete) equates the record recognizer that reads its strings in place (no octet list built: the octet-domain test is stringp, the bounds are length, the ASCII walk is by index) with fn-record-p, on every input with no hypothesis, both guard-verified at guard t; the eight twins of the dispatchers, the record pair, the binding test and the two projection steps are each equal to their reference with no hypothesis, and books/owner-commit-carried (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission calls fn-ccar-own-finish) and books/owner-prepare-carried (fn-owner-prepare installs fn-pcar-sbud-prepare) execute them. The logical model over octet lists is unchanged; the payload walk and the group-name grammar still convert (design-2026-09-25-representation.md ranks them next). proofs.title: Bounded parsing and staging
proofs.statement: For the resource profile, parsing and modeled staging terminate within declared length, nesting, allocation, and work bounds.
proofs.progress_note: Article/UTF-8/wildmat output recognizers and DP correspondence are certified. Whole matcher work has a value-corresponding polynomial bound; public transfer missing-range work has a hypothesis-free bound covering malformed validation, structural label equality, lookup and traversal. These declared operation costs exclude numeric bit complexity/runtime allocation. Other parser work, peak allocation and physical capacity remain open. Complete public article parsing now has unconditional exact value correspondence and structural-work input/profile bounds, including malformed inputs and repeated folds. This closes the article parser traversal-cost gap, not peak allocation or runtime costs. The served fold's step count is bounded by the chunk length, so a socket read of n octets cannot drive an unbounded number of NNTP steps. The pessimistic number, with its scope: the closed-form work ceiling of the public article parser is roughly 16,000x the measured traversal cost of that same parser (tests/evidence/2026-09-18-article-work.md); it is an instrumented shadow, not a host measurement. D27 (packet P2, 2026-09-25): the article parser's own preflight is the codec ceiling *fn-article-max-octets* (the record payload ceiling), and every served path hands it at most the injection configuration's max-octets first (fn-inj-decide refuses :oversize before fn-article-parse; the owner sets that bound from the carried Store profile, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-served-post-bound). The header caps stay as work bounds: the certified parse work bound is fuel per header line times input length, 9.0e15 steps at the codec ceiling and 6.9e10 at the 32,768-octet profile bound (tests/acl2/article-work-tests.lisp), so removing them needs a work theorem linear in the header. Evidence: planning/evidence/bounds-p2-2026-09-25.md. Signed-path (2026-09-25, D27): the kind-4 composite's bounds are the codecs' widths (record u32, source u32, composite u32 less the poll reply's 355 octets); the staged composite's size bound is the profile's R, exactly (fn-sbud-signed-event-boundary-refuses-exactly-past-the-record-field).

proofs.title: The statement index is a proved twin (S3-3)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-index-agrees-with-lace: under the carried index invariant the index answers lookup and the equivocator question exactly as the linear fn-stx-lace projection; fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept: acceptance preserves that invariant, so the projection is a proof-level object and never runs per served command (D3).
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `books/stx-index` CERTIFIES (w10/substrate-2). The three agreements `fn-stx-index-bindings-agree`, `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` and `fn-stx-index-equivocators-agree` are the keystones; `fn-stx-index-agrees-with-lace` is their `:rule-classes nil` corollary and is cited as such, and `fn-stx-recorded-equivocation-agrees-with-lace` is a corollary of that. THE SUBJECT GAP IS CLOSED IN BOTH HALVES (w11/sn-index, decision D21). Preservation: `fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept` hypothesises `fn-stx-acceptedp`, which `fn-stx-durable-completion-is-an-acceptance` proves of the durable branch of `fn-node-complete`, and `fn-sn-finish-preserves-indexedp` (books/store-node-invariants) is that keystone applied at `fn-sn-finish`, the only node step of the host's `fn-store-sn-finish`. Query: `fn-sn-state` carries the index and the keyring it was computed under as two new fields; `fn-sn-statement-lookup` and `fn-sn-equivocatorp` read the index and nothing else; `host/store-node-host.lisp` `fn-store-sn-statement` and `fn-store-sn-equivocator` call them on the `'fn-store-sn` global, reachable from outside as `run_store.py statement`; and `fn-sn-statement-lookup-is-the-lace-lookup` and `fn-sn-equivocatorp-is-the-lace-equivocator` equate the called function to the projection. Their hypothesis `fn-sn-indexedp` is discharged by a complete reachability chain over every transition that reaches an `f-put-global` of that global. WHY THIS IS NOT YET `certified`: (a) `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` still has no caller -- no served query walks the slot list; (b) A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification, and the only witnesses are under the toy realiser of `tests/acl2/crypto-seam-tests`; (c) the keyring is supplied per invocation and is not carried in the durable configuration history, so a restart forgets it; and (d) `fn-stx-transit-authority-ok` (books/stx-policy) still walks the whole lace per article on the ADMISSION path and has no caller, so D3 is answered at the query and not at admission. Witnesses: `tests/acl2/store-node-index-tests`, a real run of the store transitions from `fn-sn-initial` to `fn-sn-finish` with a signed `FN-Statement` article, with the same run under the empty keyring as the separating witness and a stale-index tooth. Route: planning/lanes/HANDOFF-w11-sn-index.md. CLOSED 2026-09-23 (T4): `fn-sn-finish-preserves-indexedp` no longer excludes the accepted-statement arm. Local replay lemmas establish that a non-nil composite replay from a valid idle node installs exactly one article, its payload equals the decoded composite payload, and `fn-sn-composite-delta` is that article's statement delta; `fn-sn-completion-enabledp` discharges the replay/idle premises. The host-called finish therefore preserves the carried index through retention, neutral identity, accepted composite identity, and ordinary durable acceptance. A reached composite acceptance with a nonempty statement index and a stale-index must-fail tooth are in tests/acl2/store-node-composite-index-tests. The source-book certificate and the pending test certificate are recorded in planning/evidence/store-composite-index-t4-2026-09-23.md.

On it rest fn-stx-reconnect-never-revises-admissibility, which keeps every fn-me-decide equal across the merge, and fn-stx-reconnect-exposes-the-partition, which makes two commits off a shared base a visible fork rather than a winner.

proofs.title: The reader's verdict is the recorded verdict, three-valued (S6-1)
proofs.statement: A durable kind-4 (hybrid acceptance) completion through fn-sn-finish records that event's verdict under its Message-ID; a reader opened after the owner's (:complete) pins that verdict list; and one fn-own-read of HDR :fn-verified <msgid> on an ungated reader connection, framed at its last octet, answers exactly the pinned verdict for the retrieved article, with no keyring consulted. A served NNTP POST (and a local control post or BP application submission) carrying an FN-Authorship carrier takes the transit classification: when ACL2 builds its kind-4 event under the node's current enrollment and that event is the completion record, the owner's (:complete) records its verdict at the POST's Message-ID and a later reader reports it; a present carrier the plan refuses renders its reason as its own 441 line and is never the unsigned arm. On NNTP transit (IHAVE) the same relayed reason renders `437 transfer rejected; ` with the text of that reason's 441 line. fn-stx-reader-verdict-is-the-recorded-verdict (books/stx-reader) is the definition restated and is not a proof event; it is no longer cited. D23: on NNTP transit the same fn-pa-current-plan takes the delivering boundary's carried-source list; it plans :carried only when this node has no keyring snapshot of the carrier's principal and the list names it, and off that arm it is the D02 plan (fn-pa-current-plan-off-the-carried-arm-is-the-d02-plan); the carried kind-4 event binds the received octets and the carrier and records token :carried at keyring generation 0, which replay records without a snapshot and the reader renders `carried HEX`, never `verified`.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.progress_note: Bounds P4 (2026-09-25): a verdict over a v2 carrier records the evidence tag fn-hybrid-v2, which fn-stxe-keyring-profile maps to the one D09 keyring profile so kind-4 replay and the schema-1 binding accept it (fn-hsig-keyring-profile-of-evidence-tag); verdicts recorded under fn-hybrid-v1 keep their meaning and a v1 record stored by a pre-v2 image reads verified on the P4 image (planning/evidence/bounds-p4-2026-09-25.md). This adds no PRF-026 event. Signed-path (2026-09-25, D27): the kind-4 composite's literal caps (32,768 source, 65,538 record, 196,608 composite) are codec ceilings; a served signed POST's composite is held to the store profile's record field R by fn-sbud-signed-event-boundary, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit asks through fn-owner-signed-event-boundary before the identity commit, and a composite not formed or past R is refused with its own 441 line (:event, :signed-record); an :ok composite satisfies the publish gate's fn-bs-publication-admissiblep at its framed length. Native: a 60 KiB v1 and a 200 KiB v2 signed POST are accepted, HDR verified and fn_verify exit 0; a tampered v2 is refused by name.

proofs.title: The two durable kinds are one sequence-ordered stream (R5)
proofs.statement: fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-config-record and fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-article-record: the merge of the configuration-record file and the transaction journal by the sequence field each record carries holds exactly the records of each file, in order -- the left side walks the merge, the right side walks the input file. fn-cstr-merge-is-sequence-ordered: two sequence-ordered files merge to one sequence-ordered stream, so the two-directory layout loses no ordering information. fn-cstr-ok-merged-replay-ends-in-a-configured-node: a merged replay that reports :ok ends in a fn-cnode-statep state, which carries reserved <= capacity, so every configuration record in the history was admitted at a node that had already replayed the article records before it. Covered scope: finite histories of the two record kinds; no on-disk interleaving is claimed.
proofs.progress_note: books/config-stream certifies (ACL2 8.7, persvati, 2026-09-20). The separating witness in tests/acl2/config-stream-tests is the argument for the decision: one (:set-capacity 1) over a history whose two articles reserve 2, which the configuration-only replay the host runs today accepts and the merged replay refuses with :config-refusal; a raise and a decrease to exactly the reservation total are both admitted, so the merged replay is not refusing every decrease. Open: the host still replays configuration first (specs/reconfiguration.md section 8). No event yet; T2.

proofs.title: Live reconfiguration: what a configuration generation serves, and what a crash recovers (R5, T8)
proofs.statement: fn-ocl-no-reader-observes-a-half-change, over what the host calls (staging through fn-ocfg-step at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas, publication through fn-ocl-publish at fn-owner-reconfigure-complete) and with no hypothesis: every open connection's record, every configuration pin and every served table are unchanged across staging and publication; staging leaves the live configuration where it was; a non-durable verdict changes nothing; a :durable verdict completes exactly the record whose generation the durable write named, appends that whole record to the store's configuration history, publishes what that history replays to, clears the stage and installs the matching posting configuration. The owner itself is not unchanged on the called path (store and posting configuration move). fn-ocl-publish-installs-the-whole-staged-record: under fn-ocl-config-historyp the published configuration is fn-cfg-apply-record of the live configuration and the whole staged record, by fn-ocl-cpr-loop-configuration-is-the-record-fold. fn-ocl-publish-agrees-with-ocfg-complete-on-readers equates the called path with the model event (:complete) on pins, served tables, connection records and the stage. fn-ocl-request-refused-over-a-reader-in-the-group: a group request (fn-ocl-request-deltas, the delta the host no longer builds) for a group some open connection's reader has selected is refused at staging. The model statement follows. fn-ocfg-no-reader-observes-a-half-change: the two owner events a live reconfiguration consists of, (:reconfigure other deltas) then (:complete), leave the owner -- every open connection's record, session and pinned archive, hence every reply -- and every configuration pin exactly as they were; staging leaves the live configuration where it was; and publication moves it to fn-ocfg-published-config of the staged record, the old configuration or fn-cfg-apply-record of the whole record and nothing between; one hypothesis, that a record was staged, the condition under which the host calls (:complete). fn-ocfg-pin-is-stable-without-advance: over any finite fn-ocfg-step event list holding no (:advance id), (:close id) or (:fault id), a pinned connection keeps the configuration it opened at. fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation, over what the host calls (staging (:reconfigure id deltas) and (:close id) through fn-ocfg-step, the durable write, publication through fn-ocl-publish; recovery through fn-cpr-replay of the configuration journal and the Store journal at host/owner-host.lisp:173 in fn-owner-recover), with one hypothesis, fn-ocl-config-historyp (the live configuration is what fn-cpr-replay of the store's own journals recovers): before the durable write the store and both journals are unchanged and replay :ok to the live configuration, which staging did not move; after the write and before publication, a replay of the configuration journal with the staged record appended is either not :ok (the host answers :fault and installs nothing) or recovers exactly the configuration the model's (:complete) publishes, fn-cfg-apply-record of the live configuration and the whole record, at the record's generation; on a :durable publication the installed store's journals are exactly those, their replay is :ok to the published configuration, nothing is staged and the hypothesis holds again, so the statement chains across every later reconfiguration; A-DURABILITY enters as the publisher's :durable meaning the record is in the directory the next open reads. fn-ocl-cpr-replay-ok-is-config-replay-ok relates the called replay to the configuration-only one as a refinement: an :ok of fn-cpr-replay on (configs, events) is an :ok of fn-cnode-config-replay on configs with the same configuration; the converse is false (a configuration journal whose transaction ids descend is accepted by fn-cnode-config-replay and refused :config-txid by fn-cpr-replay; tests/acl2/config-crash-replay-tests), and the called path does not write such a journal (fn-cpo-configure-durable appends only at the Store frontier and only when fn-cpr-replay of the result is :ok). The model statements fn-ocfg-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation and fn-ocfg-config-replay-of-one-more-record (books/owner-config.lisp, over fn-cnode-config-replay, which no host line calls, and fn-ocfg-step (:complete)) stay as model-level lemmas and are not registry events. fn-ocfg-open-pins-the-live-configuration and fn-ocfg-advance-observes-the-live-configuration: under fn-ocfg-statep a new or advanced connection pins the live configuration. fn-native-admin-live-group-delta-is-a-typed-delta: an accepted group create or retire stages one delta that fn-cfg-deltap admits. Covered scope: the owner's configuration and pins; NOT covered: the live node's allocation domain and capacity, which no owner transition moves, so a group created live is published and in the injection configuration but GROUP and LIST ACTIVE answer from the acceptance state's group list and do not show it until a restart (books/owner-config.lisp OPEN item 3); LIST ACTIVE on the wire answers from that list, not from the pin (OPEN item 1).
proofs.progress_note: T8 (2026-09-22): two defects found and fixed in the live arm. (1) fn-ocfg-complete published through fn-cnode-apply-config on the live node, whose domain and capacity no live transition moves, so after one live group create or capacity change every later completion kept the old configuration while the record was already durable (ground witness in tests/acl2/owner-config-tests: the second of two live reconfigurations violated fn-cnode-apply-config's guard); completion now publishes fn-ocfg-published-config, the configuration step recovery replays. (2) host/native-admin-host.lisp passed argv octets as configuration labels, so live group create, group retire and peer remove were refused :malformed-delta; the delta list is now fn-native-admin-plan-deltas. Teeth for every hypothesis in tests/acl2/owner-config-tests and tests/acl2/native-admin-tests. fn-ocfg-list-active-lists-the-pinned-served-table stays proved and is not cited: fn-ocfg-list-active has no host caller. V0-CFG-LIVE on an image is not claimed: its GROUP check needs the domain seam. T8c (2026-09-22): the dabebb84 matrix run showed the live arm faulting the owner on every request, because host/native/admin.lisp read fn-owner-open's integer id through fnn-owner-action (fixed; reproduced and fixed on hbox, planning/evidence/t8c-live-rows-2026-09-22.md), and the control reply losing the owner's fault word to its own stop hook, so the caller saw uncertain (fixed in host/native/control.lisp). fn-native-admin-publication-is-authorized-only-under-the-lock: an accepted publication result, and any result carrying a publication state, implies the lock observation the host passes, which is now the store's own (fnn-admin-lock-observation) and no longer a literal T; teeth in tests/acl2/native-admin-tests. proofs.title: The outbound feed offers exactly the peers in scope, and never a loop (K2, outbound half)
proofs.statement: fn-own-feed-target-is-offerable with fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer: for a feed table the owner carries, the peers one durably accepted article is offered to are exactly the peers of that table whose own configured record has an outbound half, whose outbound wildmat matches one of the article's own Newsgroups names, whose path-identity the article's Path does not already name, and which is not the peer the article arrived from. fn-own-feed-never-offers-a-loop is the loop-freedom half (RFC 5537 section 3.6) and fn-own-feed-target-is-in-scope the scope half; fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin transport both to the table the owner holds, and fn-own-feed-tick-peer-is-the-feed-tick is the subject rule tying one peer's tick to fn-feed-tick-step on that peer's own feed. Covered scope: one article's octets against one table; the hypothesis is the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep. NOT covered: the statement over fn-own-step and fn-feedp preservation, which is cited from books/peer-feed-invariants and not restated. Over the functions the host calls (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-own-submission-targets-are-feed-targets bounds fn-own-submission-targets -- what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent reaches through fn-own-submission-intent-records, and what fn-own-feed-durable enqueues and fn-own-feed-durable-records journals -- by fn-own-feed-targets (a bound, not an equation: a peer already holding the Message-ID is filtered out); fn-own-submission-never-targets-a-loop is the loop statement over it under the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep; fn-own-transit-outcome-never-enqueues-on-the-origin says the owner fn-owner-transit-outcome installs keeps the origin peer's feed unchanged, whatever the decision and the store word. fn-own-feed-accept has no caller in books/ or host/, so fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin are -sibling theorems and count for nothing on their own; the host-called replacements are fn-own-feed-durable-touches-only-the-submission-targets and fn-own-feed-durable-never-enqueues-on-the-origin. fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer's recognizer and bound-entry hypotheses are redundant (tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests proves the conclusion from the scope decision alone), so it has one tooth, not three.
proofs.progress_note: books/owner-feed and tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests are CERTIFIED as of 2026-09-20, lane w6/peering-feed-4 (laptop ACL2 8.7, evidence build/lanes/w6-peering-feed-4/build/acl2/certify-20260920T212559Z-13370; the persvati closure run-20260920T211802Z-ba78 reached them for the first time). What unblocked them was books/peer-feed-invariants, which now certifies with no open form. books/owner certifies too. The owner-side statement over fn-own-step is still open, and the reason has moved: books/owner-invariants is open at the :open-peer arm of fn-own-step-preserves-relation, not at the feed. The earlier non-admission explanation above is historical; later frozen owner books certified. W22 integrates the actual host tick/reply/loss/restart projections through owner-feed-port, including an all-or-nothing logical restart fold. Its owned closure and combined source gate are tracked separately; no new theorem over fn-own-step or native outbound socket/timer behavior is claimed from this adoption. Native feed component now carries a connection-table invariant from recovery through put/remove, validates only selected bounded input, and distinguishes handshake rejection from delivery refusal. Owned certification and raw boundary tests are separate from activation/real two-native-node evidence. The shell host-wrapper witness is withheld pending repair of its unconditional success marker.

proofs.title: Provenance is typed, and its wire form is lossless and legacy-compatible
proofs.statement: Every string is an admissible provenance (the :legacy kind), so widening the retention evidence slot from stringp to fn-provp changes no stored value; the rendered form of each typed kind is exactly the string that kind's writer produced before the widening; and a provenance the codec can write is the provenance it reads back from its wire form.
proofs.note: The transit path's DURABLE provenance is not covered: fn-peer-injection-arguments still passes fn-peer-evidence's rendering, and fn-peer-evidence-is-the-legacy-rendering is the equation between the typed record and that string, not evidence that the record reaches the store. books/peer-inbound and books/peer-inbound-invariants have no certificate on dev (blocked on fn-peer-echo-reply-effects-well-formed), so those two events are admitted, not certified, and are not listed here.

proofs.title: AUTHINFO on the served path, and what posting follows (W10)
proofs.statement: fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed: with authentication required and no authenticated subject, a restricted command's step submits nothing, never offers article mode, leaves the session unchanged and its whole effect list is the single 480 line (RFC 4643 section 2.2). Its seven hypotheses each have a violating value in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp; the two syntactic ones it used to carry were removed on 2026-09-22 because no value violates them while the restricted-keyword hypothesis holds (fn-auth-restricted-keyword-is-a-keyword-token). fn-auth-post-without-permission-is-not-offered and its lift fn-auth-step-post-without-permission-is-not-offered: a connection whose posting allowance is false is answered by this book and never offered 340, so no body can follow and no submission can leave; fn-auth-postingp is the authenticated principal's credential flag, so a principal enrolled without it is refused 440 however permissive the pinned injection configuration is (RFC 3977 6.3.1.1). fn-served-dispatch-of-a-refused-post-leaves-the-wire-in-place carries that to the served dispatcher: the wire is not switched into article mode and the read carries no submission. fn-auth-pass-before-user-is-482 and fn-auth-failed-pass-leaves-the-session-unauthenticated are two of the three RFC 4643 section 2.3.2 codes, each with the session unchanged or cleared. The third is stated over the called function: fn-auth-step-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls says that while the operator's policy is protected-only and the connection carries no TLS layer, an AUTHINFO command line -- USER or PASS, any arguments, configured name or not -- is answered 483 and nothing else happens: the session is the one the command arrived on, so no name is cached and no subject is installed, no submission leaves, and the secret is never compared because the branch that would compare it is not reached. Its eight hypotheses each have a violating value in the teeth book. The label half of the same channel: fn-auth-starttls-is-not-advertised-under-tls-on-any-connection, fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated-on-any-connection and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-before-tls-under-protected-only are over fn-auth-capability-lines-for-peer, which is the list fn-auth-command puts in the 101 block for EVERY connection and not only a reader's, and fn-auth-step-capability-block-unfolds-to-the-peer-aware-lines is the named unfold equating that list to what fn-auth-step emits; fn-auth-starttls-is-not-advertised-without-a-certificate is the reader-facing instance of the first. Those three say what a client is OFFERED; they do not state anything about the octets fn-nntp-multi renders the list into. fn-auth-pass-accepts-only-a-checking-secret says the accepting branch ran fn-authsec-checkp against the stored verifier; it does NOT say a wrong secret fails, which is A-CRYPTO. Covered scope: one served connection over a pinned archive and a pinned AUTHINFO configuration. The subject of the lifts above is fn-auth-step, a sibling the host does not call: books/served.lisp:617 fn-served-dispatch calls fn-auth-step-pinned, which host/owner-host.lisp:1240 fn-owner-chunk reaches through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix. P1 is stated over that called function and over fn-served-dispatch, each 480 and 483 statement proved from the fn-auth-step keystone and the bridge fn-auth-step-pinned-agrees-with-auth-step-on-handled-command: fn-auth-step-pinned-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed (seven hypotheses, the 480 keystone's) and fn-served-dispatch-of-a-gated-command-is-480-and-changes-nothing, which says that on a served connection whose policy requires authentication and which has no subject, a restricted command within the command and argument bounds leaves the whole connection (wire framing, session, pinned archive and indexes) equal to the one it arrived on and its only effect is the 480 line; fn-auth-step-pinned-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls (eight hypotheses) and fn-served-dispatch-of-authinfo-on-a-clear-connection-is-483-and-changes-nothing, the same for AUTHINFO on a clear connection under protected-only, whose only effect is the 483 line, so no name is cached and the secret is never compared; fn-auth-step-pinned-post-by-a-principal-without-the-flag-is-440, an authenticated principal whose credential lacks the posting flag is answered 440 to POST with the session unchanged and no submission; and fn-auth-step-pinned-post-by-a-principal-with-the-flag-is-delegated, one whose credential carries the flag and whose principal is the subject has its POST handed unchanged to fn-auth-delegate-pinned, where the pinned injection configuration still decides. Each has its hypotheses dropped one at a time under must-fail with an evaluated counterexample in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp (keystones 11 to 17). Covered scope: one dispatched command event; the chain from fn-served-dispatch to the host read is fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix and fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read. OB-AUTH-FOLD is fn-auth-fold-step-has-no-local-submission: if the served connection is valid, its pinned credential policy grants posting to no principal, and no local POST body is pending, every effect of the complete fn-served-step read excludes fn-inj-injectedp; fn-auth-fold-step-preserves-safe-connp carries those conditions between reads. Separately authorized fn-peer-submissionp transit remains possible, as the reachable AUTHINFO plus TAKETHIS witness shows. The invoked subject is fn-served-step, reached by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read; fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix is its named correspondence.
proofs.progress_note: Historical W10 local admission and cache-origin limitations are superseded for the frozen03 closure and source-pinned native-auth continuation by their archived certification/build evidence. The native AUTHINFO startup receiver passes scoped live wrong-password/correct-password and reader-versus-peer cases. These results do not establish independent-client interoperability, native protected transport, or complete physical adapter correspondence. Native principal administration has scoped ACL2 and actual replacement/recovery evidence; public CLI composition remains open. The existing salted SHA-256 verifier is preserved without a password-hardening or secrecy theorem claim. Lane t7/auth-teeth, 2026-09-22: the events above are curated for the first time and tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp is the teeth book, with a reachable non-degenerate witness for each keystone and one must-fail per hypothesis for the 480 gate (seven) and the 483 refusal (eight), plus separating witnesses for the three capability labels. OB-AUTH-FOLD now proves the local-submission exclusion through the served byte fold in books/nntp-auth-fold.lisp, with a reachable transit counterexample to the prior no-any-submission claim. Two of K1's four hypotheses (fn-served-connp and the not-handshaking one) are proof-support and have no must-fail, because K1 restated without them reaches an open case, a session that is fn-auth-sessionp but not consistent with its connection's archive. The 483-before-TLS and 281-after-STARTTLS behaviour on a deployed image is tools/node_probe.py's row and has not been run on one. K2 follow-up teeth isolate the no-pending-POST premise with a forged but fn-served-connp no-posters state after an actual 340 offer; it submits locally and is unreachable from a no-posters open under the preservation theorem. fn-served-connp is a structural carried connection invariant, not a separate permission test or a runtime whole-store scan.

proofs.title: The recovery window's crash images are kernel-admissible and risk no acknowledged record
proofs.statement: In the recovery window -- the phases between a process replaying what it scanned from the view and completing its five recovery fences -- a crash may drop the record the replay read, because that record's directory entry is the entry operation a dead process left pending; and it may roll the frontier back, because the pending entry operation may be the allocator rename instead. fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits exactly those two images and no other, each gated by an empty success history, the frontier arm additionally by a record list that leaves the reserved txid unused, and the two exclusive of one another; every image it admits is produced by fn-sf-image-crash with the same frontier, records, :replaying phase and success history; and an acknowledged pair of the pre-crash state names a record of EVERY image it admits, both rolled-back ones included.
proofs.note: Decisions D14-b (lane w10/kernel-freedom, the record arm) and D14-c (lane w11/bytestore-k2, the frontier arm K2f). The recognizer is a SECOND one: fn-sf-crash-imagep is unchanged and stays the reliance predicate that fn-own-reopen gates on and every reopen theorem takes as a premise, because widening it is false for the composition -- an owner reopened on an image is a recovery-window state whose own success history is empty while its ledger names records earlier processes acknowledged, and which of a state's records are fenced is a fact about the byte store's pending list, not about the kernel state. The counterexample is mechanized in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the owner half) and tests/acl2/store-observed-traces-tests.lisp (the kernel half). This target retires the open row K2r of specs/crash-model-v2.md; crash-model-v2 K2, whose conclusion this predicate is, remains open on the byte side, and what it waits on is now only K1's three remaining scan clauses: the frontier sub-case K2f is modelled, so K2's STATEMENT is true of every image the platform can leave in the window.

proofs.title: A clock the host contradicts is dropped, and the refusal is not an article verdict
proofs.statement: fn-own-observe answers exactly one of :observed, :refused and :invalid, and the host reports that word rather than inferring one from a state comparison. On a related owner a :refused reading names a host contradiction -- the monotonic counter went backwards, has-wall changed, or a widened error bound moved the earliest admissible true time back -- and never merely a reading that did not move, because a reading equal to the one held is admitted. A refusal leaves the owner with no clock, and with no usable injection reading fn-nntp-post-step emits no submission and answers `441 posting failed; this server has no usable clock reading', which is a different constant from every article verdict the step can give.
proofs.note: Decision D10-a, lane w11/clock-seam. Keystones fn-own-observe-refusal-names-a-contradiction (books/owner-invariants.lisp) and fn-post-without-a-clock-refuses-with-the-clock-line (books/nntp-post.lisp), with fn-own-observe-outcome-is-one-of-three and fn-own-observe-outcome-decides-the-clock-by-definition named for what they are and cited by :use. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the served-path second post on one connection, the same-reading collision, the clock 441 with an empty queue, DATE 503, and one-event recovery) and tests/acl2/nntp-post-tests.lisp (one must-fail per hypothesis). OPEN under this target: two submissions inside one millisecond still share a generated Message-ID, because fn-clock-later-observationp is non-strict; separating them needs the owner to remember the reading it last minted under and is not done here.

proofs.title: A reopened journal answers for a work what the pre-crash machine would have, and says which works it recovered
proofs.statement: fn-bp-work-status-of-restart: under fn-bp-statep, the :restart transition a reopen runs changes the boundary answer for one work id by fn-bp-work-status-after-restart and by nothing else -- an attempt that was in flight is marked :restart-observed, while :absent, :outstanding, :receipted, a retryable status and :delivered are fixed points. fn-bp-replay-work-status-is-the-pre-crash-status-restarted lifts that to fn-bp-replay-journal, the predecessor interpreter for the original FNWF kinds: when the replay succeeds, fn-bp-work-status of the installed image is fn-bp-work-status-after-restart of fn-bp-work-status of the trace of the initial state over fn-bp-durable-events, the journal's denotation without that trailing restart. Provenance is separate and also ACL2's: fn-bp-work-origin-at-open-is-recovered-or-absent says that against the id list fn-bp-work-ids records at open, every work the image holds reads :recovered and every other id reads :absent; fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued says this session's durable enqueue of an id that list does not name reads :enqueued. So a work recovered from a cut and a work enqueued after the reopen, which share the status :outstanding, are distinct at the boundary. fn-bprl-replay-work-status-is-durable-status-restarted covers fn-bprl-replay-journal over the release-aware FNWF language: if replay succeeds, the installed work status is the one-restart status of the exact ACL2 release-aware interpreter folded over its durable records. fn-bpiw-reopen-after-live-recovery-is-the-live-image-restarted covers the recovery outcome in the ION-overlay journal the host now opens: if fn-bpiw-replay-journal opens a journal and fn-bpiw-apply accepts a :recovery outcome on the opened image, then fn-bpiw-replay-journal accepts the journal with that outcome appended (so the history gate admits what the live gate admits), and its installed BP image is fn-bp-restart of the live image and its ION state is the live one.
proofs.note: Lane w11/workflow-replay, book books/bp-workflow-replay-status.lisp, teeth in tests/acl2/bp-workflow-records-tests.lisp. The subject of the first two keystones is what host/workflow-host.lisp:63 (fn-workflow-work-status) calls; of the last two, what host/workflow-host.lisp:73 (fn-workflow-work-origin) calls on the list host/workflow-host.lisp:8 records. Certified on hbox, run-20260921T005523Z-05dc, build/acl2/certify-20260921T005528Z-1361353. Before the ION extension, the native workflow host called fn-bprl-replay-journal, which also interprets :undertake and :release; fn-bprl-replay-work-status-is-durable-status-restarted certifies that successful predecessor path, with an extended reachable journal and a malformed-suffix must-fail tooth in tests/acl2/bp-release-tests.lisp (persvati manifests certify-20260923T173933Z-2312844.json and certify-20260923T174038Z-2322911.json). The earlier fn-bp replay theorem remains scoped to its original record language. The :enqueue kind hypothesis of fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued has a constructed rather than a reached tooth, and the test book says so: fn-bp-prepare-attempt only prepares an attempt for a work the image holds, so the composed machine reaches no :attempt pending over an image that holds none. Current scope correction (2026-09-24): host/workflow-host.lisp fn-workflow-install-replay now calls fn-bpiw-replay-journal, whose mixed FNWF stream includes :ion-route and :ion-observed. The two certified single-record structural projections in books/bp-ion-workflow.lisp do not yet lift the work-status theorem through that complete replay. A named actual-caller correspondence with a reachable mixed-history witness remains open; predecessor certificates do not discharge it. Hence the target is in-progress, while its existing component theorems remain intact. Replay fence (lane ion-replay-fence, 2026-09-24): fn-bpiw-replay-records now reconstructs the unrecorded reopen fence before a :recovery outcome (fn-bpiw-replay-fence, books/bp-ion-workflow.lisp), as fn-bp-replay-records does; before it, a journal holding a recovery outcome could not be reopened and the history preflight refused every recovery outcome (planning/evidence/m4-app-receipt-2026-09-24.md finding 4). The keystone's subject is fn-bpiw-replay-journal, called by host/workflow-host.lisp:13 (fn-workflow-install-replay) and :107 (fn-workflow-preflight-history), against fn-bpiw-apply as host/workflow-host.lisp:112 (fn-workflow-apply-record) calls it; book books/bp-ion-workflow-replay.lisp, teeth in tests/acl2/bp-ion-workflow-replay-tests.lisp (reachable enqueue, attempt and ION-carrying cuts; must-fail without the recovery-outcome and live-acceptance hypotheses; the open-success hypothesis has no separating witness because a failed open's image holds no fence, and the test book shows that refusal). Scope: one recovery outcome applied right after an open; the general live-suffix correspondence across later records is not claimed, and a live re-attempt of a :restart-observed attempt without a journaled retry request is refused by the history (the must-fail witness), which is the host's intended gate. Evidence: planning/evidence/ion-replay-fence-2026-09-24.md.

proofs.title: The frame integrity trailer has one owner, and the host's framing is the model's
proofs.statement: fn-frame-trailer (books/frame-trailer.lisp) is the only definition of the 32-octet frame integrity trailer in the tree: it is fn-frame-digest, realised through books/crypto-attach.lisp by fn-sha256-stobj (books/sha256-stobj.lisp, the word-stobj computation), which fn-sha256-stobj-is-sha256 equates to the list model fn-sha256 on every object, and it answers :bad rather than a digest for an argument that is not an octet list. For any magic, version, kind and payload in fn-frame-inputp, the byte string a host builds by asking ACL2 for the protected prefix, asking ACL2 for the trailer over it and concatenating the two is fn-frame-seal of those fields; and handing that byte string back to fn-frame-decode with the trailer re-derived over the frame's own fn-frame-protected-prefix answers fn-frame-ok of the fields that went in. The same two statements hold for the store instance the bridge executes, over fn-frame-store-protected and fn-frame-store-decode. Collision and preimage resistance are A-CRYPTO and are not claimed: the attachment introduces no axiom and the seam's constraints are shape only.
proofs.note: Lane w11/one-owner. Keystones fn-frame-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal, fn-frame-decode-of-host-framing and their store instances fn-frame-store-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal and fn-frame-store-decode-of-host-framing, all in books/frame-trailer.lisp. Subject-to-host: the host lines that call fn-frame-trailer are tools/frame_bridge.py FrameSession.trailer (called by seal and digest_of), host/native/io.lisp fnn-trailer (called by fnn-seal and fnn-digest-of) and tools/run_owner.py Acl2Owner.trailer (called by feed_frames and feed_replay_frame); each replaced a separate SHA-256 in that host. Teeth in tests/acl2/frame-trailer-tests.lisp: 25 assert-events, including two FIPS 180-4 vectors, the exact store prefix and trailer octets, the :bad boundary arm, and one violating value per clause (a magic whose third octet is 300 for the shape clause keystone 1 needs, a max-payload of 2 for the bound clause keystone 2 needs, and a non-octet record for the store instance). Byte identity with the deleted host copies was cross-checked outside ACL2 against CPython hashlib.sha256 at 32, 4096, 32768, 262144 and 1048576 octets. NOT closed by this target: fn-frame-digest's collision resistance, and the marshalling cost of sealing a 4 MiB staged inbound bundle through the decimal-octet bridge. Lane rep-sha256 (D27 boundary 3, 2026-09-25): the executable digest is fn-sha256-stobj, SHA-256 over a word stobj (books/sha256-stobj.lisp), attached in crypto-attach under fn-sha256-stobj-is-sha256; fn-sha256-stobj-is-sha256-of-octets is its instance on octet lists and fn-sha256-of-string-is-sha256-of-octets covers the string entry the host sha256 verb calls (host/native/io.lisp, the verb; the host SHA-256 twin fnn-sha256 is deleted). Teeth in tests/acl2/sha256-stobj-tests.lisp: the FIPS vectors through both entries, the padding boundaries against the list model, a must-fail and a separating witness for the string theorem's stringp; the keystone has no hypothesis. No statement of an existing theorem moved.
proofs.progress_note: Both books certified with tools/certify_books.py on the laptop (ACL2 8.7, SBCL 2.6.8), evidence dirs above. The four keystones and the 25 assert-events all pass. What the target does NOT establish: collision or preimage resistance of SHA-256 (A-CRYPTO, unchanged by the attachment); and the old tools/run_feed.py driver has since been deleted. W12 feed-durability owns the remaining FNFD envelope/recovery decisions in tools/feed_wire.py and their host adoption; that extension is separate from these trailer theorems.

proofs.title: Prefix and lower-frontier recoverability of a replayed history
proofs.statement: A history that replays successfully leaves an IDLE node whose next txid only moves forward, so dropping its last record leaves a history recoverable at the same frontier, and a history whose txids are all below a bound is recoverable AT that bound. Those are the two facts fn-sf-history-recoverablep needs beyond a successful replay -- together they are fn-replay-advance-okp -- and on them every image the platform may leave in the recovery window is replayable at its own frontier and the host's reopen entry succeeds on it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bytestore-k2, packet 2. fn-sn-replay-loop-append already gave ok(whole) implies ok(prefix); what was missing, and what blocked lane w10/kernel-freedom's first widening at fn-snt-admissible-crash-image-is-recoverable, is that the prefix node is idle with next-txid at most the frontier. The acknowledged-record half of crash-model-v2 K4 is NOT restated over the wider predicate: on both rollback arms the arm's own (null (fn-sf-successes s)) and a member-equal success hypothesis are contradictory, so the restatement would be fn-sn-acknowledged-record-survives-observed-reopen with two vacuous arms. fn-sf-recovery-admissible-image-facts carries that guarantee over every arm instead. Claimed as PRF-033 before merging dev at 81ae082 and RENUMBERED: w11/clock-seam and w11/workflow-replay had taken 033 and 034, and w11/one-owner 035, while this lane held an older dev.
