proofs.title: Checkpoint validation refuses a non-journal prefix
proofs.statement: Checkpoint validation binds a checkpoint to exactly one prefix and refuses a prefix that is not an ordered journal interval below the checkpoint frontier: fn-cpc-validp implies the checkpoint is fn-checkpoint-capture-value of that prefix at its frontier, and a prefix with any record whose recorded generation is not its transaction id is refused for every checkpoint and configuration offered with it.
proofs.progress_note: Certified over an older digest; `checkpoint-codec` are red at their current digest per `green_check` (2026-09-22); T0 re-establishes them. fn-cpc-validp accepted a prefix that fn-checkpoint-capture refuses as :history until 2026-09-21, because fn-replay carries a record generation into the node transitions without comparing it with the txid and validation compared only replay results. The journal-interval clause is now in the recognizer. Open, and not claimed here: fn-cpc-validp has no host caller, so these are properties of a sibling API to the served restore path (host/checkpoint-host.lisp calls fn-checkpoint-restore, which tests the condition itself). `fn-cpc-validp` has no caller; the served restore path is `host/checkpoint-host.lisp` to `fn-checkpoint-restore`; v1 checkpoint adoption.

proofs.title: The BPv7 bundle codec inverts, and what fn authors another implementation accepts
proofs.statement: For every bundle satisfying fn-bpb-bundlep whose encoding is within the caller's transfer bound, fn-bpb-decode of fn-bpb-encode is that same bundle and nothing else (fn-bpb-decode-of-encode), resting on the one-block round trip fn-bpb-decode-block-of-encode-block, the fold over the block sequence fn-bpb-decode-blocks-of-encode-blocks and the primary block's half fn-bpb-scan-primary-of-encode; every accepted input yields a bundle (fn-bpb-decode-yields-bundle) and an input over the bound is refused before any octet is examined (fn-bpb-decode-refuses-overlong-input). Over those, the node's two ends: what fn-bpn-send puts on the wire is a bundle (fn-bpn-send-bundle-is-a-bundle), and a peer that accepts what fn-bpn-send authored recovers exactly the ADU that was sent (fn-bpn-receive-of-send-carries-the-adu), under the receiver's own configuration and transfer limit. The covered scope is a whole bundle with at most *fn-bpb-max-blocks* canonical blocks plus the payload block; fragments, BPSec and status reports are outside it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bp-node, 2026-09-21; the codec keystones are lane w10/dtn-3's. All seven named theorems are in books/bp-bundle-invariants.lisp and books/bp-node.lisp, both certified (hbox run-20260921T005707Z-8672 and run-20260921T021131Z-1eb0). Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-bundle-tests.lisp and tests/acl2/bp-node-tests.lisp, including the 32-block boundary and the refusal one past it, the three distinct outcomes, and a node configured for a 16-octet transfer refusing a bundle a larger node accepts. The EXTERNAL check is *bpb-dtn7-0-21-0*: 132 octets dtn7-rs 0.21.0 authored, which fn decodes and re-encodes byte for byte (planning/evidence/bp-dtn7-w11-2026-09-21.md). OPEN under this target, and recorded rather than weakened: fn-bpb-decode-blocks-are-canonical-by-construction and fn-bpb-accepted-input-is-canonical-by-construction were REMOVED by w10/dtn-3 after a rewriter runaway with three cures measured and none stopping it, so 'every accepted input re-encodes to itself' is NOT proved for a whole bundle -- it holds of dtn7-rs's captured vector by evaluation only. The native outbound lifecycle now calls fn-bpn-step in books/bp-node-machine.lisp, with source-pinned runtime evidence. This codec target does not cover its persistence, restart or obligation-preservation contracts; PRF-045/046 track those still-open obligations.

proofs.title: Every connection the owner opens carries the operator's AUTHINFO policy, and its greeting says what that policy allows
proofs.statement: fn-served-peer-and-reader-open-under-the-same-policy: the AUTHINFO configuration pinned into a connection the owner resolved to a peer record (fn-served-open-peer) is the same value pinned into a reader connection opened under that policy (fn-served-open), so no decision in books/nntp-auth.lisp -- the credential fn-auth-authinfo searches, the AUTHINFO and STARTTLS labels fn-auth-capability-lines emits, the 480 gate fn-auth-gatedp applies and the posting allowance fn-auth-postingp computes -- can answer one way for a client the owner resolved as a peer and another way for the client beside it. fn-served-open-peer-pins-the-configuration is the field-level half: the pinned value is the argument, coerced by fn-auth-open-session to fn-auth-open-config only when it is not a configuration. fn-auth-step-preserves-the-config is what makes those two statements about the CONNECTION and not only about its open: for any session and any wire event, with no hypothesis at all, the step's session carries the same fn-auth-session-config -- not a login, not the handshake, not a delegated reader command and not a command books/nntp-auth.lisp does not answer writes that field. Every decision in that book reads it, so the policy a client meets on its hundredth command is the one pinned before the connection opened. Covered scope: the OPEN transition for the first two, and one step for the third; the fold over a whole read is OB-AUTH-FOLD's. The subject is what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open-peer calls through fn-own-open-peer, which tools/run_owner.py Owner.accept_nntp calls for every accepted socket whose source address matches a peer record. Second half, the same value read where a client first sees it: fn-served-open-greets-200-exactly-when-the-connection-may-post says the greeting the open emits is RFC 3977 section 5.1.2's 200 exactly when the pinned injection configuration allows posting AND fn-auth-postingp of the session just built is true -- which is the conjunction fn-auth-command hands fn-nntp-capability-lines for the POST label and the one fn-auth-postingp decides 340 against 440 and 480 by. fn-served-open-greeting-agrees-with-the-post-label states that over the octets a client sees, and is named for what it is: a corollary of the keystone and a local unfold of fn-auth-capability-lines, doing no work of its own. Covered scope: the OPEN transition. It says nothing about the greeting a connection would deserve LATER, after a 281 changes the allowance; RFC 4643 section 2.2 sends the client back to CAPABILITIES for that, and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated is the only statement fn has about the block after a login. After the open: fn-auth-step-pinned-login-installs-the-credential-posting-flag says that for any wire event, a step of the host-called fn-auth-step-pinned that takes a session with no subject to one with a subject leaves a posting allowance (fn-auth-postingp) equal to the posting flag of the credential enrolled under the session's cached name; covered scope: one step.
proofs.note: Lane w11/auth-live, decided by measurement and not by inspection. fn-served-open-peer pinned the literal (fn-auth-open-config) while fn-served-open pinned the operator's, and the owner resolves a connection to a peer by SOURCE ADDRESS alone, so on a box where a configured peer is reachable on loopback every client was opened without the operator's policy: AUTHINFO PASS answered 481 with the secret just written, CAPABILITIES carried no AUTHINFO line and POST was never gated. Both theorems are FALSE of that definition. The live before/after is planning/evidence/auth-live-2026-09-21.md and the boundary test is tests/test_auth.py ServedCredentialTests, which starts the node with `bin/fn run` over an fn.toml and writes the peer record, because no test that starts tools/run_owner.py directly can reach this. The greeting half is a second defect the same measurement found: fn-served-greeting read the injection configuration alone, so a connection under [auth] required = true greeted 200 and then answered POST 480, where section 5.1.2's MUST is 201. It takes the opened session now. Lane t7/auth-teeth, 2026-09-22: teeth in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp. Neither greeting theorem nor either pinning theorem has a hypothesis, so the teeth are the values that separate the two sides together with a must-fail on the statement the definition satisfied BEFORE the 2026-09-21 measurement: that the greeting is 200 exactly when the injection configuration allows posting, and that the peer open pins (fn-auth-open-config). fn-served-open-greeting-agrees-with-the-post-label stays uncited: the statement above names it a corollary and a local unfold, so its evidence is the witnesses on both sides of its iff, not a registry event. fn-auth-step-preserves-the-config is new in this lane and was asked for by name in the header of books/nntp-auth-invariants.lisp as the first of the three facts OB-AUTH-FOLD waits on.
proofs.native_scope: The native startup receiver installs the ACL2-produced bounded credential profile before bind, with policy projection and live login evidence. Native configured-peer/source admission and protected transport remain separate; this does not extend the OPEN theorem to every subsequent connection transition.

proofs.title: A host fault costs one connection, and the fourth outcome says so
proofs.statement: fn-own-fault (books/owner-fault.lisp) is the owner's host-fault transition. For any owner and any connection id: the faulted connection is no longer found; every connection with a different id is EQUAL to what it was, so every later step over it has the same input it would have had; a submission in flight for the faulted id, and a pending transaction held by it, are cleared, with no hypothesis that the connection was still open, while a submission in flight for a DIFFERENT id is untouched; the store, the committed view and the completion ledger are unchanged; and the octets the faulted connection receives are RFC 3977 section 3.2.1's 403 and are not the reply octets of fn-nntp-post-outcome for any session and any completion, including that function's own malformed-session 403 -- so the fault is a fourth outcome, distinguishable on the wire from accepted, refused and uncertain.
proofs.note: Lane w11/owner-survival. CLAIMED as PRF-035 and renumbered to PRF-040 on merging dev: 035 had already gone to w11/one-owner's frame trailer, 036 to w11/bytestore-k2, 037 to w11/checkpoint-validator, 038 to w11/bp-node and 039 to w11/auth-live, all inside one evening. Keystones fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection, fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and fn-own-fault-reply-is-not-a-post-outcome (books/owner-fault.lisp), with fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission, fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction and fn-own-fault-is-not-a-store-event beside them. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp on the same witness the served POST scenario builds (*own-taken*: connection 4's submission in flight, reader 3 open), including one violating value per hypothesis and the relation holding after a fault. The host side is tests/test_owner.py OwnerSurvivesAFaultTests, which injects an unexpected exception on one connection and asserts the other is still served. TEETH (tests/acl2/owner-fault-tests.lisp, 2026-09-24): every owner-fault event above has a reachable witness on *own-taken*, and one must-fail per violable hypothesis: fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection 1 (other = id), fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission 1 (the in-flight submission is another connection's), fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission 1 (it is the faulted connection's), fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction 1 (a reader faults while connection 4 holds the transaction; the review had found no violating value). REDUNDANT HYPOTHESES: the (fn-own-inflight o) hypothesis of fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and of fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission can never be violated usefully -- with nothing in flight the slot stays empty -- and the test book proves both conclusions without it (oft-clears-the-faulted-submission-needs-only-the-id, oft-keeps-another-connections-submission-needs-only-the-id). The statements keep the hypothesis; removing it is a later decision. fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, -is-not-a-store-event and -reply-is-not-a-post-outcome have no hypothesis and carry a witness only. EVIDENCE: persvati run-20260924T152544Z-e3c9, manifest planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260924T152627Z-1775721.json: tests/acl2/owner-fault-tests passed, 4.0 s (books/owner-fault unchanged). OPEN under this target: nothing states that the HOST calls fn-own-fault at every point where it can fault -- the boundary's coverage is a code property, not a theorem -- and tools/run_reader.py has no such boundary at all. Native host calls fn-owner-fault through fnn-owner-serialized/fault-service, but at checkpoint 76901c1 also stops the service for unexpected serious conditions. The logical single-connection theorem does not establish native service survival; that actual-host obligation remains open. Shared-core failure and uncertain persistence require a global fence and are not justified as connection-local faults by this theorem.

proofs.title: Every byte-level crash image of a related store scans, and scans to an image the file kernel admits
proofs.statement: fn-bs-store-crash-image-scans (K1): for every byte store related to a file-kernel state and every image fn-bs-crash-imagep admits of it, the scan tools/run_store.py performs at open -- the config entry and its integrity check, the frontier entry and its decode, the contiguity of the transaction namespace, and the record list -- returns :ok and not any of its four :fault values. No trailer assumption is used: an authority inode is fenced before any name points at it (D1) and is never overwritten (D2), so the only freedom a crash has over the authority namespace is whether the last entry operation landed. fn-bs-store-crash-image-is-kernel-admissible (K2): what that scan reads is an image fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits, which outside the recovery window is the reliance predicate fn-sf-crash-imagep and inside it is that plus the two rollback arms of D14-b and D14-c -- the record the replay read and has not re-fenced, and the allocator rename that the fourth recovery barrier has not drained. fn-bs-store-recovery-is-a-kernel-crash (K3): fn-sf-image-crash at that image reproduces its frontier, its record list and the :replaying phase. fn-bs-crash-image-consumer-replay-ok: from the maintained E2 completed-prefix relation fn-csi-full-relationp, K2 and the platform crash-image arms, the exact scanned record list strictly replays the consumer projection, including recovery rollback. fn-bs-crash-image-reopens: the host reopen entry fn-sn-open-observed succeeds on every such image whose identity and topic histories replay (fn-sn-observed-identity-okp and fn-sn-observed-topic-okp), with E2 consumer replay derived rather than assumed. fn-bs-acknowledged-record-survives-byte-crash (K4): under the same maintained and observed conditions, an acknowledged outcome names a reopened record. K-sweep: fn-bs-staging-unlink-keeps-relation-and-scan, an unlink in :staging at any name and with any outcome keeps the byte relation to the same kernel state and keeps the scan; fn-bs-recover-sweep-keeps-relation-at-every-cut, every pair of fn-bs-recover-sweep-program's run (every recovery-stage-unlinked cut) is that kernel state with a related byte state and the original scan; fn-bs-sweep-round-keeps-every-cut-reopenable, over the names fn-sn-sweep-round returns (host/native/io.lisp fnn-sweep-staging via fn-store-sn-sweep-round), every identity- and topic-replayable crash image at every cut of the sweep reopens and the kernel state is the one before the sweep. The sweep's rounds (books/store-sweep.lisp): fn-sn-sweep-rounds-collect-every-orphan, with the kernel gate open and a positive observation bound, a staging directory of N unheld staging names ends :done and empty for every N; fn-sn-sweep-rounds-keep-every-name-they-may-not-remove; fn-sn-sweep-rounds-end-done-or-refused, the loop ends :done or :refused and :refused means more than one observation of names remains and that observation removes nothing. K5 scan-record form: fn-bs-stable-prefix-retained-by-byte-crash, under the same byte/kernel relation and modeled crash-image premise, retains the durable decoded record list as a prefix and bounds the scanned list to at most one additional record. K6 partial raw-frame form: fn-bs-k6-actual-record-linked-input-has-exact-frame proves that a well-formed byte state, ACL2-valid record input, fresh staging key, and absent final name at the file-fence cut make the actual P-RECORD linked cut point that final name at the new fenced inode containing the complete supplied frame; the modeled surviving-name crash image at both the actual linked and record-attempted cuts now reads exact raw octets and the decoder returns the candidate; the related-input trace derives no-prior-operation and final-name absence at the file cut for typed Store events; the actual pair-10 whole-list scanner result is now proved conditionally on relation of that pair, while universal relation preservation remains K0. Under a related ready byte/owner input, typed successor frontier frame and fresh staging name, the actual failed P-FRONTIER pair 12 of fn-bs-run is an EIO byte cut for each modeled pending-root-entry choice; the host-called configured-owner :store/:io error observation fences the Store projection while retaining fn-bs-store-relation. The :apply choice makes the candidate durable, while :drop keeps the old frontier. The actual configured-owner retention prepare event, built from the live owner sequence and txid plus host text octets, stages that exact event on the prepared branch and leaves a reserved Store unstaged on refusal. Served-entry byte relation and physical filesystem qualification remain separate obligations.
proofs.note: K1/K2 in byte-store-scan and K3/K4 in byte-store-keystones concern every modeled crash image of an already related byte/kernel state. The reopen subject is fn-sn-open-observed, called by host/store-node-host.lisp; native process startup reaches that entry through its wrapper. K4 additionally assumes maintained consumer completed-prefix consistency and observed identity and topic replay. The topic condition is not yet derived for every modeled byte crash image by the maintained Store relation; a valid physical FNST topic-anchor image after consumer bootstrap separates it from identity and consumer replay. Its recovery-window instances are vacuous because there are no current-process successes there; fn-bs-crash-image-reopens covers that window without a success premise. The identity condition has a kernel witness; its distinct byte-level premise witness remains missing. Framed metadata, a nonempty bootstrap/publication trace and a physically framed registration-before-bootstrap counterexample exercise the other composition boundaries. K5 proves the durable record list remains a prefix of the scanned image with at most one extra record, under the byte/kernel relation and modeled crash-image assumptions. K6 proves exact typed-frame provenance at the actual P-RECORD file/link cuts, surviving-name decoding and the conditional pair-10 whole-list scanner bridge. K7 proves recovery fencing at fn-sn-io for issued link, issued allocator rename and both authority-directory barrier errors; physical error classification remains a host obligation. K8 requires an actually issued pending transaction link as well as the relation: after the completed directory fence, every modeled crash image scans the old records plus the candidate. The earlier phase-and-relation-only K8 claim was false and is not reinstated. General K0 remains open. Completed slices establish the successful P-RECORD pair-10 relation and successful arbitrary-history P-FRONTIER pair-6, pair-12 and pair-14 relations under their stated related-input, typed-frame and fresh-staging contracts. The actual configured-owner :store/:io projection is fn-bs-k0-owner-io-store-is-node-io; its four-callback frontier join is a composition corollary with a valid configured-owner witness and premise counterexamples. The root-directory EIO choice packet proves the exact failed byte-run pair 12, a full related Store-node :error state and the owner callback projection for both supported pending-entry choices, :apply and :drop. The theorem is stated for all selectors because this model treats any non-:apply selector as :drop; only the two named choices are physically admissible. The owner retention preparation bridge names the host-called fn-ocfg-step event, proves its exact Store projection, and distinguishes staged exact-candidate from refusal under a reserved input; it does not supply a byte-related served entry. These results do not establish the relation at every served entry, all error/torn/recovery paths, program-mode host execution or physical syscall/barrier semantics. Native SIGKILL/reopen and filesystem-error observations are separately scoped runtime evidence, not power-loss qualification. The linked evidence preserves each earlier partial result and failed conjecture. Host tie (books/store-open-bridge.lisp, k4-bridges lane): the cited keystones stay the registry events; fn-cpo-open-observed-is-sn-open-observed-on-the-kernel and fn-cpo-open-observed-succeeds-exactly are the named theorems relating them to fn-cpo-open-observed, which host/store-node-host.lisp:159 and host/owner-host.lisp:193 call. Corollaries (the host's subject, not registry events): fn-bs-crash-image-reopens, fn-bs-acknowledged-record-survives-byte-crash, fn-bs-sweep-round-keeps-every-cut-reopenable -> their -of-host-open corollaries (added hypothesis fn-sob-configured-openp).
proofs.progress_note: 2026-09-22 lane t5/sweep: byte-store-keystones had been red since 4857c648 added fn-sn-observed-identity-okp to the kernel reopen theorems; K4 and fn-bs-crash-image-reopens carry the identity condition over the scanned records; E2 additionally requires the maintained fn-csi-full-relationp, whose strict consumer replay consequence over K2's scanned image is proved by fn-bs-crash-image-consumer-replay-ok. Authority list, old inode entries and fences, staged durable record equality, pending link/candidate and the kernel image are derived separately. This does not establish the input relation at every served call or cover other cuts, errors, recovery or physical barriers. Article call arguments now have a finite ACL2 bridge: fn-bs-k0-article-host-arguments-are-typed-record-input proves the exact native protected-prefix/trailer frame and ACL2 transaction name decode to the staged candidate; the composed pair-10 theorem remains conditional on a related physical byte state and fresh stage. Retention/identity event codec bridges and call-entry relation establishment remain open. ACL2 fn-sf-prepare-record and the host-reached fn-sn-prepare now preserve the byte relation from any related state, including successful article staging. fn-bs-k0-served-article-prepare-to-attempted-relation composes a reserved article prepare, ACL2 frame/name and the actual P-RECORD pair10, but still assumes a related physical state at reserved entry, a valid fresh stage, and a successful prepare. Whole served trace, other event kinds/cuts/outcomes and hardware barriers remain open. 2026-09-24 K4 topic repair: the Store v6 observed reopen correctly requires topic-prefix replay. A maintained actual Store topic/crash bridge remains open; this conditional certificate is not universal recovery. 2026-09-24 K0 retention continuation: the ACL2-authored retention event now round-trips through the shared canonical Store decoder and supplies the exact native protected-frame, trailer and transaction-name arguments to the actual P-RECORD pair-10 relation theorem. The stopped pair-11 transaction-directory EIO run has both physical outcomes: :apply has the appended durable candidate and retains the attempted byte/kernel relation before the error callback; :drop retains the old durable prefix; both drain the transaction-directory choice and the callback fences. Exact applied-conclusion teeth separately drop the related-input, typed-frame and fresh-stage premises. The dropped-prefix theorem is a conditional composition result, not an independently toothed keystone: its relation and typed-frame premises may be redundant for that conclusion. The owner preparation bridge is separate; call-entry byte relation, native syscall correspondence, all P-RECORD cuts and whole recovery remain open. STAGING BARRIER ERROR (k0-steps, PKT-086): fn-bs-k0-staging-fsync-error-preserves-relation; fn-bs-k0-step-inputp admits (:fsync-dir :staging) with an error outcome whose landed part is a well-formed crash selection of the staging entry operations. ROOT RENAME AND AUTHORITY ERRORS (k0-rest, PKT-080/086): the coverage of fn-bs-k0-coveredp is generic over the :root name (fn-bs-k0s-root-rename-pendingp; the marker is its instance), the :rename arm admits any :root name but the frontier (onto config.json only from a fenced, allocated inode passing fn-bs-config-okp), and the state-checkpoint and profile programs' cuts and every step at their pairs with any outcome follow from the general step theorem. The :root and :transactions barriers' error outcomes are covered from any related state (the transactions one in :record-attempted when a link is pending): the one pending authority entry lands or is dropped, and both results are related. 2026-09-25 lane k0-recovery: the recovery window as step kinds of the general step (fn-bs-k0w-step-preserves-relation), the recovery program by the step from any window-related pair (fn-bs-k0v-recover-program-by-step), the admin.lisp:107 re-recovery over fn-cpo-open-observed (fn-bs-k0v-host-rerecovery-keeps-relation-at-every-cut), and a pre-init relation kept by :mkdir, :link-eexist and every initializer step (fn-bs-k0i-step-preserves-pre-init); see planning/evidence/k0-recovery-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.title: The inbound transit decision the served path reaches is the model's, over the node the owner holds now (K2 loop, K3 duplicate)
proofs.statement: fn-peer-loop-is-refused: an article whose Path already names this node's path-identity is never accepted through transit, and fn-peer-transfer leaves the node. fn-peer-history-is-have-at-offer and fn-peer-history-is-refused-at-transfer: a Message-ID in the history is :have :history at the offer and is never accepted at the transfer. The subject rule (AGENTS.md rule 1) is closed in two halves: fn-peer-ihave-of-a-held-message-id-is-435-and-no-article and fn-peer-check-of-a-held-message-id-is-438-and-no-offer-outstanding say the reply octets fn-peer-command emits ARE that decision and that the connection does not enter article mode, and fn-own-read-offers-against-the-live-node says the node the served path supplies is fn-sn-node of the owner's own store. The host line is host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> books/owner.lisp fn-own-read for the offer, and host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide -> fn-peer-decide-transfer for the transfer. Covered scope: one connection's offer and one article's transfer against one node and one pinned peer record; the hypotheses are the connection facts the decision needs before it reaches its history arm. NOT covered: the peer record is still the one the connection opened with, so a (:set-peer ...) delta reaches the transfer decision and not the offer decision; and fn-peer-decide-transfer emits no :date-future or :no-clock, because the tree has no certified RFC 5322 date-time reader.
proofs.progress_note: Certified on persvati (farm run-20260921T033252Z-6ba2, 0 failures over 87 books: books/peer-inbound, books/peer-inbound-invariants, books/owner, books/owner-invariants, books/served, tests/acl2/peer-inbound-tests, tests/acl2/served-tests). Until w11/transit-correct the offer half was unreachable on a live connection: fn-peer-open-session pinned the node at :open and nothing replaced it, so the wire answered 335 and 238 for an article the connection had itself delivered (V0-TRANSIT-DUPLICATE, V0-TRANSIT-CHECK-DUP at 6fb30ca). The loop half was never inert in the model and was inert in the v0 matrix's deployment, which set no path-identity on either node. CHANGED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-own-read-offers-against-the-live-node` now hypothesises `fn-peer-sessionp` of the connection's peer session beside the bound role. `fn-own-conn-live-session` (books/owner.lisp) refreshes the node only under `(fn-peer-session-cfg ps)`, so on a bound peer beside a NULL configuration the session is handed back untouched and the node equation is false of it; `64a80197` made that pairing the recognizer's business, and the object the equation fails on is not a `fn-peer-sessionp` and the served path does not reach it. The theorem's other four conjuncts -- the peer, the configuration, the transfer and the inflight count are carried over -- hold on both branches and are unrestricted.

proofs.title: Concrete storage naming, fresh initializer image and conditional frontier preservation
proofs.statement: Under successful syscall outcomes, fn-bs-init-program establishes fn-bs-store-relation from fn-bs-initial-inputp. Under a positive write unit, fn-bs-first-frontier-program preserves that relation when fn-bs-initial-inputp and fn-bs-frontier-inputp hold. The actual fn-bs-step interpreter preserves a related prestate through the enumerated noncommit frontier observations; for a successful directory observation it additionally requires phase :frontier-attempted and independently durable candidate bytes with a quiet root. These are conditional model results: current Store.initialize and Store.advance_frontier correspondence, full initialization/recovery syscall composition, general crash-image preservation, and platform durability remain open. For naturals i and j, equal fn-bs-txn-name-impl outputs imply equal inputs; the constrained naming seam is attached to that renderer. From an empty byte store and initial kernel with fn-bsi-fresh-inputp and successful syscall observations, fn-bsi-current-init-program reaches fn-bsi-current-initial-image, including configuration history and lock publication. The existing relation alone does not observe configuration history or the lock.

proofs.title: BP creation allocation non-reuse across observed-file recovery
proofs.statement: Target: under explicit stable-storage and admissible crash-image premises, finite traces through the actual sequence recover/reserve functions never return a previously returned creation sequence, including old-or-new rename outcomes, lost returns and restart without hidden in-memory phase knowledge.

proofs.title: Durable native BP lifecycle and application-obligation confinement
proofs.statement: Target: reachable traces of the host-called fn-bpn-step preserve valid lifecycle state, withhold queue acceptance and sending until the matching durable records exist, retain exact work/peer/wire context across restart, fence mutation after uncertain publication, and never discharge application obligations from transport completion or bundle expiry.
proofs.pending_subject: The native host calls fn-bpnp-step (host/native/bp-service.lisp:170, fnn-bps-foundation-step), wrapping each lower machine event as (:base E) at :176-177. fn-bpnp-step-base-event-refines-fn-bpn-step equates that arm with fn-bpn-step (state and effects), so the lower lifecycle and send-authorization keystones hold of the called step's base on (:base E) only; the served step's own receive, delivery, family, forwarding and recovery arms have no lifecycle or kind-8 send-authorization keystone. fn-bpnp-step-emits-no-release-and-no-receipt-prepare holds over every served event. A durable kind 8 without a kind 9 at a process death is re-offered on the next session to its next hop with the same held bundle, up to three retries, then held and reported as stranded (spec 4.3.1, default adopted by the coordinator 2026-09-24, pending ember); the keystones cover the lone-candidate selection, the offer binding and the retry bound, not multi-candidate fairness or the replay fact that recovered attempt epochs precede the new epoch. Physical publication observations and reachable crash cuts remain open.
proofs.progress_note: Over the called fn-bpnp-step: guard premises preserved by every host event; :progress leaves held rows unchanged and issued unchanged or a fresh pending dispatch; no :release or :receipt-prepare effect on any event; on (:base E) the answer is exactly fn-bpn-step's state and effects or nothing. The lower fn-bpn-step keystones (lifecycle invariant, send authorized by a durable attempt record) are cited through that bridge. The spec 11.1 witnesses N05 (attempt half), N06 (machine half), N08 (as the stranded negative), N11 (refusal half), BP-R02, R06, R07, R15 and R16 run through fn-bpnp-step in bp-node-counterexamples-tests. The actual fn-bpn-step preserves fn-bpn-lifecycle-invariantp under that input invariant and fn-bpn-machine-eventp, and under the lifecycle invariant its send and queue-accept effects require the exact durable authorization or an exact retained duplicate. The hbox source-pinned closure and reachable authorization counterexamples are archived in bp-lifecycle-assurance-w18-2026-09-21.md; the duplicate persvati dependency timeout remains negative evidence. These logical results assume the reported persistence outcomes and do not establish physical durability or a current combined native image. Native lifecycle append consumes the shared immutable publisher; authority-barrier failure remains uncertain. Lane defaults-precise (2026-09-24): a ready recovery through fn-bpnp-step installs exactly the held rows fn-bpnf-family-replay-rows computes from the durable FNBS rows, over the event the host builds (fn-bpnp-host-recovery-installs-the-durable-replay), so the kind-8 retry count after a restart is the one the durable kind-8 history gives; witness: four restarts from the fresh initial state over the framed rows (retries 0 to 3, then stranded), must-fail: a fenced clock-domain decision installs nothing. The sender reads a TCPCL XFER_REFUSE by its reason: fn-bpnp-tcpcl-outcome (called by host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-forward-contact) returns (:refused r) for a peer reason r, the kind-9 record fn-bpnp-step proposes carries the event's outcome unchanged, reason 1 (Completed) settles exactly as :sent through fn-bpnp-forward-result-apply, and every other reason stays non-terminal. A settled non-terminal kind 9 clears the slot, so the budget bounds uncertain re-offers only. hbox run-20260924T230614Z-3685. N16 (lane n16-rotation, 2026-09-25): fn-bpnp-step on (:rotate g ck) is fn-bpnp-rotate-step behind the uncertainty fence (fn-bpnp-step-rotate-is-rotate-step) and on a :persist-result while a checkpoint is issued is fn-bpnp-rotation-persist-step (fn-bpnp-step-rotation-result-is-rotation-result); the record count after a checkpoint's answer is 0 exactly on the matching durable answer and unchanged otherwise (fn-bpnp-step-rotation-resets-credit-only-on-durable); the four rotation effects are inside the no-release/no-receipt-prepare confinement. Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-counterexamples-tests (N16 section). hbox run-20260925T051528Z-15c2. Open: finding N16-F1, a reopened node's first operation reuses the rotation's id.
proofs.application_join_scope: Native application/Store join and receipt-decision recovery have scoped runtime witnesses. The A3 effective-handoff projection has a certified exact-job/peer/payload/FNRJ-premise theorem plus byte replay, restart and distinct-trigger tests; its native caller and combined-image test passed, with broader trace assurance still open. General joined trace preservation, observed-channel admission, expired-held delivery eligibility and physical publication cuts remain open. Transport completion or expiry does not establish application acceptance or release authority. A versioned kind-5 receive anchor and ACL2 pre-Store clocked selector are source-present. The selector's live-priority theorem and a two-durable-receive positive trace certify at the selected roots; matched application result and durable kind-7 completion leave the older clock-uncertain row held. All-uncertain selection reports uncertainty, and an ambiguous publication still fences the foundation transition. For the host-called fn-bpnp-step, fn-bpnp-step-progress-preserves-held proves one :progress event leaves held obligations unchanged, and fn-bpnp-step-progress-issued-unchanged-or-pending-dispatch proves it leaves the issued operation unchanged or, only from none, installs a pending dispatch at the current epoch and next operation id. A certified two-kind-5 reachable trace gives an older route-less transit row a per-key route wait, then delivers a younger local request and settles durable kind 7; changed generation rechecks the old row. A failed cold recovery retains the wait and state, while successful replay clears the wait. This is the route-wait part of N03. A source-matched native image, four-class N03 fairness, N04 session/MRU forwarding and N05 journal debt remain open.

proofs.title: Outbound NNTP TLS phase ordering and no protocol downgrade
proofs.statement: fn-fc-offers-and-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login: for a connection in the phase fn-owner-feed-dial-open installs (greeting, or handshake-owed for implicit TLS) whose peer record requires a protected channel (STARTTLS or implicit TLS, or a credential whose profile did not permit clear text), and for EVERY sequence of socket reads and TLS reports fed to the two functions the host calls -- fn-fc-step (host/owner-host.lisp:1591, in fn-owner-feed-reply-chunk, called by host/native/feed-service.lisp:256) and fn-fc-after-tls (owner-host.lisp:1496, in fn-owner-feed-tls-established, feed-service.lisp:194) -- the kinds the host acts on satisfy fn-fc-gate-okp, a property written over observations only: no MODE, no ready and no delivered reply (so, through the :feed-conn install at owner-host.lisp:1454 that fn-feed-offer's natp conn test waits on, no IHAVE, CHECK or TAKETHIS) before a line coded 382 was answered :tls, a TLS report was accepted after it, and, when the record carries a credential, a line coded 281 was read; and no AUTHINFO USER or PASS before the 382 and the TLS report (implicit TLS starts past the 382). A clear transport with a credential and no clear-text permission therefore never sends it and never goes live. fn-fc-starttls-refusal-closes-before-the-credential: in the STARTTLS phase, a complete line whose code is not 382 (RFC 4642 2.2.1's 502 or 580) is :refused -- the host records the peer-local loss and closes (feed-service.lisp:391-395) -- the connection is closed, and the observations of any later reads and TLS reports on it contain no command, handshake or offer, so nothing falls back to clear text. fn does not read CAPABILITIES before STARTTLS; the peer's answer to STARTTLS is the advertisement the machine acts on. Trusted, not proved: that the host reports TLS up only after fnn-tls-connect verified the chain against the record's anchor and the server name (OpenSSL; tests/test_native_tls_transport.py's wrong-anchor and wrong-hostname witnesses), and that the socket carries the rendered bytes. Covered scope: one connection incarnation's phase machine; the composition with owner-feed's offer (fn-feed-offer and fn-feed-send need a natp fn-feed-conn, set only at :ready and cleared by fn-feed-lost) is read from the definitions, not proved here.
proofs.pending_subject: The image gate (plan T9): the matrix's V0-TRANSIT-TLS-AB/BA and V0-TRANSIT-TLS-WRONG-ANCHOR rows measured on a frozen image, two nodes on one box, including a kill -9 of the sender mid-transfer and exactly one copy after restart. OpenSSL chain and hostname behavior remains trusted integration evidence, not an ACL2 proof.
proofs.progress_note: T9c, 2026-09-22: the two keystones above over the functions the host calls, with tests/acl2/feed-connection-teeth-tests.lisp as the teeth book -- a reachable non-degenerate witness per keystone (a connection built from a decoded profile and driven through a real peer's replies, STARTTLS and implicit), and one must-fail per hypothesis under the keystone's own hints, each preceded by the keystone itself through the same macro so that no must-fail passes on a broken hint. The earlier status text named fn-fc-step theorems that did not exist; these replace them. Status stays in-progress until an image measures the matrix rows.

proofs.title: Principal-bound inbound peer role selection
proofs.statement: fn-auth-step-binds-a-peer-role-only-by-a-principal-login: for any session and any wire event, if fn-auth-step leaves a peer role on a connection that had none, then the connection was well-formed, not handshaking, unauthenticated and on a channel its policy accepts (so protected-only without TLS never binds, which is also fn-auth-step-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls, PRF-031), the event was an AUTHINFO PASS line with one token that checks against the cached name's stored verifier, the subject installed is that credential's principal, the role is fn-auth-principal-match of the principal under the configuration pinned into the connection, and the role is principal-derived (fn-auth-principal-rolep). fn-auth-principal-match is the one peer whose record, read back through fn-cfg-peer-find, says (:principal HEX) and which is the only auth-principal row naming HEX; zero rows (mismatch) or two (duplicate) give nil. fn-auth-step-principal-login-binds-exactly-the-unique-match: on a well-formed, non-handshaking, unbound, unauthenticated reader whose channel the policy accepts, a command line inside the 510-octet bound that tokenizes to AUTHINFO PASS <one token>, after a USER, with a checking secret, is answered 281, installs the principal and leaves exactly the match as the role -- a peer for one match, a still-authenticated reader for a mismatch or a duplicate, and the 281 the same in every case. fn-auth-step-starttls-clears-a-principal-role: whenever a step enters the TLS handshake (a hold that is not an XREDEEM redemption hold, fn-auth-redeem-waitp; that hold is PRF-164's fn-auth-step-redeem-hold-keeps-the-role), the new session has no subject, no cached name and no principal-derived role, and keeps the old role exactly when it was not principal-derived (a source-address peer stays a peer). fn-ocfg-open-begins-unbound: every open fn-ocfg-open accepts installs, at the identifier it allocated, a reader with no role, subject, cached name, TLS layer or handshake, whatever the owner's other connections did, so a reconnect begins unbound. Covered scope: one step of fn-auth-step, and the OPEN transition of fn-ocfg-open; the fold over a whole read is OB-AUTH-FOLD's. That the check refuses a wrong secret is A-CRYPTO and is witnessed, not proved. The subjects are what the host calls: fn-auth-step through books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk reaches through fn-own-read and fn-served-step, and fn-ocfg-open at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t9b-role, 2026-09-22 (plan T9, row PRF-049): the four events above are the keystones; tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp keystones 8 to 10 and tests/acl2/owner-config-tests.lisp carry a reachable witness each (a real enrolled credential, a replayed peer table with one principal peer beside a source-address peer, a duplicate table, a table with no principal row, and a reconnect through fn-ocfg-read and fn-ocfg-open) and one must-fail per hypothesis, generated by a macro that first admits the full statement from the keystone, with a refuting value evaluated beside each; tools/teeth_check.py does not expand those macros. The same lane repaired fn-auth-bind-principal-peer: it bound on the auth-principal row count alone, so a row group carrying an auth-principal row that denotes a source-address record (admissible through a :set-peer delta; the teeth's shadow table) was bound, was not principal-derived, and survived STARTTLS; it now binds only fn-auth-principal-match, which reads the record back. Status stays in-progress until the image gate: a native reconnect on a deployed image, which is root's.

proofs.title: Mandatory hybrid authored-source profile binding
proofs.statement: The host-called fn-hsig-authorize-at, at the version fn-hsig-source-version names (version 1 for an authored source of at most 65535 octets, the u16 length's width; version 2 above, up to the u32's 4294967295), authorizes only a canonical Ed25519-and-ML-DSA-65 profile with exact fixed component widths and two verified primitive observations; each version's domain-separated, length-delimited signing preimage contains the principal, ordered enrolled key set and exact authored source octets. Across both versions equal preimages determine the same version, principal, keys and source (fn-hsig-signed-preimage-at-injective), no v1 preimage equals any v2 preimage (fn-hsig-v1-v2-preimages-disjoint), and on a v1 source the versioned preimage and authorization are the v1 functions (fn-hsig-preimage-at-v1-source-is-v1-preimage-by-definition, fn-hsig-authorize-at-v1-source-is-authorize-by-definition), so every v1 signature keeps its bytes.
proofs.progress_note: host/native/signatures.lisp calls fn-hsig-host-authorize, whose body calls fn-hsig-authorize. The framing keystones prove that equal valid subject bodies, and equal tagged signing preimages, determine the same principal, ordered Ed25519/ML-DSA-65 key set and exact authored source. Projection witnesses are non-degenerate and each theorem has one must-fail event per hypothesis. Reachable tests cover both-valid, each bad component, absent ML-DSA, unknown/unsupported ML-DSA, stripping, component order/profile confusion, source changes and enrolled-key changes. Native component evidence covers libsodium Ed25519 and OpenSSL 3.6.4 ML-DSA-65. These are byte-framing results, not cryptographic injectivity: primitive security, RNG, ABI and library correctness remain trusted assumptions; key custody, recovery authority and durable article/verdict composition remain open. The byte-framing injectivity book and its hypothesis counterexamples certified on hbox in certify-20260921T181329Z-2345431; the complete selected closure source digests match the integrated source. This does not certify live author submission or either signature primitive. Bounds P4 (2026-09-25, D27): the v1 source bound is the u16's 65535, not the article constant, and carrier v2 (item 1 = 2, tag fn-authored-source-hybrid-v2, u32 length) signs sources above it; the host calls fn-hsig-authorize-at and fn-hsig-signed-preimage-at through fn-hsig-host-authorize and fn-hsig-host-preimage (host/hybrid-signature-host.lisp) with fn-hsig-source-version. The two -by-definition events are the v1 correspondence, not keystones; the keystones are the per-version injectivity, the cross-version disjointness and the versioned injectivity, each with one must-fail per hypothesis in its test book. Certified with every dependent in certify-20260925T025612Z-3717718; native and verifier results in planning/evidence/bounds-p4-2026-09-25.md. Signed-path (2026-09-25): every source a carrier version admits (fn-hsig-subject-at-p) is within the kind-4 composite's authored-source bound, which is the v2 carrier's u32 width, so the Store never refuses a signable source by a data cap. The native signature copy (host/native/crypto.lisp fnn-crypto-octets) read the preimage list by ELT, quadratic in the source (99.6% of a 215 KB signed POST, 99.9% of signing); it is one pass now: signing 200 KiB 145.29 s to under 5 s, the signed POST 47.45 s to 0.76 s (unsigned 0.34 s).

proofs.title: Authoritative mixed Store history and atomic identity acceptance
proofs.statement: The host-called owner publication path writes one ordered Store-event stream whose journal sequence is independent of burned allocator transaction IDs; a bound kind-4 article and historical verdict commit atomically against the exact earlier enrolled key snapshot, recovery reconstructs the same historical verdict without current-key recomputation, and expected prepublication refusal consumes its reservation while indeterminate or structural faults remain fenced.
proofs.pending_subject: The carried journal sequence is preserved by initial, prepare, I/O, refusal, abort, finish and recovery transitions, but its invariant has not been joined to every actual owner publication path or the physical publication/recovery cuts. Prove the kind-4 snapshot/article/verdict binding over the host-called completion and recovery paths. The raw witness establishes condition routing and reservation cleanup only; it does not prove filesystem durability or cryptographic primitive correctness.
proofs.progress_note: Source integration carries journal sequence separately from allocation frontier, uses one native prepared-publication helper for article, retention and identity events, and replays enrolled kind-3 plus bound kind-4 history. The phase-aware relation fn-sn-identity-sequencep and fn-sn-finish-preserves-identity-sequence cover every completion arm. The selected kind-4 schema-1 codec now carries exact authored source and its ACL2-derived identity separately from the embedded received-carrier article; the replay snapshot binder checks carrier projection, enrolled ordered keys, both signature components' shape and the recorded principal. ACL2 constructor/codec tests exercise source and keyset substitutions. The native caller now verifies both primitives before asking ACL2 to construct this event. Combined saved-image acceptance/reopen evidence, reader HDR projection, host/physical recovery refinement and key succession remain open; structural replay checks do not prove native primitive correctness.

proofs.title: Outbound AUTHINFO phase ordering and secret custody
proofs.statement: WHEN: fn-fc-offers-and-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login (PRF-047's keystone) says the AUTHINFO lines are sent only after the 382 and the TLS report, and that the feed makes no MODE, no ready and no offer until a 281 is read, on every sequence of reads and TLS reports fed to fn-fc-step and fn-fc-after-tls; a credential on a clear transport without the profile's explicit permission is never sent. REFUSAL: fn-fc-refused-login-closes-without-an-offer: in either login phase, a complete line whose code is not 281 (and, answering USER, not 381) is :refused, which fn-owner-feed-connection-result-kind (owner-host.lisp:1566) reports as :connection-refused and feed-service.lisp:391-395 answers with the peer-local loss and a close; the connection is closed and nothing fed to it afterwards produces a command, a handshake or an offer. WHAT: fn-fc-auth-user-command-sends-the-configured-name-alone and fn-fc-auth-pass-command-sends-the-configured-secret-alone: on a state whose name (secret) is an fn-fap-tokenp true list, the renderer the host calls (owner-host.lisp:1505, 1605, 1610) returns exactly the prefix, the token and CRLF, one line, so a credential cannot carry a second command; fn-fc-decoded-profile-renders-verbatim-in-every-state composes it with what the host does, with no hypothesis: the profile bytes go through fn-fap-decode (feed-service.lisp:172), the decoded fields are installed by fn-fc-initial-auth-state (owner-host.lisp:1484), and in every state any sequence of reads and TLS reports reaches, the USER and PASS lines are the prefix, the decoded field and CRLF. Not proved here: that the profile file is owner-only and bounded (feed-service.lisp:161-168, native integration evidence), the secrecy of the secret on the wire beyond the TLS ordering above, and the loss-to-requeue composition of fn-feed-lost.
proofs.pending_subject: The image gate (plan T9): the matrix's V0-TRANSIT-AUTHINFO-AB/BA and V0-TRANSIT-AUTHINFO-WRONG rows measured on a frozen image. Filesystem ownership and mode checks on the profile remain native integration evidence; the loss-to-requeue composition is PRF-029/K5's (T9a).
proofs.progress_note: T9c, 2026-09-22: events are the five theorems above; the teeth book is tests/acl2/feed-connection-teeth-tests.lisp (for the unconditional composition, the must-fail is the false neighbour: the same claim over a name and secret that did not come through fn-fap-decode, refuted by a name carrying CRLF and a second command). fn-fap-decode-yields-two-renderable-tokens and fn-fap-decode-refusal-yields-no-credential in books/feed-auth-profile.lisp are the decode facts the composition uses. Status stays in-progress until an image measures the matrix rows.

proofs.title: NEWNEWS exactly filters durable acceptance stamps and reads no payload
proofs.statement: fn-nntp-newnews-scan-is-the-acceptance-filter equates the one-pass served scan with an independent quadratic specification that searches later-accepted articles for the nearest natural stamp, proving soundness and completeness of the conservative legacy horizon and wildmat scope. fn-nntp-newnews-scan-reads-no-payload proves erasing all article payload octets leaves the answer unchanged; fn-nntp-newnews-scan-lines-at-most-candidates bounds the output by matching available articles; fn-nntp-newnews-lines-are-clean proves every line is safe to render. fn-nntp-step-dispatches-newnews-to-the-newnews-response is the subject equation for the host-called dispatcher; fn-nntp-newnews-response-preserves-session and fn-nntp-effects-newnews-response carry the response through the served effect path. Covered scope: one reader session on a pinned committed archive, with a natural schema-1 acceptance stamp or the conservative schema-0 horizon. One command costs O(A*Gprime) for A committed articles and Gprime matched groups, reads no payload and emits at most C lines for C candidates. The true-time no-miss claim for legacy articles assumes A-CLOCK and is outside this theorem.
proofs.note: At this source, green_check finds books/nntp-newnews green at its exact include closure in certify-20260923T232942Z-484654, its test book green in certify-20260924T005919Z-653679, books/nntp-invariants green in certify-20260923T232820Z-480447, and books/nntp-effects green in certify-20260923T232942Z-484654; none has moved dependencies. These are archived certification records, not a current native image qualification. The earlier T2b affected-closure run is certify-20260923T170842Z-2026382; native served-reader validation remains separate.

proofs.title: The operator's post is injected as a served POST is, and its retry is the stored article
proofs.statement: fn-own-operator-submission-is-an-injection-of-the-payload: if fn-own-operator-submit-result answers :submitted, fn-own-operator-submit queues exactly one control submission whose decision is injected, carries the Message-ID and newsgroup list the command named, and whose octets are a re-injection of the submitted octets by the owner's injecting agent (fn-inj-reinjectionp: the agent's Path line, an Injection-Date, the agent's Injection-Info, optionally the generated Message-ID and Date lines, then the submitted octets unchanged); fn-own-operator-decision-is-an-injection-of-the-payload states the same of the decision for any configuration, clock and node. fn-own-operator-submit-without-a-clock-refuses-and-changes-nothing: with no clock observation, or one without a wall time, the result is :refused and the owner is unchanged (D10-a). fn-own-operator-retry-resubmits-the-stored-injection: if fn-inj-decide injected the octets under one clock with that Message-ID and the node holds exactly those injected octets under it, then under any later usable clock the decision is those stored octets, so the store answers the Message-ID's duplicate rather than a conflict. All three rest on fn-inj-injected-article-is-a-reinjection-of-its-source (books/injection-invariants.lisp): every article fn-inj-decide injects is a re-injection of its source by its configured agent, for every clock reading. Covered scope: the owner's decision and its queue entry; the store attempt that follows is the served POST's, and the duplicate decision the store answers is fn-pb-existing-action (books/poster-bytes.lisp, host-called since D25), which refines fn-sn-existing-action (fn-pb-existing-action-refines-the-byte-identity-decision; its exact outcome is stated in books/poster-bytes-invariants.lisp); a single theorem composing this operator retry through the host-called Store attempt is still open. The subject is what the host calls: fn-own-operator-submit through the (:operator-submit ...) event, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-operator-submit steps and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized calls for `fn operator CONFIG post`.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the INN lab's finding 1 (operator post fed INN an article with no Path; 437). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-operator-tests.lisp builds the lab's own operator article through a real owner (configure, observe, submit, take, the store events, the completion) and asserts the queued octets byte for byte against the Path, Injection-Date and Injection-Info lines the lab's served POST carried; one must-fail per hypothesis with a refuting value beside it (the retry keystone through a macro that first admits the full statement). The native tests that run it on an image (tests/test_native_control.py) have not run: no image carries this yet.

proofs.title: An injected article's From is an RFC 5322 mailbox-list (RFC 5536 3.1.2)
proofs.statement: fn-mbx-mailbox-list-names-an-address: every value fn-mbx-mailbox-listp accepts contains an "@" octet, the addr-spec every mailbox carries. fn-inj-injected-proto-article-has-a-mailbox-list-from: whenever fn-inj-decide injects, the From field of the parsed proto-article is accepted by fn-mbx-mailbox-listp and names an address, so `From: yue` (answered 240 and served on 2026-09-22) is refused :from-invalid with `441 posting failed; From is not a valid mailbox list`. fn-mbx-mailbox-listp is RFC 5322 section 3.4's mailbox-list under RFC 5536 sections 2.1 and 2.2 (no obsolete syntax but obs-phrase, US-ASCII), bounded by the header block before either of its two passes, and reads nothing through the Lisp reader. Covered scope: soundness in the one direction stated (accepted implies an address); that the recognizer accepts every conformant mailbox-list is not a theorem and is witnessed across the grammar's productions. The subject is fn-inj-decide, which books/nntp-post.lisp fn-nntp-post-step calls on the served POST path (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read) and books/owner.lisp fn-own-operator-decision calls on the operator's.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the agents run's `From: yue`. Teeth in tests/acl2/injection-tests.lisp: the INN lab's POSTed article (its injected octets are what innd received) and `From: yue` refused :from-invalid; accepted and refused values across the productions; one must-fail per hypothesis. The v0 matrix row V0-POST-FROM-MAILBOX measures it on a node; no image carries it yet.

proofs.title: A relayed article changes in Path and Xref only, once, at acceptance (RFC 5537 3.6, 3.7)
proofs.statement: Over fn-peer-relayed-octets, the octets this node stores, serves and feeds on for an article a peer transferred: fn-peer-relayed-octets-change-only-path-and-xref -- removing every Path and Xref field (with its continuation lines) from what arrived and from what is stored leaves the same octets, so every other header field in order, the blank line and the body are byte-identical; fn-peer-relayed-octets-are-idempotent -- a second pass by the same node changes nothing; fn-peer-relayed-octets-carry-no-xref -- no Xref field is stored; fn-peer-relayed-octets-name-this-node-in-every-path -- when the node has a <path-identity>, every Path field of what is stored begins with it and "!" (RFC 5537 3.6 step 7, 3.7 step 6; the 3.2.1 diagnostic follows it). None has a hypothesis but the last, whose one is the identity. Each is the article-level keystone of books/path-update.lisp (fn-pu-relay-article-changes-only-path-and-xref, -is-idempotent, -leaves-no-xref, -names-the-agent-in-every-path), proved by one induction each over a walk of the raw header lines whose re-read of its own output is exact. fn-peer-injection-arguments-payload-unfolds: the payload the transfer stages for fn-node-prepare is fn-peer-relayed-octets of the received octets. Covered scope: the octets; what a reader receives is those octets (fn-durable-completion-installs-exact-pending-article, PRF-002), and the served rendering's dot-stuffing is the wire books'. An article with no Path field gets none (RFC 5537 3.7 step 1's rejection of it is open). The subjects are what the host calls: fn-peer-relayed-octets at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take, which fills fn-owner-submit-octets, the octets host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-one digests and stores; and fn-peer-injection-arguments at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide, whose staged payload the drain compares with them before the store attempt. fn-peer-relayed-octets-keep-the-received-path-tail (2026-09-24; keystone fn-pu-relay-article-keeps-the-received-path-tail, books/path-update-tail.lisp): when the node has a <path-identity>, the content of each stored Path field line, read by fn-pu-path-contents with the walk's own line classification, is the received content with <identity>!<diagnostic>! in front, or unchanged when it already begins with <identity>!; so the update prepends and the received Path is the tail. Covered scope: the first physical line of each Path field; folded continuation lines are copied and not read.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the INN lab's findings 2 and 3 (fn served INN's Path without itself, and INN's Xref). Decided at acceptance, not at serving time: specs/peering.md 2.3 carries the argument. Teeth in tests/acl2/peer-inbound-tests.lisp, last section: innfeed's own TAKETHIS octets become the stored article byte for byte (Path fnA.hbox.test!!inn.hbox.test!..., no Xref), through the transfer to the durable article, with the parser's view of the result; .MISMATCH. for a peer expecting another identity; a Path line the update would push past 998 octets refused :oversize; one must-fail per hypothesis (and, for the three statements with none, the stronger statement refuted by the lab's value). The INN lab rows V0-INN-SERVING-AGENT and V0-INN-OPERATOR-POST measure it on a node; no image carries it yet.

proofs.title: A served POST's Injection-Info names the node's path-identity
proofs.statement: fn-oag-post-config-agent-is-the-path-identity: when the replayed configuration's path-identity policy is set, the posting configuration fn-oag-post-config installs (called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-config, which fn-owner-recover and fn-owner-reconfigure-complete install with fn-own-configure) has that identity's octets as its agent; unset, the agent is fn.example.invalid. fn-oag-open-pins-the-owner-config: a connection fn-ocfg-open opens (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open) at an identifier no connection already holds pins the owner's installed configuration; fn-oag-configured-open-pins-the-path-identity composes the two. fn-oag-served-post-names-the-pinned-agent: for any socket read fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix performs (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk), if the connection's served state satisfies fn-served-connp, the submission the read hands the owner, when it is an injected article, carries the Injection-Info line generated from the agent the connection pinned; the chain runs through fn-served-step, fn-served-feed, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step, fn-peer-step and fn-nntp-post-step to fn-inj-injected-article-names-the-configured-agent over fn-inj-decide. Covered scope: the served POST path; the fn-served-connp premise is the served invariant the owner does not carry (the premise PRF-006 records for fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix), and no value is known on which the conclusion fails without it. fn.toml's [posting] agent is refused by run (fn-native-config-unsupported-key), so the path-identity policy is the only agent.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t6b-profile, 2026-09-22: the served-POST keystone is proved over the host-called fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix under the fn-served-connp premise; tests/acl2/owner-agent-tests.lisp carries a reachable witness built as the host builds it (a replayed history with the policy set path-identity delta, fn-oag-post-config, fn-ocfg-open, one POST read through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix whose queued article says Injection-Info: hbox.ember.software) and a must-fail per hypothesis, with a refuting value for the identity and freshness hypotheses and none known for the served premise. The image measurement is tests/test_native_profile.py and V0-NODE-PROFILE.

proofs.title: The native service log says what the reply says, one line per event
proofs.statement: fn-olog-served-post-line-says-accepted-iff-durable: the line host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-outcome renders for a served submission begins with the word accepted exactly when fn-own-outcome-completion of the host's word is :durable, the completion fn-own-outcome renders into the 240; a host word alone never makes it say accepted. fn-olog-control-post-line-says-the-control-result: the control line's first word is the word of fn-own-control-outcome-result, the value the control reply carries. fn-olog-served-post-line-is-one-line, fn-olog-control-post-line-is-one-line and fn-olog-connection-line-is-one-line: no line contains CR or LF, whatever octets the Message-ID, agent or peer name held. fn-olog-staging-cleanup-line-is-one-line: the line host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-staging-cleanup renders for an error fnn-publish's best-effort staging cleanup swallowed after the record is durable contains no CR or LF, whatever the stage path or the OS error text held; that the host writes it exactly once per swallowed error is measured by the NNTP probe's record-stage-unlinked EIO row, not proved. Covered scope: the rendered octets; that host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-log writes them and one LF to the file run opened append-only is measured by tests/test_native_profile.py, not proved. bp-app-refusal-line-says-refused-iff-refused: the BP application receiver's line for a transfer it did not accept (host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-deliver, through host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-refusal-log) begins with refused exactly when the receiver answered :refused or :clock-unusable, so a busy owner reads deferred and an unknown word uncertain; fn-olog-bp-app-refusal-line-is-one-line: that line holds no CR or LF, and it carries the application planner's reason field. Covered scope: the rendered octets; that host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-log writes them and one LF to the file run opened append-only is measured by tests/test_native_profile.py, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t6b-profile, 2026-09-22: the keystones have no hypotheses; tests/acl2/owner-log-tests.lisp evaluates each renderer on a real injected decision and a real control decision, and its must-fails name the weaker statements a host-word log would satisfy (the line echoes the host word; the control line uses the served classification) with the refuting owner evaluated beside each.

proofs.title: Bounded canonical BPv7 status-report payload codec
proofs.statement: For every fn-bpn-reportp payload, fn-bpn-report-decode of fn-bpn-report-encode returns that report and no trailing octets (fn-bpn-report-decode-of-encode); valid reports encode in at most 1194 octets (fn-bpn-report-encode-length-bound), below the decoder 4096-octet preflight, and every accepted input re-encodes byte-for-byte (fn-bpn-report-accepted-input-is-canonical). This covers RFC 9171 section 6.1.1 whole and fragment payloads, four assertions, optional requested times, and local reason codes 0 to 11. Reports are remote observations only; node-machine generation, correlation, consumption and release authority are outside this codec claim.
proofs.note: D1a codec source and its tests have ACL2 certification, including a maximal-profile witness and rejected malformed/noncanonical vectors. No native node path calls this codec yet. These component theorems are therefore not credited as requirement keystone events under the actual-caller rule; D1b/D2 generation and consumption remain open. The evidence records the component claims without implying a served implementation.

proofs.title: TCPCL final acknowledgement follows the durable delivery disposition
proofs.statement: The exact native fn-tcl-host-drive caller emits final END ACKs only immediately before matching :bundle-received events; at each such event, the ordered held messages satisfy fn-tcl-held-final-ackp. The host-called fn-tcl-delivery-plan then releases that ACK only for (:accepted path-or-nil), replaces it with XFER_REFUSE for definitive (:refused reason), and withholds it for (:uncertain reason). The source-level proof does not establish the physical FNBS barrier, raw Lisp execution, or socket delivery.
proofs.progress_note: ACL2 8.7 certified the exact host-drive event order, ordered held-list projection and conditional delivery plan. Reachable witnesses cover coalesced prior-transfer partial ACK/refusal, two completed bundles in one read, and missing-held/path-type counterexamples. Native source executes the selected message list; combined-image A2 callback runtime remains pending.

proofs.title: BP persisted age anchors are compared only within a durable boot domain
proofs.statement: The host-called fn-bpnf-clock-domain-plan returns :same only when a valid saved FNBS kind-6 frame decodes to the exact canonical current Linux boot ID; a different boot fences regardless of the numeric monotonic reading, and a missing marker with legacy obligations fences rather than renewing or expiring them. The 82-byte marker roundtrip and served guards are certified. The host's boot-ID observation, physical barriers, and combined-image caller still require native evidence, and cross-boot reanchoring remains open.
proofs.progress_note: The exact startup planner and canonical kind-6 marker are ACL2-owned, guard verified, and focused-book certified. Concrete witnesses include same-boot restart, both directions of incomparable new-boot uptime, legacy outbound and received rows, malformed marker, invalid observed ID, and a crash in the publisher link window. Native combined-image and physical clock/barrier evidence remain pending. A mismatched or legacy domain is an explicit lifecycle fence, not completed reboot recovery.

proofs.title: Native authored carrier receives the local NNTP injection trace without changing signed source
proofs.statement: For any nonnil result of the exact ACL2 fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets called by host/native/hybrid-control.lisp, fn-hsig-injected-carrier-retains-exact-signed-source proves the authenticated authored source is a suffix of the received octets, and fn-hsig-injected-carrier-is-a-news-injection proves the received octets satisfy the ordinary fn-inj-reinjectionp grammar for the rendered portable carrier, configured agent and projected Message-ID. The native event constructor accepts only the same injected bytes. This is an ACL2 byte-projection claim under a successful injection decision; it does not prove cryptographic primitives, filesystem durability, or peer I/O.
proofs.progress_note: The source-matched ACL2 book/test and dependent Store tests passed on hbox. The positive fixture constructs a real schema-1 injected event and replays its exact source; closed injection and pathless carrier witnesses fail the conclusions when the successful-injection premise is removed. The combined native two-owner peering/restart test awaits the shared image.

proofs.title: Exact-source topic metadata candidate is bounded and canonical
proofs.statement: The native topic-inspect-carrier command passes only the exact source returned after hybrid-carrier verification to fn-th-host-inspect-source. Successful inspection binds to exactly one FN-Topic field in that parsed source and its canonical raw physical lines. Every valid root, control, or report constructor encodes within 1,531 binary octets and 39 items; decoding its encoding recovers the constructor. The canonical folded field renderer emits lines of at most 85 octets. Accepted decoder bytes are canonical. This establishes no topic anchor or admission.
proofs.progress_note: ACL2 8.7 certified the codec, general constructor bound/inverse, host-called authored raw-line binding, canonical folded-field line bound, and max-profile/negative tests at exact digests on hbox. The full-envelope native saved-image max-profile gate remains pending; no topic admission claim is made.

proofs.title: Consumer projection equals the completed Store prefix through publication and crash replay
proofs.statement: Under fn-csi-full-relationp, the actual decoded Store dispatcher fn-snrt-step preserves the phase-aware relation for every event (fn-csi-store-step-preserves-full-relation). The relation equates the carried consumer projection with strict replay of the completed dense Store prefix, checks a linked unfinished candidate before finish, erases the process projection on crash, and reconstructs it from physical records on recovery. Induction over fn-snrt-run yields arbitrary finite mixed traces; a corrupted carried projection refutes the premise in the test book. This component covers logical Store transitions and admissible crash images, not a host-observed syscall refinement or served consumer call.
proofs.progress_note: The logical Store invariant and test roots are certified in scope. Native image 1d26e01f separately witnesses local-owner poll, advancing ACK/reopen, selected packing and fenced clone cursor recovery. Those tests do not prove syscall refinement or the consumer-owned transaction/ACK/reply join; general remote policy and two-store composition remain open. The current topic/consumer composition now certifies the actual :prepare-topic consumer-relation arm and a reachable bootstrap/register, topic admin/anchor/report, observed-reopen trace with ACK unchanged; the hbox source-matched scope is in planning/evidence/consumer-topic-store-trace-2026-09-24.md. This adds no served-path or physical durability claim.

proofs.title: Topic candidate author and root declaration bind to verified historical context
proofs.statement: The native topic inspector calls the ACL2 selector with exact source, principal and ordered keys returned by hybrid verification. A selected root is marked controller-matched only when its declared controller equals that principal and its declared keyset ID equals the ACL2 subject identity of the canonical principal/key snapshot. Reports obtain their author reference from that same verified context, not metadata or From. For a retained schema-1 event the historical selector first requires the T10 exact-source/carrier/keyring-snapshot binding; no topic admission or succession decision follows.
proofs.progress_note: The selector and accepted-event wrapper plus matching/mismatching principal, changed-key, From, relay and unbound historical event witnesses certify on hbox at the lane source. A source-matched saved-image CLI run and integrated reverse closure remain pending. The native command keeps generic candidate output and explicitly reports admission=unestablished.

proofs.title: Pinned group buckets and OVER ranges refine the committed archive
proofs.statement: For a projection-consistent accepted archive, fn-gidx-listgroup-command-of-build equates indexed LISTGROUP with the archive command. For an accepted archive, maintained bucket and trie correspondence, and an OVER or XOVER keyword, fn-nntp-carried-over-range-equals-archive-command equates the actual pinned archive dispatcher with the original response for every one-argument token; invalid ranges and untagged indexes fall through. fn-gidx-number-article-of-build proves that a bucket entry resolves through the trie to the same first article as the archive scan, including the identifier and number availability gates. For ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY and STAT and every argument list, fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned-msgid-arms-are-the-scan equates the same pinned dispatcher with the scanning archive dispatcher under the trie correspondence and no withdrawal hit (fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p and fn-nntp-msgid-withdrawn-p false: a withdrawn number or Message-ID answers 423/430 withdrawn, PRF-084). fn-own-read reaches that dispatcher through served dispatch; fn-own-relation and fn-served-connp maintain the pins across view refresh, open, feed and read. On a peer connection, fn-pix-history-hasp-is-peer-history-hasp equates the IHAVE/CHECK history test the host's carried read runs (one fn-midx-lookup in the owner view's trie when the session node holds the list the trie is keyed to) with the fn-peer-history-hasp scan for every Message-ID, under fn-node-statep and the trie correspondence; fn-oix-ocfg-step-keeps-view-indexed carries that correspondence over every configured-owner event. fn-pgc-peer-arm-is-peer-step-pinned equates the peer arm the carried read runs, which evaluates no fn-node-statep, with fn-peer-step-pinned under fn-peer-sessionp, a named peer and the trie correspondence. The claim excludes arbitrary tagged indexes, unindexed HDR/GROUP/NEXT/LAST/NEWNEWS, disk indexing, and elapsed-time performance.
proofs.progress_note: Scoped ACL2 certification and called-owner sparse/historical LISTGROUP witnesses are recorded in the group-bucket evidence. Indexed OVER/XOVER resolve selected-group bucket entries through the pinned trie; the called pinned dispatcher equality has direct reachable and malformed-state premise teeth, with redundant range, tag, bound and session assumptions removed. HDR remains on the archive fold. The native OVER/XOVER socket driver is prepared but has not run on a source-matched image; combined-image qualification and full dependent closure at integrated source remain open.

proofs.title: Experimental root-only topic admission is grounded in historical authorship and finite local policy
proofs.statement: The experimental root-only Store path selects prior T10-bound exact source and snapshot, checks installed local administrator, roster, same-topic parents and finite quota, and completes only a matching topic event. Fresh version-2 root anchors bind the exact earlier immutable administrator-install event ID and generation; historical version-1 anchors retain ID-only replay semantics and cannot be freshly staged. The owner-called report selector returns :replayed-historical only for selected earlier exact source and retained admission, without another Store event. Topic completion advances the exact Store sequence/transaction and slot-12 projection while preserving article acceptance. Observed reopen separately validates topic replay; deriving that validity for every modeled crash image from a maintained live Store relation remains open. Native v2 migration and physical publication are not yet qualified.
proofs.progress_note: Scoped v2 local proposal, Store fresh-v1 refusal, canonical event/prefix and mixed-source vector roots passed at exact bytes. Historical v1 meaning is retained. The dual-image native migration test is prepared but has not run; a v2 saved image and full affected closure remain open. The maintained topic/crash relation is under separate active proof work and is not supplied by the interim BP/byte reopen premise.

proofs.title: Local consumer status reports the scoped committed journal distance
