proofs.statement: The experimental local-owner command `consumer status CONTROL ID` reports the registered consumer ACK, committed journal frontier and their event-distance from fixed committed Store projections after the same local principal, query-version and view-version scope checks used by position and poll. The diagnostic leaves owner state unchanged. For the exact host-called kind-9 FNCT codec, decoding an encoded accepted reply returns its ACK, frontier and gap when ACK and frontier are uint32 values, ACK is no greater than frontier, and gap equals frontier minus ACK; decoding an encoded refused, uncertain or fault reply returns that status with empty fields under the constrained frame-digest shape. This target remains in progress because the subsequent topic/index composition requires its own native qualification. The codec theorem does not prove concrete hash security, native filesystem recovery or article unreadness/application processing; Store recovery authority remains PRF-064.
proofs.progress_note: The ACL2 local status codec, owner scope decision and native-control host test passed the scoped status/index run. The general accepted and nonaccepted kind-9 codec roundtrips and their isolating teeth certified in the selected hbox book/test roots at the exact new source bytes; these are proof-only changes to the executable codec. The earlier e160442f image passed unknown-consumer refusal, read-only status, advancing ACK and recovered status checks. The joined topic/index source has scoped certification but has not yet run on a matching saved image. The diagnostic does not assert application processing or discharge.

proofs.title: Operator-local hybrid key lifecycle preserves per-principal authority and historical verdicts
proofs.statement: The host-called local enrollment and revocation constructors require the next durable keyring generation; new hybrid-author requests use only the named principal's newest recognized enrollment, leaving unrelated principals active, while identity replay retains earlier snapshots and accepted verdicts byte-exact across rotation and revocation.
proofs.progress_note: The per-principal selector, next-generation event constructors and versioned tombstone are implemented. Completed kind-3 Store-node theorems equate the post-finish selector to identity replay and preserve historical verdicts; successful recovery theorems equate the carried selector and verdicts to replay of recovered durable records. A reachable Store trace commits A1 and a kind-4 verdict, then B2, A3 rotation and A4 tombstone, checking maintained node/file and identity-sequence relations and observed reopen. Selected crash cuts before and after B2 publication distinguish absent from durable enrollment. The host calls the selector under the serialized owner. The frozen 863c2141 production image passed three targeted native lifecycle/carrier tests on scratch Stores with OpenSSL 3.5.8. A global crash-phase relation for every lifecycle trace, incoming signed-carrier authority caller, and cost/index correspondence for a large snapshot history remain open. Local permission does not define portable succession or retroactive signature invalidation.

proofs.title: The POST outcome at the wire keeps its three outcomes and names its refusal
proofs.statement: fn-own-consumed-completion-is-240-or-uncertain: over fn-own-outcome (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-outcome), once a completion has been consumed into the ledger after the connection's submission was taken, the reply is the 240 for the host word :durable and the uncertain `441 ... do not repost' for every other word, so a durable record is never answered as a refusal. fn-post-outcome-store-refusal-kinds-are-distinct and fn-post-outcome-store-refusal-is-not-uncertain: over fn-nntp-post-outcome, each Store refusal kind (duplicate, conflict, malformed, unaffordable, storage-failed, unnamed) is its own 441 line and none is the uncertain line. D25, over fn-own-outcome with the word fn-pb-existing-action returns (books/poster-bytes.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt), keyed on the poster's source recovered by the injection inverse fn-inj-source-of (books/injection.lisp; fn-inj-source-of-inverts-the-injection: every injected article gives back its source exactly, at every clock reading, in all four generated-field cases): fn-pb-a-resend-at-any-clock-is-answered-already-stored, the held article is a source injected at clock A and the submission is that source injected at clock B under the same Message-ID and groups, with the Date present or absent, and the reply is `441 posting failed; this article is already stored here' while no completion has been consumed; fn-pb-a-changed-source-is-answered-conflict, any other source under that Message-ID (one changed authored byte, an authored Date changed or removed) is answered the conflict line; fn-pb-an-existing-action-writes-nothing, whatever fn-pb-existing-action answers, the outcome leaves the owner's Store, its feeds and its outcome records as they were. RFC 5537 section 3.5 item 11 over fn-inj-decide, one theorem per case: fn-inj-no-injection-date-when-date-and-message-id-are-supplied (the injected article is the Path line, the Injection-Info line and the source, at every clock reading), fn-inj-injection-date-is-the-clock-otherwise, and fn-inj-a-supplied-injection-date-is-never-replaced (a local acceptance policy refuses such a proto-article).
proofs.note: Lane p2-wire, from the campaign's W1/W2/W3 (planning/evidence/campaign-1a9dd747-2026-09-24.md). The refusal kind is relayed by the host from the ACL2 step that refused (fn-pb-existing-action since D25, fn-owner-prepare, fn-store-publication-admissibility, fn-owner-known-abort); the capacity comparison against max-transactions is still a host computation. The durable word of a POST commit is fn-ccar-own-finish's (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission), equal to fn-own-finish by fn-ccar-own-finish-is-own-finish. The refusal words are a local policy choice pending ember's decision. D25 (lanes d25-dup-conflict, then d25-injection-inverse): the duplicate-versus-conflict decision is fn-pb-existing-action; since lane d25-injection-inverse its subject is the poster's source through the injection inverse, not a projection that drops named fields, so no scope limit on an opening Date remains for records of injection recipe v2. The provenance of generated fields is carried by the injected block itself (recipe v2: Path, then Injection-Date, generated Message-ID, generated Date, then Injection-Info closing the block); no Store record field was added. Recipe v1 records are read under v1 only where unambiguous (fn-inj-source-of-a-v1-record) and otherwise compared octet for octet (fn-inj-source-of-an-ambiguous-v1-record). A relayed article, or one another agent injected, is compared octet for octet, so a transit copy whose Path differs is again a conflict (as before D25). The supplied-Injection-Date refusal is a local acceptance policy, not an RFC requirement. It refines fn-sn-existing-action (fn-pb-existing-action-refines-the-byte-identity-decision).

proofs.title: Group names are the RFC 5536 section 3.1.4 grammar and reserved names are never created
proofs.statement: fn-record-group-namep-is-the-rfc-5536-grammar: the recognizer every host site applies admits exactly an ASCII string of 1 to 128 octets (local bound) whose octets are an RFC 5536 section 3.1.4 <newsgroup-name>; four rejection theorems name a forbidden octet, a leading dot, an empty component and a trailing dot. fn-native-admin-plan-refuses-a-reserved-group-create: a well-formed `group create NAME` whose NAME is reserved (first component "example" or the name "poster", ASCII case folded) is refused :reserved-group-name and carries no configuration delta; the subject is fn-native-admin-plan, which host/native-admin-host.lisp:7 calls. fn-native-operator-run-refuses-a-reserved-init-group: an `init` naming a reserved group in any position is never an accepted plan; the subject is fn-native-operator-run, which host/native-operator-host.lisp:19 calls, and host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-dispatch-plan exits on a non-accepted plan before any store observation. fn-native-admin-group-name-creatablep-is-the-rfc-5536-rule: a creatable name is a valid group name whose case-folded octets are not "example", do not begin "example.", and are not "poster". Covered scope: the operator and admin command paths; the initial configuration record's refusal in fn-cfg-host-initial-octets (program mode) is witnessed, not proved. fn-native-admin-plan-create-ignores-special-purpose: for every creatable name, including RFC 5536 section 3.1.4's specific-purpose names (fn-native-admin-group-name-special-purposep: a first or only component "to" or "control", any component "all" or "ctl", exactly "junk", case folded), a well-formed `group create NAME` plans exactly the accepted :create-group of the typed name with no capacity, rows or policy, so no plan field derives from the special-purpose class.
proofs.progress_note: Lanes group-name-validity (grammar, 2026-09-24) and group-names-2 (reserved names, 2026-09-24). Teeth: records-shape-tests has the grammar witnesses and seven must-fails; native-admin-tests and native-operator-tests have the reserved witnesses (example, example.test, Example.a, EXAMPLE.test, poster, POSTER, Poster refused; fn.example, examples.test, poster.x, fn.poster accepted; retire of example.test accepted) and one must-fail per hypothesis. fn-record-group-namep-bounds-length-by-definition is the local bound by definition and is not cited. Lane defaults-precise (2026-09-24): specific-purpose recognizer and the local-agreement theorem; teeth in native-admin-tests (15 special witnesses, 12 near misses, the plan witness over five special names and one ordinary, one must-fail per hypothesis). persvati run-20260924T230642Z-0e1b.

proofs.title: Offline store-profile upgrade: the operator's fields (format 8), only non-shrinking upgrades, every gate monotone, old or new at every crash cut
proofs.statement: The store profile is the operator's (D27): format fn-store-8, twelve fields validated by fn-bs-profile-validp (1 <= T <= 2^32-1; R <= H; R at least every Store event kind's publication ceiling; R, A, G and the group-name bound within their codec ceilings; 1 <= K <= T; each namespace count in 1..2^32-1), with a format-7 tuple run under its translation fn-bs-profile-of. fn-bs-profile-validp-codecs-accept: every field of the profile a store runs under is within its codec, and when admitted R covers every kind. fn-profile-upgradep OLD NEW holds when OLD is admitted, NEW is a valid profile, NEW is not OLD, and none of the twelve fields is smaller; fn-profile-upgrade-format-7-to-8: a format-7 tuple upgrades to its translation with every kind's budget unchanged, and the verb with no field writes exactly that. Monotone gates, over the functions the host calls at open and publication: fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-txn-observation (fn-profile-txn-observation with the profile's max_transactions, host/native/io.lisp fnn-transaction-files), fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-replay-bound (fn-profile-replay-within-boundp with max_history_octets, per record from fnn-durable-records), fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-publication-admissibility (fn-bs-publication-admissiblep, fnn-publish) and fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-verdict (fn-sbud-verdict: the count gate and the history-octet gate, fn-sbud-verdict-is-the-count-and-history-admissibility). Replay takes no profile argument, so an admitted store replays to the same state. fn-profile-upgrade-verdict-writes-only-upgrades: an :upgrade verdict of the function fnn-command-upgrade-profile calls (through fn-store-profile-upgrade-verdict) carries octets that decode to the requested profile, an upgrade of the store's (under A-CRYPTO, fn-bs-config-decode-of-encode, now over every valid profile); fn-profile-upgrade-budget-after-reopen: the next open's budget is the requested profile's. fn-bs-profile-program-crash-is-old-or-new: for the byte program fnn-upgrade-profile-write runs, from a store with nothing pending, every crash image of every cut of the successful run names the old inode with its old content or the new inode with exactly the staged octets; -crash-budget-is-old-or-new gives the old or the new budget. Covered scope: the successful run and its crash images; syscall error arms are classified by the host and witnessed natively, not modelled. The owner's history gate uses a carried record-octet sum equal to the kernel's when the cache is a prefix sum (fn-sbud-bytes-used-is-kernel-sum); the host resets it at profile install and relies on committed records growing append-only within one owner process, which is stated, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane m5-profile-upgrade (2026-09-24). Teeth in tests/acl2/store-profile-upgrade-tests.lisp: the relation over the four named profiles (two pairs), the verdict's five answers, 129 and 200 transaction names, the 24 MiB replay bound, 128 and 200 used, a reachable byte run whose rename cut has both images, and one must-fail per keystone hypothesis at constants (including a store with a pending write to config.json's inode and a step list that renames an unfenced stage). Native, developer image of 05b96703 on hbox: three articles, upgrade, budget 4096 with 3 used, the fourth POST accepted; same profile and downgrade refused through both entries; a held writer lock refuses; the five PROFILE_CUTS cuts x kill/eio x operator/store entries (20 cases) reopen with the old or the new frame byte for byte, with the candidate column's budget. Open: the checkpoint pack coverage (fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-coverage with field 4) is not in the monotone set; fn-store-txn-prefix-reclaim-plan kept its own copy of the namespace bound (that function is no longer in the tree at 17ff24aa; PKT-120). Lane bounds-p1-profile (2026-09-25, D27): the profile became the operator's twelve fields in format fn-store-8 with relations, not tables; init and store upgrade-profile take --FIELD N over a preset or the current profile; the upgrade is any valid non-shrinking profile, including the format 7 to 8 step; status prints every field and bytes-used/history-bound. Every keystone above restated by name over every valid profile; new: fn-bs-profile-validp-codecs-accept, fn-sbud-bytes-used-is-kernel-sum, fn-sbud-verdict-is-the-count-and-history-admissibility, fn-profile-upgrade-format-7-to-8. Native on hbox, images of 73ccdaa7 (planning/evidence/bounds-p1-2026-09-25.md): init with custom fields; P-1/P/P+1 octets against A = 20000 (accepted, accepted, refused `payload exceeds the modelled bound`); raise and shrink-by-name; 7 to 8 on a fresh format-7 scale store written by the c3420013 image, and its 20 cut cases old-or-new byte for byte. Format 6 is no longer opened. Open: R has one valid value (196608) until P2 raises the FNST ceiling; the article-record relation uses the kind table's figure until P2's fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling merges; under T > 4096 compaction's one-unit pack can refuse (fn-cverb-preset-count-within-pack-events, P5).

proofs.title: Transaction-prefix reclaim keeps the reconstructed history, over the functions the reclaim and the next open call
proofs.statement: Let NAMES be the transaction namespace the reclaim observed, LOWER the selected pack's boundary (fn-ccp-framed-boundary, the value fn-ccp-coverage-framed returns to host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-pack-lower-bound), and GONE any subset of fn-bs-pack-reclaim-plan NAMES MAXIMUM LOWER (the names fnn-pack-prefix-reclaim unlinks; every process-death image of its program deletes such a subset). fn-ccp-reclaim-keeps-namespace-observation: if fn-profile-txn-observation NAMES MAXIMUM LOWER (the open gate host/native/io.lisp fnn-transaction-files calls through fn-store-txn-observation-selected) is valid, then on NAMES without GONE it is valid and equals the old observation with exactly GONE's pairs left out. fn-ccp-covered-deletion-keeps-reconstruction: when fn-ccp-observe-framed (the body of host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe, called by fnn-pack-recover-records inside fnn-recover) answers :ok on an observation, it answers identically on any sub-observation that leaves out only pairs below the pack boundary. fn-ccp-reclaim-preserves-reconstructed-history composes the two over the host's read of each issued pair: if the open before the reclaim reconstructed its history, the open after the reclaim (at any cut) observes a valid namespace and hands the generic replay the identical record list. fn-ccp-complete-observation-reconstructs-its-records: for a complete contiguous observation from 0 at least as long as the boundary, that list is exactly the records read, which is what the same open handed replay before any pack existed. Hypotheses: the pre-reclaim open succeeded (the reclaim command runs only after its own fnn-open-live-store), LOWER is the selected pack's boundary, and the bytes of every surviving name are unchanged (for the uncovered suffix, fn-bs-selected-reclaim-crash-preserves-suffix-payload in the byte model; the reclaim program writes no file content). Replay is a function of the record list, the frontier and the configuration records, and the reclaim program touches neither the frontier nor config.json, so GROUP counts and watermarks, ARTICLE by number and by Message-ID, HDR, retention pins and every other replayed fact are unchanged; that last step is by definition, not a theorem. One owner: fn-bs-pack-reclaim-plan reads fn-profile-txn-observation (no inline bound), and fn-ccp-profile-upgrade-keeps-reclaim-plan gives its monotonicity under an offline profile upgrade.
proofs.progress_note: Lane m5-compaction (2026-09-24). Certified on persvati (run-20260924T213519Z-7956, manifest certify-20260924T213534Z-827010, ACL2 8.7, every book under 4 s) and on hbox with the w28 toolchain. Teeth: a reachable five-event store (record, undertaking, release, identity, enrollment) whose open before, after losing covered names 1 and 3, and after the whole plan reconstructs the same five records; concrete counterexamples and a must-fail for each composition hypothesis (a suffix gap; losing the newest suffix name, which the gate accepts and which silently drops record 4; a plan computed above the pack boundary, same loss; a conflicting surviving covered file, refused before and accepted after). Native, developer image of this branch on hbox: six operator POSTs around a selected pack, then reclaim and every reclaim cut (each covered unlink occurrence and the directory barrier); GROUP, ARTICLE by number and by Message-ID, HDR Subject and store retention are identical, the suffix files byte-identical, and the next POST gets high+1. Open: the byte model states survival for the uncovered suffix only, not old-or-absent for a covered name; guards of the framed observe stay unverified (the Store-event decoder chain); one pack holds at most 4096 events and 4 MiB, so the exact-history pack cannot compact an arbitrarily large store; no operator entry reaches reclaim (developer `checkpoint` verb only). Lane m5-compact-verb (2026-09-24): the operator entry `operator CONFIG store compact` (fn-cverb-decide decides pack+select+reclaim+retire, resume, or a named refusal; the host carries out exactly those steps). fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-profile-budget: when the decision packs, every file present plus the pack the host seals from the same records fits the profile's aggregate bound (field 3); fn-cverb-pack-decision-capture-succeeds: a pack decision on an exact event history below a uint32 frontier is never refused by the capture; the operator argv reaches :compact exactly for `store compact` (two native-operator theorems). The 4 MiB pack is kept as the compaction unit (refused by name above it; the 4096-event limit never binds, fn-cverb-profile-count-within-pack-events). Native on images of 5181e0ea: the ten CHECKPOINT_CUTS (now including the two retire cuts) pass through the developer checkpoint verbs and the operator verb, 20/20; the production image compacts, rereads every article identically and posts at high+1. Finding 3 of m5-compaction is not detectable from the open's observation: the frontier is reserved before the record, so a lost newest file equals an abandoned reservation (fn-cverb-open-history-gate-admits-a-lost-suffix); a post-commit witness is a decision for ember. Lane bounds-p1-profile (2026-09-25): fn-cverb-profile-count-within-pack-events is renamed fn-cverb-preset-count-within-pack-events and holds for the presets only; under an operator profile with max_transactions above 4096 (the D27 default is 2^32-1) the 4096-event pack limit can refuse compaction by name (:exceeds-compaction-unit) until chained packs (P5).

proofs.title: LIST COUNTS is the archive's exact count from the pinned buckets; a Message-ID retrieval's number names the same article
proofs.statement: For a projection archive and the group buckets the owner carries (the build of its articles), fn-gidx-list-counts-command-is-the-archive-fold equates the served LIST COUNTS reply, read from the pinned buckets, with the archive fold fn-nntp-list-counts-command, for every argument list; fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned-list-counts states it at the pinned dispatcher; fn-nntp-group-count-is-listgroup-length makes the count field the length of LISTGROUP's number list for the group, with no hypothesis; fn-gidx-counts-work-of-build-bound bounds the reply's bucket work by G*B + M for G distinct listed groups, B buckets and M memberships (linear per group in B plus its own entries, each visited a constant number of passes; an empty group adds one lookup in the next-number table). For ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY and STAT with a Message-ID the number is fn-nntp-msgid-local-number: the article's available number in the selected group, else 0 (RFC 3977 section 6.2.1.2); under fn-statep (fresh local numbers) fn-nntp-msgid-number-retrieves-the-same-article shows a positive number, sent back as any number token reading as it, retrieves the same article in the same group, the section's second-ARTICLE clause. fn-served-step-list-counts-is-the-archive-counts and fn-served-step-msgid-retrieval-carries-the-local-number carry both to fn-served-step, which fn-own-read runs (fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk), under the trie and bucket relations fn-own-relation carries and one framed command line. Excluded: HDR/XHDR/GROUP/NEXT/LAST, which still fold the archive; elapsed-time performance.

proofs.title: D23 relay trust: carriage, authorship and release authority are separate questions over the functions bp-node calls
proofs.statement: fn-bpaj-carried-source-decision CFG P G SOURCE (books/bp-session-admission.lisp) is the one decision for a delivered bundle: :direct when SOURCE is the delivering neighbour P's own enrolled EID; :carried P A when P's boundary has a (P "bp-boundary-carries" SOURCE 0) row and A is the unique boundary directly enrolled with transport-bp SOURCE; else refused with :generation, :source-not-carried or :carried-source-unenrolled. fn-bpaj-carried-decision-is-the-authors-direct-decision: a carried decision names an author whose own delivery of SOURCE at the same generation is decided :direct under A. fn-bpaj-carried-request-is-judged-as-the-authors-direct-request: for a carried view and a view identical except that its CL ingress names A at the same generation, fn-bpah-request-trustedp (host/bp-native-app-host.lisp, called by host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-request-result) answers the same and fn-bpaj-transit-plan (called by fn-owner-app-plan-install) returns the same plan. fn-bpaj-unlisted-carried-request-is-refused: when P's boundary has neither a transport-bp nor a carries row for SOURCE, the request check does not trust the view and the plan is (:refused :no-principal). fn-bpaj-carried-unenrolled-request-is-refused: for a CL ingress at the current generation of a well-formed configuration whose neighbour carries SOURCE while no row enrols SOURCE as a transport-bp EID, the decision is (:refused :carried-source-unenrolled), the request check does not trust it and the plan is refused. Release authority (books/bp-release-authority.lisp, host-called as fn-bpah-receipt-release-record through fn-owner-bp-receipt-release-record by fnn-bpnode-receipt-result, which publishes only the record it returns): fn-bpah-unauthorized-issuer-releases-nothing: for a bare (unsigned) receipt whose issuer is neither the delivering neighbour's own enrolled EID nor on its (NAME "bp-boundary-releases-for" EID 0) list, the host's gate fn-bpah-receipt-gatep is false and the release record is nil. fn-bpah-carrier-without-release-row-releases-nothing: the same for a bare receipt when the neighbour's boundary has no transport-bp and no releases-for row for the issuer, with no hypothesis about its carries rows. fn-bpah-released-receipt-names-exactly-its-obligation: a non-nil record implies the receipt is authorized (a signed receipt by fn-bpah-receipt-signature-verifiedp, a bare one by fn-bpah-release-issuer-authorizedp), the work the receipt's work id finds is outstanding and satisfies fn-bp-authorized-receiptp, the record's work id is that work's, and fn-bprl-apply-journal-record admits it. fn-bpah-receipt-naming-other-terms-releases-nothing: a receipt whose work id finds no outstanding work, or whose subject, policy or terms differ from that work's, gives nil. Signed receipts (books/bp-signed-receipt.lisp frame; preimage fn-bpsr-signed-preimage, the article scheme's fn-hsig-subject-body under the tag fn-bp-receipt-hybrid-v1 over the requester EID and the exact receipt ADU; host observations by fnn-hsig-observe-raw, the verdict fn-hsig-authorize; A-CRYPTO): fn-bpah-signed-receipt-releases-through-any-carrier: for a signed receipt of the delivered shape whose signature verifies under the issuer's own enrollment at this node (the unique boundary directly enrolled for the issuer EID names the principal in a bp-boundary-receipt-signer row, and this Store's current keyring snapshot for the principal gives the keys), the release record is fn-bprl-receipt-auto-record of the carried ADU with authorization equal to fn-bpah-receipt-names-obligationp; no hypothesis mentions the delivering neighbour's rows. fn-bpah-unverified-signed-receipt-releases-nothing: a signed receipt whose signature does not verify gives a false gate and a nil record whoever delivered it. fn-bpah-receipt-signature-needs-both-observations: verification implies both primitive observations are :verified and the signer row is the issuer's own. fn-bpah-trusted-bare-receipt-releases: for a bare receipt the gate trusts on a carrier without require-signed-receipts, the record is the workflow's answer with authorization equal to the obligation check (a listed relay's forgery naming the exact obligation releases: the delegation profile). fn-bpah-required-signature-refuses-bare-receipts: under (NAME "bp-boundary-require-signed-receipts" "yes" 0) on the delivering neighbour a bare receipt gives a false gate and a nil record. fn-bpah-request-trust-ignores-release-rows and fn-bpaj-source-decision-ignores-release-rows: two configurations at one generation, equally well-formed, that agree after dropping releases-for rows make the same source decision and trust the same requests.
proofs.progress_note: Lane d23-issuer-authority (2026-09-24): receipts release only under the release list and the exact obligation; certified on hbox w28 run-20260924T231033Z-cfaf (manifest certify-20260924T231054Z-2148356, 94 books, the affected sets of bp-session-admission and native-admin) and run-20260924T232022Z-575d (certify-20260924T232040Z-2181356, 20 books, bp-release-authority and native-admin after the cost fix; every book under 10 s). Lab: planning/evidence/d23-issuer-authority-2026-09-24.md. Lane d23-bp-carrier (2026-09-24). Certified on hbox with the w28 toolchain: run-20260924T222039Z-5919 (manifest certify-20260924T222100Z-2041510, 85 books, the affected set of bp-session-admission, native-admin and native-operator, every book under 9 s); bp-session-admission and its tests in certify-20260924T221731Z-2038126. Lab: through dtn7-rs with one and two relays the request is accepted under the author's enrollment and the receipt is accepted at home (planning/evidence/d23-bp-carrier-2026-09-24.md). The bp-boundary verb takes `carries EID ...'; its rows ride the :set-peer delta, the configuration record round-trips and replay recovers them (ground witness in native-admin-tests). Teeth: one must-fail per hypothesis of each theorem and reachable witnesses in bp-transit-join-tests (a relay carrying dtn://b/ with dtnB enrolled plans the same :submit under dtnB), bp-session-admission-tests and bp-app-handoff-tests (a relayed receipt). Open: bp-node serve's own forwarding still expects the application peer as its TCPCL neighbour (a routing choice, not this rule); verification of a signed article against the author's enrollment is the posting path's.

proofs.title: M5 committed-history boundary: no reachable history is refused, a lost suffix containing an acknowledged or resolved record is refused by name, and a required store refuses an absent marker
proofs.statement: Over the host-called decisions fn-hm-after-commit (what the marker holds after the record of SEQUENCE: the FNSM kind-3 frame of SEQUENCE+1, host/native/io.lisp fnn-mark-committed) and fn-hm-open-verdict (the open's check, io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker called by fnn-recover with the reconstructed record count), and the history step fn-hm-step: burned reservations, uncertain publications that did or did not survive, and commits whose marker program crashed at any cut, with a crash table in which the marker is old before the rename, old or new after it, and new after the root barrier. fn-hm-run-keeps-every-open-admitted: from an admitted state, every such history with its count within uint32 is admitted. fn-hm-open-refuses-a-lost-acknowledged-record: after a commit whose marker program completed at a natural count C, followed by any history within uint32, an open that observes K <= C records is (:refused :history-short-of-marker M), where M is the marker's count. fn-hm-decode-of-encode: the marker codec round-trips every uint32. D31 (books/store-history-required.lisp), over the host-called decisions fn-hmr-open-verdict and fn-hmr-catch-up (io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker, the catch-up written by fnn-recover through fnn-mark-committed) and fn-hmr-upgrade-verdict (io.lisp fnn-command-upgrade-profile), and the history step fn-hmr-step over (D marker A profile live): burns, uncertain publications, commits in a live process crashed at any marker cut or finished (A covers the record), opens whose catch-up crashed at any cut or completed (live only then), resolutions of a held record in a live process (A covers it), and migrations whose profile crash image is old or new. fn-hmr-step-preserves-the-invariant (the model lemma the next rests on; not a registry event): the open admits, A <= M, and a live process's marker counts D. fn-hmr-open-refuses-below-every-answered-record: after any history from an invariant state, an open observing K < A records (K natural) is (:refused :history-short-of-marker M). fn-hmr-required-store-never-admits-an-absent-marker: from a required profile, after any history, an absent marker at any natural count is (:refused :marker-missing). fn-hmr-requirement-follows-a-covering-marker: a step that makes an unmarked profile required is a migration in a live process over a marker counting D, and leaves the marker. fn-hmr-legacy-store-migrates-by-the-two-step: from an unmarked store no process holds, two steps reach required only as an open (the catch-up) then a migration, over the covering marker.
proofs.progress_note: Lane m5-history-lifetimes (2026-09-24). Certified on persvati (run-20260924T230612Z-64bc, manifest certify-20260924T230629Z-1648710, ACL2 8.7 w25, book 2.5 s, tests 2.2 s; at 72d40647, run-20260924T232158Z-fa11, manifest certify-20260924T232218Z-1792716, book 2.6 s, tests 2.3 s). Teeth: a reachable seven-step history (commit, burn, commit crashed after rename with the old marker, surviving uncertain record, commit, burn, lost uncertain) that is admitted, refuses a lost newest record by name, and admits the same history after further burns. For every hypothesis of both keystones, a concrete instance where the others hold and the conclusion is false. Open: the crash table is not a program of the fn-bs byte model; an absent marker is admitted; an unacknowledged survivor above the marker is not covered.

proofs.title: The native request is the workflow's request for exactly that work, over the plan bp-obligation request executes
proofs.statement: fn-bprq-plan S WORK ATTEMPT (books/bp-request-plan.lisp), called by host/workflow-host.lisp fn-workflow-request-plan, which host/native/bp-obligation.lisp fnn-bpo-request-publish calls, returns nil or (:request ATTEMPT-RECORD OUTCOME KEY ADU DESTINATION RETRY). fn-bprq-plan-is-the-works-request: whenever it returns a plan, the attempt record is an :attempt naming exactly WORK and ATTEMPT, KEY (the FNBS job key the host enqueues under) is (WORK ATTEMPT generation) with the attempt's generation, ADU decodes exactly (fn-bpa-decode-exact) to fn-bpa-make-request over the work WORK holds in the image reached by publishing RETRY (if any), the attempt and its durable outcome (fn-bprq-published-state), that request is fn-bpa-requestp with work id WORK, and DESTINATION is that work's peer EID. Hypothesis: the plan exists. The published image is the host's: fn-bpiw-apply on these records is fn-bprl-apply-journal-record (reachable witness in the test book, not a general theorem). ION is an adapter: fn-bpiw-attempt-record-is-the-generic-attempt (test book) equates the ION constructor with fn-bprq-attempt-record, which host/workflow-host.lisp fn-workflow-ion-attempt-record now calls. Not claimed: that the image's work fields equal those before the attempt (they are stated over the published image), any transport or receipt property, or recovery of a fenced attempt.
proofs.progress_note: Lane m4-native-request (2026-09-24). Certified on hbox, w28 ACL2 8.7, 2 jobs: run-20260924T230759Z-4d2f (manifest certify-20260924T230813Z-2144048, bp-request-plan 7.6 s, tests 1.9 s) at the source of commit 41799aaf; the first run (certify-20260924T230223Z-2118502) certified the plan before the retry-request clause. Teeth: reachable witness over the committed-article image of bp-outbound-tests (the plan's attempt and ADU are the hand trace's exact record and octets); must-fail at the refusal witness for the one hypothesis; refusals for an in-flight attempt, a pending image, a fenced image and a work bound to no article (where the attempt alone would be admitted); a restart-observed work planned with its :retry-request replays through fn-bpiw-replay-journal while the same history without it is refused. Status stays in-progress: the lab evidence is on a scratch DTN developer image, and the recovery of an attempt fenced by a cut between the attempt and its outcome has no native verb.

proofs.title: A control article is filed only in control.<verb>, or refused, over the filing plan every ingress calls
proofs.statement: fn-ctl-control-article-is-filed-only-in-control: for every received octet string that fn-ctl-classify-octets classifies (:control VERB ARGS), fn-pa-filing-plan RECEIVED GROUPS DOMAIN (books/peer-authored-accept.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-control-filing calls it and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit calls that first, for served POST, bound submission, NNTP transit and BP transit, and host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author calls fn-owner-control-filing itself for the local signed-author path) either files the article in exactly one group, its filing group fn-ctl-filing-group VERB, which is "control" or begins "control." and is a member of DOMAIN, or refuses it :control-not-filed; the ingress's own GROUPS (the names its Newsgroups field gave) are never the answer unless they are that group. fn-ctl-classify-reads-only-the-control-field: inserting any field F whose name is neither control nor supersedes anywhere in a field list leaves fn-ctl-classify-fields unchanged. fn-ctl-cmsg-subject-is-ordinary: an article whose parsed fields have no Control field is filed in GROUPS unchanged by fn-pa-filing-plan, whatever its Subject, Newsgroups or Also-Control. Covered scope: the filing decision; the host's use of the filed groups is a transcribed stub test (tests/native_peer_authored_accept_raw.lisp) and the native cases of the evidence file. A signed control article is filed the same way (the :control-signed refusal was removed 2026-09-25 by lane control-c3 when the signed record binding came to name the filing group; PRF-084).
proofs.progress_note: Lane control-c1 (2026-09-25), packet C1 of planning/design-2026-09-25-control-messages.md. Teeth in tests/acl2/control-tests.lisp: reachable witnesses (a cancel naming fn.test with control.cancel configured is filed in control.cancel; without it, refused; a cmsg Subject article and a .ctl/Also-Control article keep fn.test), must-fail per hypothesis (an ordinary article is filed outside control; a Control field or a Supersedes field inserted changes the classification; a signed control article is not filed). 2026-09-25 (control-c3): the signed record binding names the filing group, so a signed control article is filed; fn-ctl-unsigned-control-filing-by-definition became fn-ctl-control-filing-by-definition without its carrier hypothesis.

proofs.title: A held bundle is offered only to the routed hop, over the step the host calls; unrouted bundles stay held and are reported; the decision is deterministic in the table
proofs.statement: fn-bpnp-step-offers-only-the-routed-hop: for a routed :session event (:session PEER S t MRU OBS (:via HOP ANNOUNCED TABLE)) to fn-bpnp-step (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step, from host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-forward-session), a :persist-attempt effect is for the row the arrival-order scan chose, and fn-bprt-next-hop of that row's own destination EID text over TABLE and live set (HOP) is HOP, the route fn-bprt-hop-route is a member of TABLE whose pattern matches the destination and whose boundary is HOP, and ANNOUNCED is the octets of that route's enrolled EID. fn-bpnp-step-unrouted-bundle-stays-held-and-is-reported: if the issued operation is not uncertain, no row the table routes to HOP is ready, the scan over every held row is ready and no route in TABLE matches that row's destination, the step's only effect is (:forward-no-route ARRIVAL HOP :no-route) and the held list is unchanged. fn-bprt-next-hop-deterministic-in-the-table: two tables whose routes matching DEST are the same set give DEST the same answer. fn-bprt-next-hop-names-a-live-matching-route: a boundary answer is the boundary of a live matching route in the table. Covered scope: the 7-field routed :session arm and the :resume arm with VIA scan only the rows the table routes to HOP (PRF-103); a :session open or :resume without VIA offers nothing; LIVE is the single session's hop.
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-routing (2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-route-tests.lisp: a reachable witness (the bp-node-forward-retry fixture's held transit to dtn://bp-dest/, routed to relay, proposes the attempt) and must-fail cases for an unlisted hop, a wrong announced EID, a prefix route to another boundary, the route present (no report), and tables whose matching sets differ.

proofs.title: Bounds join: an article the profile admits is a record it publishes; the group-name ceiling is the label width; a refused operator article names the profile bound
proofs.statement: fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record (books/byte-store-frame.lisp): under a profile a store runs under (fn-bs-profile-admittedp), every record whose payload is at most the article field A and whose group count is at most G encodes (fn-record-encode) to at most the record field R; it rests on fn-record-encode-length-bound and the validity relation R >= fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling A G (:max-record-octets-below-the-article-record in fn-bs-profile-validp, which the host calls through fn-bs-profile-init-verdict, host/store-host.lisp:385, fn-profile-upgrade-verdict, :429, and fn-bs-profile-admittedp at install, host/owner-host.lisp:219). The format-7 translation takes G and the group name at the codec ceilings and R as the larger of H/T and the article record of (A, G). fn-cfg-labelp-of-record-group-name (books/config.lisp): every group name the record codec admits is a configuration label, the one statement relating *fn-record-max-group-name* and *fn-cfg-max-label*. fn-native-control-refusal-status-is-a-refusal (books/native-control.lisp): the control word for a refused operator submission (:article-exceeds-profile-bound for the injection reason :oversize, else :refused) is in the FNCT reply vocabulary and of class refused; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized calls it through fn-native-control-host-refusal-status. Covered scope: record encodings under a valid profile; the frame :blob width (131,072) and the owner's per-octet recursion at take are not covered.
proofs.progress_note: Lane bounds-join (2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/byte-store-frame-tests.lisp: a tight witness (R equal to the article record of its (A, G)); one refusal by name per argument of the relation; a concrete counterexample per hypothesis (a non-profile reads R = 0 while an empty record encodes to 70 octets; 196,609 payload octets in one group; six 256-octet groups at A). config-tests: a 256-octet group name is a 256-octet label; a 257-octet string is not a label. native-control-tests: the named status survives the sealed reply and exits 1; :uncertain and :fault are not refusals.

proofs.title: BP journal rotation: recovery from a selected held-row checkpoint equals recovery over the whole history, and every publication cut leaves one authority
proofs.statement: fn-bpnr-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover (restated for N16-F1, lane bp-n16-prod): for every authority plan0 that is not damaged, whose ordered received-final rows replay :ready, the projection ck1 of that replay (a checkpoint), E the epoch field of the recovery event over plan0 and the rows, and the file of the checkpoint the rotation publishes, fn-bpnr-rotation-checkpoint ck1 E (operation frontier (E . 0), the rotation's own id; what fn-bpnp-rotate-step's effect carries and host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-publish-generation writes): fn-bpnr-recover-auto-event (the event fnn-bps-open passes to fn-bpnp-step) over that file with no later rows names epoch E + 1 with the old replay at frontier (E . 0) and row count 0, so no operation after the reopen reuses the rotation's id; over later rows that start after (E . 0) it equals the event over plan0 and the concatenated rows with field 5 set to the later rows' count. fn-bpnr-rotation-crash-recovers-old-or-new: at every phase of the publication driver fn-bpnr-publish-action/-step/-outcome (followed by fnn-bps-publish-generation) and for either outcome of an atomic rename, the visible selection file is the old or the new one, before the rename may have been issued it is the old one, and under the new one recovery with no rows is the reopen event above. fn-bpnp-rotate-step-proposes-only-own-projection: a proposal carries fn-bpnr-rotation-checkpoint of the state's own projection, from a quiescent state, and its file exists. fn-bpnr-retirement-cut-keeps-open-view: when the root's selection file selects G and no other name the open reads is retired, the open's view (selection plan, selected directory, the other names) after any prefix of fn-bpnr-retire-ops (the removal program host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-retire-generations runs step by step: older generation directories and killed rotations' staged selections) equals the view before it; fn-bpnr-retired-names-never-the-selected-directory. fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode-of-octets: every file fn-bpnr-checkpoint-octets writes decodes to its checkpoint. Covered scope: one atomically renamed kind-19 file; the chunked kinds 19 plus a manifest kind, the :quiesce event and the empty new-generation premise are not modelled; the removal model is a name-to-entry alist, not K0's byte store; the codec runs on octet lists (no D27 concrete twin); a killed rotation's unselected new-generation directory is kept (never reused).
proofs.progress_note: Lane n16-rotation (2026-09-25), spec bp-node-machine 3.6 slice E, trace N16. Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-counterexamples-tests: the positive trace through fn-bpnp-step, must-fails for a damaged plan0, absent octets and an unready prefix (recovery keystone) and a visible new file before the rename (crash keystone). Certified in hbox runs run-20260925T044146Z-230d, run-20260925T050214Z-702e and run-20260925T051528Z-15c2. Lane bp-n16-prod (2026-09-25): N16-F1 repaired (the published checkpoint's frontier is the rotation's own id; the recovery keystone restated with the event's epoch), and old generations retired by an ACL2 program whose every prefix is a model crash point; teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-counterexamples-tests (N16 section, over real kind-5 rows) and tests/acl2/bp-node-retire-tests.

proofs.title: Open from an exact-state Store checkpoint equals the full open
proofs.statement: fn-sn-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover: for every configuration history, frontier, record prefix P and suffix Q, (fn-sco-open (fn-sco-capture configs P) configs frontier Q) equals (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier (append P Q)), with no hypothesis; fn-sco-open is what the host calls at open when a checkpoint verified (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint) and fn-cpo-open-observed is the full open (fn-store-sn-recover). Built from one append lemma per fold of fn-cpo-open-observed: fn-cpr-loop-append (configuration and node fold, paused at the prefix end), fn-replay-identity-append, fn-cpe-projection-replay-append, fn-th-prefix-project-append, fn-cei-build-append; the history recognizer runs over the carried record list. fn-sco-extend-of-capture: the next checkpoint is the extension. fn-sco-capture-of-later-configs: a configuration whose txid is above every covered record does not change the capture. fn-scc-decode-segments-of-segments: the FNSC segments decode to the value, for every tree whose program and record count fit the u64 header fields. fn-bs-scp-program-crash-is-old-or-new: at every cut of the publish program the checkpoint name is the old file, absent, or the new octets. fn-bs-read-ranges-concatenate: consecutive range reads concatenate under A-HOST-EXCLUSIVE-READ. Owner (2026-09-25, lane owner-checkpoint-open): fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover, with no hypothesis: the owner fn-ock-recover-extended installs from (fn-sco-extend (fn-sco-capture configs P) configs Q) is the owner fn-ock-recover-full installs from the full open of P ++ Q (the composition fn-orec-recover-installs-ocl-relation is stated over: the Store open, the configuration replay, fn-own-start's archive, views, trie and ledger, fn-own-configure, fn-ocfg-make) or :fault on both; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended calls fn-ock-recover-extended on both paths (fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint over the decoded checkpoint and the suffix, fn-owner-recover over the empty capture and the whole history, fn-ock-recover-from-empty-capture-is-full). fn-ock-recover-installs-ocl-relation carries fn-ocl-relation and fn-scar-view-indexedp to what is installed on either path. Publication: fn-ock-next-checkpoint-is-the-capture (hypothesis: an admitted history, which has no must-fail) and fn-ock-published-checkpoint-opens-to-the-full-open: what the owner publishes is the capture of its whole history and opens, over any later records, to the full open; fn-ock-not-due-keeps-the-checkpoint-open: until fn-ock-publication-duep (twice the suffix reaches K) the durable checkpoint is the one a restart selects. Replay carries the node invariant: fn-cpr-apply-event-preserves-cnode-statep (no hypothesis beyond non-refusal) and fn-cpr-loop-preserves-cnode-statep; fn-cpr-apply-event and fn-cpr-loop test a refusal by NIL on the executable path.
proofs.progress_note: Open items: K0 coverage of the publish program's :root rename and :root fsync (fn-bs-k0-step-inputp admits neither; the profile program has the same gap); the whole-file statement over the host's range loop; the publication keystone's history hypothesis has no must-fail (the identity fold's fault is absorbing); the owner's open still re-encodes the covered prefix's octets for fnn-open-live-store's other callers (P3 finding 4) and the Store open and the owner open each replay the suffix.

proofs.title: Control authority requires a verified principal and a covering grant; a withdrawal record is decided once and serves no view that holds its cancel
proofs.statement: fn-ctl-authorize-requires-verified-verdict: an :execute from fn-ctl-authorize VERDICT VERB GROUPS ROWS (books/control-authority.lisp) has verdict token :verified with a 32-octet principal. fn-ctl-authorize-requires-a-covering-grant: under :execute, for every GROUP of GROUPS, fn-ctl-covering-row is a member of ROWS whose principal is the verified one, whose verb is VERB and whose namespace pattern covers GROUP. fn-cfg-grant-control-admissible-iff: fn-cfg-delta-reason admits (fn-cfg-grant-control NS P VERB) iff NS is a namespace pattern, P 64 lowercase hex characters and VERB is cancel. fn-ctl-revoke-changes-decisions-not-records: when every cancel entry's txid is below the first appended configuration record's, fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals ENTRIES (append CONFIGS MORE) equals fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals ENTRIES CONFIGS. fn-ctl-cancel-executes-only-for-author-or-authority: a withdrawing fn-ctl-withdrawal-effect W T-GROUPS T-VERDICT means the target's verdict names W's principal, or W's scope is nonempty and covers every one of the nonempty T-GROUPS. fn-ctl-target-is-never-visible-beside-its-cancel: an article targeted by a record of WS whose cause is among ARTICLES and whose effect withdraws is not in fn-ctl-visible-articles ARTICLES WS VERDICTS. fn-ctl-pinned-view-keeps-its-archive: a record whose cause is absent from ARTICLES leaves the visible articles unchanged. fn-ctl-visible-is-arrival-order-independent: (T C . REST) and (C T . REST) serve the same articles. fn-hsig-signed-control-record-lists-its-filing-group: fn-hsig-carried-record-metadatap SOURCE RECEIVED RECORD (books/hybrid-store.lisp; a conjunct of the schema-1 and carried replay bindings replay's identity step calls, and required by the native constructor fn-hsig-authorized-carried-submission-event-base that host/native/hybrid-control.lisp and host/native/owner.lisp reach) with SOURCE classified (:control VERB ARGS) implies the record lists exactly (fn-ctl-filing-group VERB). fn-hsig-malformed-control-binds-no-record: a source classified :malformed binds no record. fn-ctl-visible-add-is-visible and fn-ctl-visible-extend-is-visible (books/control-visible.lisp): when the carried list equals fn-ctl-visible-articles OLD WS VERDICTS, the incremental list after one new article (resp. a batch DELTA) equals fn-ctl-visible-articles of (A . OLD) (resp. (append DELTA OLD)); an ordinary article costs one pass over WS, an executed cancel one pass over the visible list. fn-ctl-refresh-visible-is-visible (books/control-visible.lisp; called by fn-own-refresh, books/owner.lisp, which every owner step at an idle store runs): when the carried visible list equals fn-ctl-visible-articles OLD WS OLD-VERDICTS and NEW has distinct Message-IDs, fn-ctl-refresh-visible NEW OLD OLD-VISIBLE WS2 OLD-VERDICTS VERDICTS equals fn-ctl-visible-articles NEW WS2 VERDICTS, WS2 being fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals NEW OLD WS VERDICTS RECORDS CONFIGS (the records fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan decides for each cancel or superseding article the refresh first publishes, under fn-ctl-config-at of that article's own acceptance-record txid in the Store records RECORDS over the configuration journal CONFIGS). fn-ctl-articles-withdrawals-is-the-journal: the rebuild the refresh runs at a discontinuity (start, reopen) equals fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals over the archive's entries (TXID CAUSE VERDICT TARGET). fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals-is-the-journal (called by fn-own-refresh with the Store's records and fn-sn-config-history): when the carried records are the journal of the old archive under the old Store records R0, verdicts V0 and configuration journal C0, every withdrawing article of the old archive has its acceptance record in R0, the verdicts grew by at most one pair for a Message-ID outside the old archive, and the configuration records appended since carry txids above every old entry, the refresh's records over the grown inputs are the journal of the new archive under them: the live decision is recovery's. fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan-record-is-bound: a record names its cause, its target (a cancel argument or a Supersedes field, fn-ctl-article-target), the verified principal, the principal's cancel grants and the generation. fn-ctl-visible-state-statep: the visible state of an acceptance state is one. Supporting (not registry events; teeth are the owner tests' relation witnesses): fn-own-refresh-preserves-relation and fn-own-conn-serves-a-projection (books/owner-invariants.lisp), the restated K1 holds after every refresh; the committed view's archive is fn-ctl-visible-state of its prefix under the records and verdicts it carries, and a connection's archive is that prefix's state with a subsequence of its articles. Covered scope: the served view and every connection pinned after a withdrawing article's refresh, records decided at each article's own txid live and at recovery alike, Supersedes under the cancel's rules. Served answers (control-c3e; subject fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned, books/nntp.lisp, reached from fn-own-read through fn-served-step and fn-served-dispatch; the control pin is the fourth slot of the group pin, the owner connection's fn-own-conn-control set from fn-own-view-control at open and advance): fn-nntp-423-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-holder, when the pin's withdrawn list is fn-ctl-withdrawn-articles RAW WS VERDICTS, a `423 withdrawn' answer names an article of RAW holding the number that the view does not serve and the pinned archive holds nothing at that number; fn-nntp-withdrawn-holder-answers-423-withdrawn, the converse for ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY/STAT with one number argument and a selected group; fn-nntp-430-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-article and fn-nntp-withdrawn-article-answers-430-withdrawn, the same by Message-ID under the pinned trie's correspondence with the archive; fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-is-the-status, `HDR :fn-control <msgid>' answers one line whose item is fn-ctl-control-item of fn-ctl-control-status (the kernel, over the trie by fn-ctl-served-status-is-control-status) of the article with that Message-ID, served or withdrawn, or 430, or 503 when the item would not be a clean field; fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-executed-means-withdrawn, an executed status names a target RAW holds and the view does not serve, withdrawn by the record the article caused. fn-own-read-archive-command-is-the-pinned-dispatcher (books/owner-control-read.lisp; host line host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk): one read framing one archive command line answers that dispatcher's reply over the connection's archive, trie, buckets and control pin whenever the reply offers no article; fn-own-related-conn-control: under fn-own-relation a connection's control pin has W = fn-ctl-withdrawn-articles of its pinned prefix under the pinned records and its archive serves that prefix's visible list (fn-own-control-okp in fn-own-conn-okp; the view carries W = fn-ctl-subseq-diff of its raw and visible lists, refreshed by fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawn). Kernel (books/control-served.lisp): fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawn-is-withdrawn (now for any RAW), fn-ctl-number-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-holder, fn-ctl-msgid-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-article, fn-ctl-executed-status-means-withdrawn, fn-ctl-owed-status-means-not-held. Not covered: the owner-level lift has no teeth book yet (no reachable owner witness nor must-fail per hypothesis for fn-own-read-archive-command-is-the-pinned-dispatcher); the owner relation does not carry the journal equality nor the configuration-txid fact it rests on (records appended later have larger txids); the txid lookup walks the Store records (no Message-ID-to-txid index); a view with an empty group index pins no control, so it answers the plain 423/430 (a view serving no article).
proofs.progress_note: Lane control-c2c3 (2026-09-25), packets C2 and C3 of planning/design-2026-09-25-control-messages.md under D29. Teeth in tests/acl2/control-authority-tests.lisp: per keystone a reachable witness asserting antecedent and conclusion, and per hypothesis a removal witness (the carried verdict; the cross-post outside the grant; the wrong principal; the revoke before the cancel; the view pinned before the cancel; the early cancel). The two reconfiguration headlines (fn-ocl-no-reader-observes-a-half-change, fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation) are universally quantified over delta lists and were recertified with the new slot and kinds. Open: the served view (K1 restated over fn-ctl-visible-articles at fn-own-refresh), signed control filing, the host's commit-time call, Supersedes. Lane control-c3 (2026-09-25): the signed record binding names the filing group (the :control-signed refusal is gone, signed cancels can be verified), and the visible list has an incremental form with its correspondence keystones. Still open: the owner wiring (fn-own-refresh carrying the visible list, K1 restated), the host's commit-time and recovery calls, 430/423, HDR :fn-control, Supersedes, fn_verify. Lane control-c3d (2026-09-25): records decided at each withdrawing article's own Store txid, live and at recovery (the journal keystones); Supersedes; the config-owner-live rules scoped (15.1 s to 7.6 s); the reader kernel for 423/430 withdrawn and HDR :fn-control with no caller yet; fn_verify's withdrawal report. Open: the served wiring of the reader kernel, the owner relation carrying the journal equality, the two-node native cases.

proofs.title: Owed receipts leave from bp-node serve: the contact offers exactly the queued receipt job on its route
proofs.statement: fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-offers-the-queued-job: over the called fn-bpnp-step on (:base E), where E is fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-event of the node state and the peer (the event host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-send-receipts asks for after each fnn-bpnode-queue-outboxes in bp-node serve), for a well-formed base, a non-nil event and a journal token below *fn-bpn-machine-max-records*, the one effect persists the :attempting record of the first :queued job for that peer and the pending success effect is that job's :cl-send with its route, peer, key and wire. fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-event-needs-a-queued-job: the event is non-nil exactly when the peer is an EID, nothing is issued, no delivery is uncertain, the base is neither fenced nor pending and a :queued job for the peer exists. fn-bpnp-uncertain-receipt-transfer-keeps-the-job-owed and fn-bpnp-receipt-reoffer-after-uncertain (spec 4.3.2): an uncertain base transfer is connection-local; over the called fn-bpnp-step it proposes only the durable :requeued :uncertain record, keeps the job :attempting until that is durable, fences nothing and emits no release, receipt-prepare or :forwarded; once durable the job is :queued again with its own identity and the receipt contact event opens for its peer again. Only an uncertain publication fences. Covered scope: the decision, the offer and the uncertain transfer's outcome; a connect that produces no socket reads :failed and requeues the same way. The host's exit scope (serve and dispatch continue; bp-contact tick answers exit 3) is host reporting over these effects. Open: 'offered once per contact' is not an ACL2 statement over the host loop (fnn-bpc-drive-contact stops at the first transfer or outcome that is not :accepted and the durable :attempting record takes the job out of :queued; the latter is witnessed in the test book, not proved over a driver).

proofs.title: The running owner's status report is the offline report of the same state, and its pages join to it
proofs.statement: fn-nls-live-report-is-the-offline-report: for every KIND (status, pins, peers, obligations), profile, configured owner OC and observation, when the carried octet sum CACHE is valid for the records of OC's Store (fn-sbud-octets-cache-validp) and no connection is open (no pin in fn-ocfg-pins), (fn-nls-live-report kind profile oc cache obs) equals (fn-nls-offline-report kind profile (fn-own-store (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) (fn-ocfg-config oc) obs); the owner reaches fn-nls-live-report through fn-native-live-status-host-answer (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer), once per request and the offline command reaches fn-nls-offline-report through fn-native-live-status-host-offline (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-live-report). fn-nls-client-step-of-owner-reply: for every octet REPORT whose length is a uint32 and every client prefix ACC of it (with, past the first page, the report's total and digest), the client's step on the owner's page from (len ACC) is :done REPORT, or :next with the strictly longer prefix of one more chunk; fnn-control-live-status folds pages through fn-nls-client-step. fn-nls-page-of-buffer-is-reply: for every REPORT and OFFSET, (fn-nls-page (fn-nls-buffer report) offset) equals (fn-nls-reply report offset), with no hypothesis; fn-nls-buffer is the report as one string with its frame digest and fn-nls-page answers a substring of it (the D27 twin of the page). fn-nls-client-step-of-owner-page: the client-step keystone with the same hypotheses over the page the owner answers, (fn-nls-page (fn-nls-buffer report) (len acc)). fn-nls-cached-buffer-of-put: for a positive offset, the buffer the owner looks up for KIND after storing BUFFER for KIND is BUFFER; fn-native-live-status-host-answer renders anew at offset 0 and otherwise pages from the stored buffer. fn-nls-nat-is-the-decimal-digits: for every natural N, (fn-nls-nat N), which renders every number of the report, is a nonempty run of decimal digits whose value under fn-nntp-decimal-value is N. Supporting: fn-nls-reply-decode-of-encode, fn-nls-request-decode-of-encode, fn-nls-open-of-seal. fn-nls-report-of-query-kind-is-query-report: for every administrative plan, the status-path report of the kind fn-native-admin-result-report-kind names -- the kind host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-admin passes to fnn-operator-status-once for an accepted `peer list' or `control list', live (fn-nls-live-report) or offline (fn-nls-offline-report) -- is fn-nls-query-report of the plan over the same configuration (fn-native-admin-query-report, or books/accounts.lisp fn-acct-list-report for `account list'), so `control list' renders the authority rows (fn-cfg-authorities), `peer list' the peers and `account list' the accounts slot; supporting: fn-native-admin-control-report-empty-iff-no-rows (the listing is empty only over no grant row). Covered scope: the rows are rendered, not parsed back (qual-e747dbcc A3).
proofs.progress_note: Answering changes no state by signature (the host wrappers return one value and no state), not by a theorem. The multi-page join trusts the frame digest to name one report (A-CRYPTO): a report that changes between pages restarts the join, at most 8 times. The owner pages from a string buffer rendered once per request (fn-nls-page); the renderer and the FNLS frames are still octet lists (their D27 twin is open). The open= line names each process's own open, the offline orphan listing is the reader's own observation, and the checkpoint-file line is each answering process's lstat at the request. The words (the history-marker word, checkpoint-file, open-cost) are tests, not theorems; the live and offline reports share them through fn-nls-report.

proofs.title: A recognized Store event's kind and fields are read by shape on the commit the host calls
proofs.statement: On every Store event (fn-store-event-p), fn-evc-field-by-shape at 0, 1 and 2 equals fn-store-event-sequence, -txid and -generation, and fn-evc-class-by-shape names exactly the recognizer that holds (fn-record-p, fn-store-retention-event-p, fn-stxe-p, fn-stxk-p, fn-stxa-p, fn-cpe-eventp, fn-th-topic-eventp); each reading is O(1) and looks at the head and at most ten conses (books/store-events-carried.lisp, ten keystones, :rule-classes nil). The carried accessors fn-evc-* are the references in the logic and these readings in execution, guard fn-store-event-p, which a history record carries under fn-sn-statep (fn-ccar-seek-finds-a-store-event). The commit the host calls reads the completion record through them: fn-ccar-own-finish-is-own-finish (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission) and fn-ccar-ocfg-complete-is-ocfg-step-complete, fn-ccar-ocfg-complete equal to fn-ocfg-step of (:complete) for every configured owner with no hypothesis (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish, the completion of identity, retention, consumer and topic events: the signed POST). The feed intent's Path is parsed once at take and carried: fn-icar-submission-targets equals fn-own-submission-targets under fn-icar-carryp (host fn-owner-submission-intent and fn-owner-submission-resolution).
proofs.progress_note: Open: the identity prepare (host fn-owner-prepare-identity) still goes through the unverified fn-ocfg-step and fn-sn-prepare-identity, whose fn-sf-prepare-record replays the whole appended history (fn-sf-history-recoverablep); the article path's correspondence (fn-spc-related-candidate-is-recoverable) has no identity analog yet. fn-replay-apply-record and fn-replay-identity-step still recognize the composite and decode its record on the gate and again on the finish. UPDATED 2026-09-26 (PRF-144, lane signed-history-index): the identity prepare no longer replays the appended history; fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity stages through fn-spc-stage-record and equals fn-sn-prepare-identity under fn-snt-relation.

proofs.title: The octet buffer abstracts to the octet list
proofs.statement: fn-octets (books/octets-stobj.lisp) is an abstract stobj whose logical value is the octet list and whose executable is a resizable (unsigned-byte 8) array with a fill count. The abstraction relation fn-octets$corr (the array's first FILL cells read in order are the list, the fill count is within the array, the concrete object is well formed) is established by the creator (create-fn-octets{correspondence}) and preserved by every export, and every export's executable step equals the list operation on the abstraction under the export's guard: fn-octets-get{correspondence} is nth, fn-octets-put{correspondence} is update-nth, fn-octets-append-octet{correspondence} is append of one octet (through the array's doubling resize), fn-octets-list{correspondence} is the list read tail-recursively, fn-octets-from-list{correspondence} is the list written; each with the guard theorem and the logical preservation ACL2 requires. The derived readers a codec twin reads the buffer with are their take/nthcdr terms over the logical value, under the hypothesis that the value is a true list, which every buffer value is: fn-oct-slice-list-is-take-nthcdr, fn-oct-prefix-equalp-is-list-prefixp (a prefix test against the list-model shape fn-inj-strip has, not take, which pads with nil past the end), fn-oct-suffix-equalp-is-equal. Every executable function is guard-verified. The host fills the array from the byte vector of a socket read in raw Lisp (host/native/io.lisp fnn-octets-fill: reserve, one replace, the count; A-HOST) and calls the buffer entries with the live stobj (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt).
proofs.progress_note: Consumers on the buffer: the existing-article test and the prepare of the served POST (fn-pbb-existing-action-is-pb-existing-action, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer and fn-owner-prepare-buffer). Since 2026-09-25 (pbb-d32) the buffer twin reads a recipe v3 record (D32, a supplied Path): the source is a description (K A B) of buffer positions, st[K..A) then st[B..) with the AGENT! insertion cut out, found by the index Path scan (fn-pbb-path-scan-is-inj-path-scan, fn-pbb-unsplice-at-is-inj-unsplice, fn-pbb-source-index-is-inj-source-of) and compared in place (fn-pbb-range-match-is-equal-of-append, fn-pbb-desc-equalp-is-equal); the agent of a v3 record is read from its block (fn-pbb-block-agent-is-pb-block-agent, fn-pbb-path-agent-is-pb-path-agent). Open: the payload digest over the buffer needs a SHA-256 reader by index (books/sha256-stobj.lisp, a third message reader beside the string and list readers); the chunk read (fn-owner-chunk) and the accumulated body are the owner's logical state (wave C); the record encoder, the frame and the article parser over the buffer are boundaries 7 to 9 of planning/design-2026-09-25-representation.md.

proofs.title: Frame blobs have per-schema widths; the control socket carries an article up to the profile's A
proofs.statement: D27, packets PKT-008/009. The frame field grammar (books/frame-fields) has a spec form (:blob . W), 1 <= W <= 2^32-1, beside :blob (131 072, the node's own fields); fn-frame-field-parse-of-octets-wide-blob (books/frame-invariants) is its round trip, and fn-frame-fields-octets-within-width: a record whose values satisfy SPECS encodes to at most (fn-frame-specs-width SPECS) octets, which is the journal encoders' guard bound (books/frame-journal, with the FNWF and FNRJ tables proved within their payload caps). The FNCT request's article field is (:blob . *fn-record-max-payload*) and its group-list field the encoded list at the record's group ceiling (books/native-control). KEYSTONE fn-native-control-request-within-profile-frame: for naturals A and G, every request encoding (fn-native-control-request-encode, which the client calls through fn-native-control-host-request-encode in host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-submit) whose article is at most A octets and whose group list has at most G names is at most (fn-nctrl-max-frame-for A G) octets; fn-native-control-request-within-read-bound gives the same under fn-nctrl-read-bound-for, the bound the owner reads a control connection under (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-handle-client, computed once at fnn-control-start from the carried profile's A and G through fn-owner-control-profile-bounds and fn-native-control-host-read-bound, or fn-native-hybrid-control-host-read-bound = fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for when hybrid control is built in, which covers both, fn-nhctrl-read-bound-covers-both). The owner's injection decision then refuses an article past A as article-exceeds-profile-bound (PRF-016's boundary). Covered scope: the request encoder and the read bound; the frame decoder's cons walk and the ACL2 octet lists at runtime are D27's representation work, not this target. The FNRJ request-context blobs (a Store record and a request ADU at 131 072), the app journal's record count and aggregates, and the history pre-check figures (PKT-011) are open.
proofs.progress_note: Certified: runs 22ae (538 passed) and 2f56 (exit 0) on persvati, e8e4 on hbox (image closure, 198 passed); native operator post of 131 073 and 290 000 octets under A = 300 000 accepted, 300 001 refused by name (planning/evidence/bounds-blob-2026-09-25.md). Open: the FNRJ receipt blobs and app-journal counts (PKT-010 remainder), the pre-reservation figures (PKT-011, blocked by fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-verdict, PRF-072), and the octet lists at runtime on this path (D27 representation).

proofs.title: Content reclamation removes only unheld payload bytes and every history decision reads the same afterwards
proofs.statement: fn-rcl-reclaimable-is-no-obligation-names-it: (fn-rcl-reclaimable rule now h verdicts article) equals: not a tombstone, rule not keep-forever and a rule, the rule permits the article's stamp at now, no authorship verdict other than :absent (fn-rcl-verdict-heldp), and no obligation of (fn-rcl-obligations h) -- reader pin, consumer cursor, undelivered feed to a live peer, BP obligation -- names the article; no hypothesis. fn-rcl-reclaim-never-touches-a-held-article: if an obligation names the article or the rule is keep-forever, fn-rcl-reclaim-if-permitted is the identity. fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-the-duplicate-history: fn-acceptedp of every Message-ID is unchanged, no hypothesis. fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-every-binding and fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-the-numbering: groups, memberships, pin, stamp, per-group next numbers, next txid and pending unchanged; every other article unchanged. fn-rcl-reclaim-preserves-statep: under fn-statep. fn-rcl-prepare-commutes-with-reclaim: under fn-statep, fn-accept-prepare after reclaiming equals reclaiming after fn-accept-prepare. fn-rcl-existing-action-after-reclaim: for an article M present and not already a tombstone, the D25 verdict fn-rcl-action-over (host subject fn-rcl-existing-action) for every Message-ID, submission and groups is unchanged, or SHA-256 collides on the compared pair, or the submission names another agent under which the removed payload gives back a source. fn-rcl-config-rule-after-retention-set: under fn-rcl-rulep, the rule read after fn-cfg-apply of fn-rcl-rule-deltas is the rule, on any prior value. fn-nntp-reclaimed-article-answers-reclaimed: fn-nntp-article-response on an article with a usable identifier and a tombstone payload answers 423 (number or current) or 430 (Message-ID) article reclaimed. fn-rclb-existing-action-is-rcl-existing-action: under fn-octets-p (the buffer's recognizer), the buffer verdict the native owner calls (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer, fn-owner-prepare-buffer) equals fn-rcl-existing-action; the list sites call fn-rcl-existing-action directly (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare, fn-owner-existing-action; host/store-node-host.lisp prepare and fn-store-sn-existing-action). fn-nntp-over-by-msgid-answers-reclaimed: for a Message-ID token naming a held tombstone, fn-nntp-over-response (called by fn-nntp-archive-command) answers 430 article reclaimed; fn-nntp-over-current-answers-reclaimed: with a selected group and a current article that is a tombstone, 423 article reclaimed. fn-nov-lines-indexed-skip-a-reclaimed-article (subject of fn-nntp-over-range-indexed, the pinned OVER/XOVER range) and fn-nov-lines-skip-a-reclaimed-article (unpinned): the lines over NUMBERS equal the lines over NUMBERS without a tombstoned article's number. fn-nntp-newnews-scan-lists-only-live-articles: every Message-ID fn-nntp-newnews-scan lists is that of an article that is not a tombstone; no other hypothesis. fn-rcl-store-holders-hold-behind-a-lagging-consumer: while a registered consumer's acknowledgement is below the committed frontier, no article numbered (n >= 1) in a served group is reclaimable under fn-rcl-store-holders, for every rule, clock and verdict list. fn-rcl-absent-verdict-contributes-nothing: when fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of a payload under any keyring is :absent, fn-stx-delta of that payload is nil under every keyring, so an :absent verdict holds nothing; with fn-sn-finish-records-the-acceptance-verdict (the recorded verdict is fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of the payload) and fn-rcl-tombstone-contributes-nothing (fn-stx-delta of any payload satisfying fn-rcl-tombstonep is nil under every keyring), reclaiming such an article leaves the statement index every later open derives unchanged. fn-rcl-tombstone-refused-at-carrier-form: every payload satisfying fn-rcl-tombstonep gets (:refused :article) from fn-pa-carrier-form, which the host calls as fn-owner-peer-carrier-form (host/owner-host.lisp) in host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit before any Store call, on every served ingress (POST, IHAVE, TAKETHIS, peer and BP transit, bound submissions); no other hypothesis. Its keystone lemma fn-rca-nul-first-octet-is-not-an-article: an octet string whose first octet is 0 does not parse (fn-article-parse), no other hypothesis. Not covered: the developer image's store post (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-post), which prepares a raw payload file without an article check.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the durable `store reclaim` byte program and its `--dry-run` verb in books/native-operator (design B, reclaim through the compaction pack: planning/evidence/reclaim-host-2026-09-25.md); the reclaimed record's own replay step; holders: the consumer reading is conservative (a lagging consumer holds every article), feed state and FNBS rows are not read, reader pins have no durable form (offline reclaim needs none); the retention charge released with the payload; articles with a verdict other than :absent are held; the buffer's source digest slices the two ranges of the D32 description into one list on the resend-of-a-reclaimed-article path (a two-range buffer digest reader would remove it); native N=5,000 run and cut campaign (SCN-048).

proofs.title: A supplied Path is prefixed in place and the injection inverse still recovers the exact source
proofs.statement: Over fn-inj-decide (books/injection.lisp), which books/nntp-post.lisp fn-nntp-post-step calls for a served POST and books/owner.lisp fn-own-operator-decision for the operator's post: fn-inj-source-of-inverts-the-injection, every injected article gives back its source exactly under fn-inj-source-of, at every clock reading, in all four generated-field cases, with or without a supplied Path (recipe v3); its keystone for the Path case is fn-inj-unsplice-of-a-splice (books/injection-path.lisp): inserting AGENT! where the source's Path content begins and removing it gives back the source, because fn-inj-path-scan-of-a-kept-prefix shows the scan reads nothing at or past the offset it returns. fn-inj-injected-octets-are-the-block-and-the-prefixed-source: with a Path supplied the injected octets are the v2 block without its Path line followed by the source with AGENT! inserted at fn-inj-path-offset; fn-inj-injected-article-retains-the-source-octets now holds under the hypothesis that no Path was supplied. RFC 5537 section 3.5 item 11 twins: fn-inj-no-injection-date-when-date-and-message-id-are-supplied-with-a-path and fn-inj-injection-date-is-the-clock-otherwise-with-a-path. D25 over v3 (books/poster-bytes-invariants.lisp, fn-pb-existing-action the host calls): fn-pb-path-agent-of-an-injection reads the agent from a v3 block's Injection-Info line, so fn-pb-one-source-at-two-clocks-is-one-article and fn-pb-two-sources-are-two-articles cover a supplied Path: a resend at any clock is already stored here, a changed supplied Path is the conflict.
proofs.progress_note: Certified on persvati at 694935ab (run-20260925T092122Z-f678, manifest certify-20260925T092155Z-3183327, 239 of 239) and again inside the config fan-out at bba8bb15 (certify-20260925T094334Z-3395289); native witnesses in planning/evidence/path-and-login-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.title: A bound login's accepted signed article carries its bound principal; the policy off changes nothing
