proofs.statement: Over fn-lb-owner-gate (books/login-binding.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-gate calls for host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-served before the transit attempt, composed with fn-pa-current-plan, which that attempt calls next: fn-lb-bound-login-accepted-signed-article-carries-its-principal, when the owner's live configuration sets posting-policy bound-logins, the in-flight submission's login is bound to principal P, the gate passes and the plan answers :ok, the plan's principal (the one its verified verdict names) is P. fn-lb-bound-login-unsigned-article-is-refused and fn-lb-bound-login-other-principal-is-refused: under the policy a bound login's article with no FN-Authorship carrier is (:refused :login-unsigned LOGIN), and one whose carrier names another principal is (:refused :login-not-bound LOGIN). fn-lb-policy-off-never-refuses and fn-lb-unbound-login-never-refuses: without the policy, or for a login with no binding (an unauthenticated connection's login is nil), the gate passes and the host continues into the attempt it made before. fn-lb-verdict-names-the-login: every verdict names the in-flight login. The policy the gate reads is the value set last: fn-cfg-set-policy-sets-the-policy (books/config-invariants.lisp), over fn-cfg-apply-delta, after a :set-policy delta for a slot the policy read for that slot is the value set, so `policy set posting-policy open` turns the gate off (before 2026-09-25 the first value set stayed in force).
proofs.progress_note: Certified on persvati at 694935ab (manifest certify-20260925T092155Z-3183327) and, with the config fold fix, at bba8bb15 (certify-20260925T094334Z-3395289); native rows B1-B5 and O1-O2 in planning/evidence/path-and-login-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.title: The operator surface's verdicts are ACL2's: the served bound, refused-POST log lines, the credential change's effect, the developer init words, needs-upgrade and the rollback check
proofs.statement: fn-osb-install-serves-the-profile-bound: for an admitted Store profile, fn-osb-install -- which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-profile calls from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-install on every run path, the developer owner run included -- answers :installed and leaves an owner whose fn-own-body-limit, the bound every later connection's wire reads, is the profile's max-article-octets A; fn-osb-install-keeps-the-posting-configuration: the posting bit, agent and served groups are unchanged; fn-osb-install-keeps-configp: a well-formed posting configuration stays one. fn-olog-served-refusal-lines-one-per-441: the lines host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk leaves for a socket read are exactly one per 441 reply in the effects the client is sent, each one line beginning refused; fn-olog-post-refusal-reason-names-the-sent-reason: each injection reason fn-post-refusal-line names reads back from its reply as itself. fn-olog-control-refusal-line-says-refused-iff-submit-refused: the line fn-owner-operator-submit leaves says refused exactly when fn-own-operator-submit-result is :refused (no hypothesis). fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-restart-unless-no-owner: the credential verb's answer, fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word, which host/native/auth-admin.lisp fnn-native-auth-admin-result-code calls, is restart-required exactly when the writer-lock observation taken after the durable change is neither :free nor :absent and the running owner did not answer :accepted or :uncertain to the binding reload (PKT-221, PRF-175; a password change never asks, so for it this is the old statement). Covered scope: that the host observes the lock after the durable write, writes each line and one LF, and that the developer init routes its words through fn-nop-developer-init is measured by the native tests, not proved. fn-profile-format-7-store-needs-upgrade: fn-profile-needs-upgrade-verdict, which host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-needs-upgrade calls for `operator CONFIG store needs-upgrade', is by definition the no-argument upgrade-profile verdict's (one owner), and is :needs-upgrade for every admitted format-7 store. fn-profile-rollback-sound-iff-records-within: fn-profile-rollback-verdict, which fnn-command-rollback-check calls with the kept config.json's decoded profile, the store's own config.json profile and the committed transaction files' octet lengths, says :sound exactly when the kept profile is admitted, does not drop the store's history-marker requirement (fn-profile-rollback-drops-markerp), and every length is within fn-profile-rollback-record-bound (R for format 8, H/T for format 7). fn-profile-rollback-keeps-a-required-marker: when the store's profile requires the committed-history marker and the verdict is :sound, the kept profile requires it too; the kept format-7 config.json over a migrated store is refused as history-marker-required-dropped (qual-e747dbcc U1). Covered scope: that the older image's open reads records under that bound is the bounds-join record's statement about that image, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane operator-verdicts, 2026-09-25: PKT-103, PKT-104 (native run), PKT-095, PKT-102, PKT-099. Teeth in the five test books; native runs in planning/evidence/operator-verdicts-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.title: Configuration generations and credentials are bounded by the operator's profile: refused exactly past it, admitted within it, never lowered by an upgrade
proofs.statement: The configuration listing the host calls at open (fn-nco-observe, via host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-config-observation from host/native/io.lisp fnn-config-record-observation) reports :budget iff the namespace has more entries than the profile's max-config-generations (fn-nco-observe-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound, hypothesis: a proper list). The administrative writer (fn-native-admin-publication-authorize, via fn-store-cfg-native-admin-authorize from host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-authorize) accepts only a natural generation within that bound (fn-native-admin-publication-within-the-operator-bound). The AUTHINFO loader the owner installs from (fn-native-auth-load, via fn-native-auth-host-load from host/native/auth.lisp fnn-native-auth-install) installs at most max-credentials credentials, with no hypothesis (fn-native-auth-load-within-the-operator-bound, from the parser keystone fn-native-auth-parse-lines-within-the-operator-bound). Every admitted profile's five namespace counts are within 1..2^32-1 (fn-bs-profile-namespace-counts-within-width), and fn-profile-upgradep never lowers one (fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-namespace-counts).
proofs.progress_note: Consumers (field 9) moved to PRF-167 (community-bounds). Open: BP rows (field 10, *fn-bpn-machine-max-records* 4096 and its 2x), policy members (field 13, *fn-pol-max-members* 64, inside a signed statement codec), pack generation names (*fn-cpp-max-generations* 4096) and the BP ADU bounds (*fn-bpa-max-article*, *fn-bpa-max-octets*). No theorem composes the writer bound with the listing bound through contiguity (the namespace after an accepted publication has GENERATION entries); the admin credential writer's serialized file is not proved within the loader's octet bound, so the runtime check stays (native-auth-admin.lisp fn-native-auth-admin-set-password and the bind arm, (:fault :serialized-profile)): the reason is that the per-credential 512 octets is a comment (native-auth-profile.lisp) and no lemma bounds fn-native-auth-admin-serialize-cred under fn-auth-credp and the bindings' principal width (about 366 octets by count: name 64, three 64-hex fields, a 32-hex salt); the contiguity composition lacks the lemma that config replay of k records has fn-cfg-generation k, and the writer's figure is fn-cvec-config-generations (field 11, one fewer for a non-retention record). Both are PKT-435 item 3 (planning/evidence/community-bounds-2026-09-26.md section 9).

proofs.title: Opaque carriage stays within the boundary's budget over the owner-carried projection, and a present carrier's refusal has exactly one of four classes
proofs.statement: Over the constructor the host calls for the carried arm (fn-pcb-carried-event, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carried-relay-event): given the projection fn-pcb-usage of the committed records at the event's release evidence, committing whatever it returns keeps the history admitted (fn-pcb-carried-event-keeps-history-admitted), and across any admitted history the carried charge through the boundary is at most its charge budget and the count at most its count budget (fn-pcb-carried-history-within-budget); with no budget nothing is carried (fn-pcb-admission-without-a-budget-admits-nothing, fn-pcb-no-budget-history-carries-nothing) and each exhaustion is refused by its own name. The owner's cache read at the evidence equals the projection whenever it is the fold of a prefix of the committed records (fn-pcb-carried-usage-is-the-projection) and stays so (fn-pcb-extended-cache-is-valid, fn-pcb-cache-valid-after-commit). The operator's budget rows read back exactly after the extension delta (fn-pcb-peer-budget-after-extend-delta). For a present carrier not carried and not accepted under both primitive observations, fn-pcb-refusal-class is one of no-local-binding, unsupported-profile, signature-failed and malformed (fn-pcb-present-carrier-not-accepted-has-a-class); an absent carrier has none.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the class is a log detail, not a durable :unverified verdict (dev holds no present-carrier article that is not accepted or carried); the budget is fixed across the admitted history in the trace theorem (a lowered budget refuses from then on but is not restated); BP transit keeps the plan reason.

proofs.title: Queued base jobs are offered only to their routed hop, each at most once per contact; the routed session scans only routed rows and the ungated forms offer nothing
proofs.statement: Host subject since PRF-120: the host asks fn-bpnj-contact-next (books/bp-node-job-offer.lisp; host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact before every offer of a base contact, for bp-service run/resume, bp-obligation request, bp-contact tick and bp-node serve, and fnn-bpnode-send-receipts) and drives its event through fn-bpnj-step (fnn-bps-foundation-step); the named theorems fn-bpnj-contact-next-offer-shape (the offer is the key of fn-bpnj-select's job) and fn-bpnj-step-delegates-every-other-event (fn-bpnj-step is fn-bpnp-step on every event but the three new arms) connect the theorems below, stated over fn-bpnp-contact-next and fn-bpnp-step, to the host-called functions. fn-bpnp-contact-offer-is-the-routed-hop: when fn-bpnp-contact-next (formerly asked directly by fnn-bpc-drive-contact) answers an offer with routing (:table TABLE) in force, fn-bpnp-step on its event (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step), for a well-formed base and a journal token below its bound, persists exactly the :attempting record of the peer's first queued job, the :cl-send it owes carries that job's durable route, and that route is the one fn-bprt-send-decision names over TABLE: the contact port of the boundary fn-bprt-next-hop chooses for the destination among the boundaries with a contact; the EID the host passes as the expected TCPCL peer is the decision's. fn-bpnp-contact-holds-an-unrouted-job: with no route matching the destination the driver never offers. fn-bpnp-contact-offers-each-job-at-most-once: along any sequence of states the host consults it at, threading OFFERED, the keys one contact offers are distinct and none was offered before. fn-bpnp-contact-closes-only-when-nothing-owed-remains: with the peer an EID, nothing issued, no delivery uncertain, the base neither fenced nor pending and a queued job for the peer, a close means that job's key is in OFFERED; fn-bpn-apply-record-keeps-forwarded: no lifecycle record returns a :forwarded job to :queued, so a job queued again after its offer had a transfer that was not accepted. fn-bpnp-step-session-offer-is-the-scan-choice (restated) and fn-bpnp-routed-rows-skip-an-unrouted-row: a routed :session proposes the row the arrival-order scan chooses among the held rows the table routes to its hop, so an unrouted older row never blocks a younger routed one; a :session open or :resume without VIA offers nothing. Covered scope: queue-time routing is host-driven through fn-bprt-job-route and a job is not queued without a route; a table change after queueing holds the job (:route-changed) and a durable re-route record is open; verbs without a Store keep the queued address; the contact host is loopback.

proofs.title: XPAT on the served reader step: the arm is fn-nntp-xpat-response, comma alternatives OR, the label is listed; the POST boundary's refusal text is ACL2's
proofs.statement: Over fn-nntp-step-pinned (books/nntp.lisp), which fn-nntp-post-step-pinned calls for every non-POST command on the served path (fn-served-step, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step-pinned; host/native/owner.lisp through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk): fn-nntp-step-pinned-xpat-is-the-xpat-response, for an open, well-formed, projected session and a command line within the preflight whose keyword is XPAT, the step's result is fn-nntp-xpat-response over the line's arguments (the pinned dispatcher adds no XPAT arm). fn-nntp-xpat-alternation-is-or: appending non-negated wildmat alternatives q to a pattern list p ORs them in the matcher the XPAT arm calls (fn-nntp-xpat-matchesp), over every header content; RFC 2980 section 2.9's join of additional arguments into one pattern is kept. fn-auth-capability-lines-advertise-xpat: the served CAPABILITIES block (fn-auth-capability-lines-for-peer) lists XPAT for every configuration. Over fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusal (books/store-budget-naming.lisp), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-validate-post-boundary calls: fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusal-is-nil-exactly-when-admitted, the rendered refusal is NIL exactly when fn-sbud-post-boundary admits, with fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusals-are-distinct (two different words, one of them a boundary word, never share a text) and fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusal-is-a-printable-line; the host keeps no text table.
proofs.progress_note: See planning/evidence/reader-surface-2026-09-25.md for the farm manifest and native logs.

proofs.title: Records of the old schemas decode and re-encode identically under the u64 record codec
proofs.statement: fn-record-v1-bytes-decode-identically: for all octets, if the pre-P6 decoder (fn-record-v1-decode-exact, books/records-schema-v1.lisp, the text of books/records.lisp at e366c633) accepts them, then (fn-record-decode-exact-impl octets) equals (fn-record-v1-decode-exact octets); fn-record-v1-bytes-are-their-translation: under the same hypothesis the new encoder writes the decoded record back to exactly those octets. The host reaches fn-record-decode-exact-impl through fn-store-event-decode-exact (host/store-host.lisp fn-store-decode-records, called by fn-store-sn-recover) and the seam attachment (books/records-attach.lisp), so an old store opens to the records the old image read and nothing is rewritten. Built on fn-cbor-decode-prechecked-wide-extends-narrow and the restated record keystones fn-record-impl-round-trip and fn-record-impl-accepted-input-is-canonical (now over u64 fields and schema 2). Record ceiling (the fix of the lane's first cut, which raised the overhead a profile's R must hold to 1 111 octets and so refused a saved format-8 profile with R = 17 138 486): fn-record-impl-encode-narrow-length-bound: a record that is not fn-record-widep (sequence, txid, generation, charge and a natural stamp all at most 2^32 - 1) encodes to at most fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count, the 1 083-octet overhead the profile relation reads; the seam exports it as fn-record-encode-narrow-length-bound, and any record, wide or not, is within fn-record-wide-encoded-octets-ceiling (1 111). fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record gains the hypothesis that the record is not wide (every record was narrow before P6; the width of the producers is stated, not proved, and a wide record past R is refused at the publish gate, host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility). fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-stays-valid (books/byte-store-profile-v1.lisp): every VALUES the relation of dev 56eb33ee admitted (fn-bs-profile-v1-invalid-reason, frozen, the ceiling written out at 1 083) is admitted by fn-bs-profile-admittedp, which host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-admittedp calls, and fn-bs-profile-of VALUES is VALUES; its relation half is fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-is-valid.
proofs.progress_note: Certified with teeth; the theorem is over the implementation the seam attaches, not over the constrained seam function; the open corollary over fn-store-sn-recover is by congruence of the program-mode host map and is not an ACL2 event.

proofs.title: The subject digest reads the octet buffer in place
proofs.statement: fn-sha256-of-prefixed-buffer (books/sha256-buffer.lisp) digests (append PREFIX buffer) over the word stobj of books/sha256-stobj.lisp with the buffer read by index: fn-shb-byte is the prefix's octet below the prefix length, the buffer's cell at i - lp below the message length and the padding past it, and the block loader, the compression loop and the digest are the string reader's with the buffer and the prefix in place of the string. fn-sha256-of-prefixed-buffer-is-sha256 (the keystone) says the buffer digest equals fn-sha256 of the appended list on every prefix and every value, with no hypothesis; it is proved as the correspondence of the buffer reader with the list reader on the list's suffix (the byte, the loaded word, the loaded block, the compressed block, the block loop, the digest) and then sha256-stobj's keystone fn-sha256-stobj-is-sha256. fn-sha256-of-prefixed-buffer-is-sha256-of-octets is its instance on an octet prefix and a buffer value (fn-octets-p). fn-shb-subject-id is fn-id-subject-of-payload with the payload in the buffer, and fn-shb-subject-id-is-id-subject-of-sha256-preimage says it is fn-id-subject of fn-sha256 over fn-id-subject-preimage, with no hypothesis: fn-id-subject-of-payload with fn-sha256 in the place of the constrained fn-frame-digest, which is what books/crypto-attach.lisp attaches (fn-sha256-stobj, equal to fn-sha256), so on the host image the two identities are the same octets. Every function is guard-verified. The host calls fn-shb-subject-id through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-subject-id-buffer (the list entry's length test, then the buffer identity), reached from host/native/io.lisp fnn-subject-id-buffer under fnn-metadata-buffer, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt calls for the served POST after fnn-octets-fill: the last per-POST octet list of the payload before the store record is gone.
proofs.progress_note: Lane rep-wave-c (D27 wave C, 2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/sha256-buffer-tests.lisp: the FIPS 180-4 vectors through the buffer reader on a live local buffer with the prefix/buffer split varied, the padding boundaries and a 3,000-octet buffer (past the array's first 1024 cells) against fn-sha256-stobj, non-degeneracy, and the subject identity equal to fn-id-subject-of-payload under the attachment and to the theorem's right-hand side on a 160-octet article, the empty payload and a 3,000-octet payload; both keystones have no hypothesis, so no must-fail case exists; the octets instance's hypotheses are proof support (as sha256-stobj's instance). NOT done here: the owner's chunk read (fn-owner-chunk) and the accumulated body are still octet lists (the owner state's representation, wave C boundary 10); the record encoder, the frame and the article parser over the buffer (boundaries 7 to 9); the obligation identity and the frame trailer still digest short lists.

proofs.title: The checkpoint open and publication cost: one Store open, a count-carrying file, linear list checks, the publication off the owner mutex
proofs.statement: fn-sco-store-open-of-extended-capture: over the capture of any prefix P extended over any Q (P = NIL is the full path), the open fn-sco-store-open computes is (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier (append P Q)), and when it is :ok its configuration fold is (fn-cpr-replay configs (append P Q)); host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended calls fn-sco-store-open on both paths (fn-store-sn-recover over the empty capture, fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint over the decoded checkpoint) and tests the kind, which is fn-sn-open-okp by fn-sco-finalize-okp-is-kind-ok. fn-ock-install-of-store-open-by-definition: fn-ock-install over that pair is fn-ock-recover-extended of E, so PRF-083's owner keystone holds of host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-from-store-open (native owner.lisp fnn-owner-recover-core), with no second extension. fn-sco-thaw-of-freeze: for every checkpoint of the right shape, thawing the file's value (the count in the record slot, the records read back out of the event index) gives the value; fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count: a capture of at most 2^32 records is written with its count; fn-ock-published-segments-decode-to-the-checkpoint composes it with the FNSC round trip under the codec's tree and width hypotheses (host fn-store-sco-decode thaws; fn-store-sco-publish-octets and fn-ock-publication freeze). fn-ock-publication-is-the-capture-at-the-capture-point (hypothesis: an admitted history): the publication the owner runs outside its mutex over the values captured under it (fn-owner-sco-capture, native fnn-owner-publish-captured) is the capture of the captured history. The linear :exec paths equal the unchanged :logic definitions with no hypothesis: fn-ks-distinctp-is-nodupp, fn-ks-subsetp-is-subset-logic, fn-no-duplicatesp-is-ks-nodupp, fn-subsetp-is-ks-subset-logic, fn-article-listp-is-shape-and-distinct-msgids, fn-node-binding-listp-is-shape-and-distinct, fn-retain-no-duplicatesp-is-no-duplicatesp; fn-cnode-statep reaches them through fn-node-statep in fn-sco-cpr-resume, fn-sco-cpr-finish and fn-sco-finalize-from.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the Store state still holds the record list (fn-sf-records; a commit appends to it, store-files.lisp), so the kernel does not yet carry a count; fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp and fn-articles-freshp are still quadratic in the whole-node recognizer; the covered prefix's octets are still re-encoded for fnn-open-live-store's callers; two hypotheses have no must-fail (the :ok hypothesis of the Store open's replay conjunct and the admitted-history hypothesis of the publication keystone) and the 2^32 bound of fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count has no reachable counterexample.

proofs.title: Key succession and revocation over the acceptance plan: the owner's key-statement executor, the :revoked token and its replay binding
proofs.statement: Over fn-pa-current-plan (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carrier-plan, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit), which now takes TRANSITP and has a fifth outcome :revoked: while a principal's newest snapshot is its tombstone no plan for it is :ok on any path (fn-pa-no-ok-plan-for-a-revoked-principal, fn-pa-revocation-leaves-no-ok-plan), and on NNTP transit a carrier under keys once enrolled is :revoked at the tombstone's generation, elsewhere refused :local-enrollment (fn-pa-revoked-principal-on-transit-is-revoked-at-its-tombstone); fn-pa-revoked-event exists only with both primitive observations verified and is the composite replay's revoked branch admits at those snapshots (fn-pa-revoked-event-binds-the-arm-and-both-observations), and replay admits a :revoked composite exactly when its generation names a tombstone of that principal (fn-osp-replay-admits-a-revoked-composite-exactly-at-its-tombstone), leaving the keyring unchanged, as the carried composite does (fn-osp-*-composite-keeps-the-keyring). Over the key-statement executor fn-ks-plan / fn-ks-execute (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-plan / -event, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement after a :verified kind-4 commit): a statement acts only on its own stored :verified verdict with a keys grant covering its groups (C2's fn-ctl-authorize), so a :carried or :revoked statement never changes a keyring; the verdict's generation was the principal's current enrollment and a succession's old key is that enrollment's; the PoP is a D09 signature by the new keys over the statement's Message-ID and old key with both observations verified; after the succession's kind-3 event the new keys are selected and any other key set, the old one included, is refused :local-enrollment; after a revocation's no plan is :ok. The executor runs after every durable kind-4 composite, :carried and :revoked included (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-statement-committed), and a Store refusal of the key change leaves the article accepted and is reported as such (transit detail :key-change-refused; log line `key-statement ... refused`). The crash cut between the statement's commit and its change's is a model crash point: the open's recovery (fn-ks-recover; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover over the newest record, through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-pending) reaches from the cut exactly the uninterrupted acceptance under the recovery's rows and observations (fn-ks-recover-completes-the-cut) and, after an acceptance that acted, changes nothing under any rows or observations (fn-ks-recover-after-an-acting-acceptance-changes-nothing); executing a statement whose change is already the newest snapshot yields nothing (fn-ks-execute-is-idempotent). The verb keys is grantable (fn-cfg-grant-control-admissible-iff over *fn-cfg-control-verbs* = (cancel keys)). The rendered item for :revoked begins `r`, never `v` (fn-stx-verified-item-first-octet-names-the-token), and token code 5 round-trips. The next generation is ACL2's (fn-hl-next-generation; control kinds 7 and 8). Evidence is never rewritten: a kind-3 completion keeps every stored verdict (fn-hls-finish-snapshot-keeps-historical-verdicts, existing) and a kind-4 one conses its own (fn-hls-finish-kind4-verdicts, existing).
proofs.progress_note: Open: no native run (no image was built on hbox for these bytes); a crash between the statement's kind-4 commit and the executor's kind-3 commit leaves the statement accepted and unexecuted (no model crash point, no recovery re-run); a refused kind-3 commit surfaces as the transit attempt's refusal after its kind-4 committed; fn_verify.py does not render :revoked; the served path (NNTP POST, BP transit) never reports :revoked by design (TRANSITP nil).

proofs.title: Invitation binding: accept enrols only a bound invitation; confirm consumes a pending invitation this node issued exactly once and enrols only the acceptance that consumed it
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-accept-step-enrols-only-a-bound-invitation: a (:enrol EVENT) from fn-pinv-accept-step SEQ TXID GEN RECEIVED OBSERVED-ML ED ML SNAPSHOTS (books/peer-invite.lisp; called by host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-accept) has EVENT = fn-hl-enroll-event at fn-hl-next-generation SNAPSHOTS of the carrier's principal P and key set K, P not already enrolled with K, and fn-pinv-bound-document-p: fn-hsig-authorize-at over the carrier decoded from RECEIVED and the two primitive observations, the body has the invitation kind line and names P, the Ed25519 and the ML-DSA-65 key of K (fn-pinv-body-names-p, a line of the body), and fn-prin-genesis-bindsp P (Ed25519 || ML-DSA-65) TOKEN. fn-pinv-issue-plan-records-the-signed-invitation: an :issue delta is fn-cfg-issue-invitation of the body's nonce, the verified principal and the invitation's authored-source identity, the nonce keying no row. fn-pinv-confirm-consumes-only-a-pending-named-invitation: a (:consume DELTA) from fn-pinv-confirm-plan (called by fnn-pinv-owner-confirm) has a bound acceptance, the row its nonce keys pending, naming the body's Inviter-Principal and Invitation-Source-Id, and DELTA = fn-cfg-consume-invitation of the nonce, the acceptor and the acceptance's source identity. fn-pinv-confirm-step-enrols-only-the-consuming-acceptance: an (:enrol EVENT) from fn-pinv-confirm-step (called by fnn-pinv-owner-enrol-confirmed) has a bound acceptance, the row consumed (state 1) by exactly its principal and source identity, P not enrolled with K, and EVENT the kind-3 enrolment of P and K. fn-pinv-consumed-stays-consumed-across-replay: a consumed invitation stays consumed through fn-config-replay-loop; fn-pinv-consumed-refuses-consumption: fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses every :consume-invitation of it; fn-pinv-consumption-consumes. fn-pinv-confirm-after-its-consumption-enrols: after the consuming delta is applied (the crash point before the kind-3 record) the same acceptance's plan is :enrol; fn-pinv-confirm-step-never-enrols-twice. Covered scope: the owner's three steps and the configuration admission and replay; the peer record is still `peer add`; the crypto primitives are A-CRYPTO.

proofs.title: The NEWNEWS pull feed advances its cursor past a round only when every listed Message-ID drew 235, 435 or 437 from the local node, and a crash mid-round recovers the cursor that round asked with
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp calls (fn-pull-begin, fn-pull-step through fn-pull-step-pair, fn-pull-close, fn-pull-replay over fn-pull-journal-scan): closing a round moves the cursor only if the round ran to its end and every Message-ID its NEWNEWS listed has a 235, 435 or 437 answer, the new instant being the peer's DATE less one second (fn-pull-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round; per id fn-pull-unanswered-id-holds-the-cursor); an answer is recorded only by a local reply and is that reply's own code for the article in hand (fn-pull-step-answers-only-from-the-local-node); no step changes the round's cursor or journals anything (fn-pull-step-keeps-the-cursor-and-journals-nothing) and every NEWNEWS it sends names the round's cursor instant (fn-pull-step-newnews-names-the-cursor); if the FNPL journal replays to the owner's cursor, it replays after the begin, after any events and after the close to that cut's cursor (fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut), so the round begun after a crash asks the dead round's instant (fn-pull-recovery-asks-the-dead-rounds-newnews). The schedule starts only a due, idle peer and spaces rounds by the operator's interval (fn-sched-pull-due-is-due-and-idle, fn-sched-pull-started-is-not-due, fn-sched-pull-finished-waits-its-interval). That the peer lists again what it listed for the same instant is RFC 3977 7.4's NEWNEWS semantics, not proved. Restated 2026-09-26 by PRF-165 (PKT-213): the cursor carries PENDING (per-id consecutive 430 counts) and fn-pull-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round / fn-pull-unanswered-id-holds-the-cursor now admit an id the peer answered 430 for BOUND consecutive complete rounds; PRF-165 states them.
proofs.progress_note: Native (hbox, SCN-058): a second fn node, INN 2.7.4 nnrpd and a SIGKILL mid-round then the same NEWNEWS all pass. Open: the pull client has no TLS arm (a TLS transport is not pulled); a remote 430 for a listed id holds the cursor until the peer stops listing it; the cursor lives in <store>/pull/*.fnpl (FNFD envelope and phase machine), not a Store transaction record.

proofs.title: The operator's configuration is ACL2's: [alerts]/[ops] rows, the rendered configuration, missions and their store profiles, the SIGHUP log reopen, and file-first on the bound commit route
proofs.statement: fn-native-config-show-round-trip: for every configuration C that fn-native-config-show-wfp admits, fn-native-config-load -- the loader fn-native-operator-run (host/native-operator-host.lisp:19) reads fn.toml through -- of fn-native-config-show-octets C, the text `operator CONFIG show' prints and a mission writes, is (:accepted C); the [alerts] and [ops] rows are part of C. fn-native-config-load-renderable: every configuration fn-native-config-load accepts satisfies fn-native-config-show-wfp (the parser's values are parsed-shaped and each field's normalization keeps its bound), so fn-native-config-show carries no run-time check; with the round trip, fn-native-config-loaded-show-round-trip: the rendering of every loaded configuration loads back as itself. fn-native-mission-profiles-valid and fn-native-mission-store-opens-with-its-profile: for each of small-community, relay and archive, the mission's profile request resolves to an admitted profile, and the frame `init' writes for it (fn-bs-config-frame-for-profile, host/store-host.lisp fn-store-metadata-config-frame) decodes at every later open to exactly that profile (under A-CRYPTO through fn-bs-config-decode-of-encode). fn-native-operator-run-init-under-a-mission: under a configuration naming a mission, an accepted init plan's profile is the mission's request. fn-olr-reopen-iff-requested: fn-olr-decide, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-log-reopen answers host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-maybe-reopen-log with, reopens exactly when a log path is configured and a SIGHUP arrived since the last one handled, and every counted request is then handled. fn-obc-commit-only-after-filing: fn-obc-commit-gate, which fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission asks (through fn-owner-bound-commit-gate) before any commit callback, answers :commit only when fn-pa-filing-plan files the article in exactly the committed groups; with C1's keystone a control article then commits only in its filing group (fn-obc-control-commits-only-in-its-filing-group). Covered scope: that the host calls the callback only on :commit, and swaps the log descriptor under the log mutex, is host code measured natively, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane operator-config, 2026-09-25: PKT-096, PKT-097, PKT-101, PKT-069.

proofs.title: BP outbound fragmentation: every fragment the send plan answers fits the peer's Transfer MRU, reassembles exactly to the parent's payload with no data cap, and restores the parent
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-bpfs-plan WIRE MRU (books/bp-fragment-send.lisp, logic mode, guard-verified), which host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-send-effect calls after SESS_INIT with the session's negotiated Transfer MTU (fn-tcl-negotiated-transfer-mtu). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-fit-mru: when the plan answers (:fragments W1 ... Wn), every Wi is at most MRU octets (the chunk is MRU minus 8 minus the encoded length of the empty fragment at the largest offset; fn-bpfs-fragment-length-bound over fn-bpfs-fragment-primary-length-shift and the payload block's exact length). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-exactly: the decoded views of the Wi draw the decoded parent's payload exactly on the reassembly canvas fn-bpf-canvas at the parent's ADU offset (0 for a whole parent, its own offset for a fragment parent) and all carry the parent's total, for every payload length and fragment count (no data cap). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-restore-parent: every Wi decodes to a bundle with the parent's extension blocks and ADU key and the fragment flag, and a whole parent's fragment primary unfragments to the parent's primary. fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-within-caps: for a whole parent of at most *fn-bpf-max-length* (65538) octets cut into at most *fn-bpf-max-fragments* (64) pieces, the receiver's executable reassembler fn-bpf-reassemble answers (:ok payload). Covered scope: the sender's base-job send path (bp-service run and the bp-node send of queued jobs through fnn-bps-send-effect); held-transit forwarding (the :session arm's MRU wait) does not fragment; the receiver's reassembler and held-row recognizers keep the 65538 x 64 caps; one job attempt covers all fragments (no per-fragment custody records); the plan runs on octet lists (no D27 concrete twin).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-n16-prod-2 (2026-09-25), PKT-061. Productionizes spike/bp's :program fn-bpfs-plan. Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-fragment-send-tests: witnesses at MRU 300 and 400 over a real 1000-octet bundle, a fragment parent at ADU offset 500 of 3000, a 70000-octet ADU (above the receiver cap) and a 100-fragment cut (above the fragment cap); must-fails for dropping the 8-octet head reserve, for each keystone without :fragments, and for each cap hypothesis of the within-caps corollary.

proofs.title: Peering composed: the confirm's one configuration record consumes the invitation and configures the peer; a declined key statement is decided at reopen under the configuration in force at its txid; the admission verdict names its class
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-confirm-record-configures-the-issued-invitations-peer: a (:configure DELTAS) from fn-pinv-confirm-record-plan RECEIVED INVITATION OBS ED ML INVITATIONS SNAPSHOTS PEERS (books/peer-invite.lisp; host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-confirm calls it through fn-pinv-host-confirm-record-plan) has fn-pinv-confirm-plan :consume, the row pending, the invitation of kind invitation whose authored-source identity is the row's, the confirmed peer fn-cfg-peerp with auth (:principal ACCEPTOR) and a name no peer of PEERS has, and DELTAS = (consume-delta, fn-cfg-set-peer-delta peer). fn-pinv-confirm-record-fold-consumes-and-configures: over fn-cfg-apply V GEN STAMP DELTAS (the fold fn-cfg-apply-record runs when the owner completes the publication) the invitation row is consumed by exactly this acceptor and acceptance source identity, the peers table holds exactly the peer's rows under its name, and (not enrolled) the next confirm plan is :enrol. fn-ks-reopen-is-blind-to-later-configuration and fn-ks-a-decline-replays-as-a-decline: fn-ks-recover-recorded (the open's recovery; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover with AT-OPEN, rows from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-rows = fn-ks-statement-rows with AT-OPEN; no policy switch) decides the pending statement under fn-ctl-config-at its own txid, so configuration records later than the statement change nothing, and a statement whose plan declined is left as the acceptance left it. fn-ks-recorded-recovery-completes-the-cut: when every configuration record precedes the txid and the journal replays, the recorded recovery of the cut is the uninterrupted acceptance under the live grants. fn-pcb-admission-verdict-names-its-class: the verdict is one of :unsigned :carried :malformed :cryptographically-invalid :unenrolled :unsupported-profile :verified; :verified iff the plan is :ok under both verified observations; :carried iff the D23 arm; a present carrier is never :unsigned. Not covered: pull over TLS (packet 8), the observation determinism the decline theorem assumes (A-CRYPTO), fn-pcb-admission-verdict has no host caller yet (its classes are the transit refusal detail's plus :carried/:verified).

proofs.title: A resend of an accepted source after its withdrawal or reclamation is answered from the Store (duplicate or conflict), never prepared as a fresh acceptance, and is served a 441 line
proofs.statement: Over the decision the host calls at POST (fn-rclb-existing-action, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt; fn-rcl-existing-action, fn-owner-existing-action from fnn-owner-attempt-transit): for a string Message-ID held in the Store's article list, both answer :duplicate or :conflict after fn-sn-finish of that Store, whatever the completed record (fn-vj-a-completion-keeps-a-held-message-id-answered; a cancel that withdraws the target is accepted by such a completion, and the owner's carried commit is fn-sn-finish by fn-ccar-sn-finish-is-sn-finish), and for any Store whose article list is fn-rcl-reclaim-state of an acceptance state holding it (fn-vj-reclamation-keeps-a-held-message-id-answered); while the resend is the connection's in-flight submission with no completion consumed, fn-own-outcome renders the duplicate or the conflict 441 line for it (fn-vj-a-held-message-id-is-answered-441). The host returns the word before fnn-advance-frontier and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, so no number is allocated (host control flow, observed natively, not a theorem). The same source being :duplicate rather than :conflict after reclamation is fn-rcl-existing-action-after-reclaim with its SHA-256 collision disjuncts.

proofs.title: The record producers the node runs stay inside the widths the profile admits, discharging the width hypothesis of fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record
proofs.statement: fn-sn-prepare-stages-a-narrow-article-record (books/record-width-producers.lisp): if CHARGE is at most 2^32 - 1 and fn-sn-prepare stages the record fn-sn-article-record builds (the result is not the input state), that record is not fn-record-widep: sequence, txid and generation are within u32 because the file machine stages only the reserved txid (frontier - 1), generation = txid and sequence = the committed count, and every file state holds a u32 frontier with strictly increasing committed txids below it (fn-sf-prepare-record-stages-u32-coordinates, fn-sn-prepare-stages-u32-coordinates); the stamp is below 2^32 by fn-record-stamp-of-observation (fn-sn-article-record-stamp-and-charge). The charge premise is discharged by the charge gate: fn-sbud-post-boundary answers :ok only for a u32 charge (fn-sbud-post-boundary-admits-a-u32-charge), and fn-post-admitted-article-record-is-within-r composes the boundary verdict :ok under PROFILE, the producer and the prepare into the conclusion of fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record: the staged record encodes within the profile's R, so the publish gate's record check (host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility, asserted by host/native/io.lisp fnn-publish) never refuses it. The BP ingress producer: fn-bpi-staged-record-is-narrow (policy charge u32 by fn-bpi-policy-p). Host calls: host/store-node-host.lisp and host/owner-host.lisp call fn-sn-article-record and then the prepare (fn-spc-prepare, equal to fn-sn-prepare by fn-spc-prepare-equals-specification-under-relation; fn-pcar-sbud-prepare, equal to fn-sbud-prepare by fn-pcar-sbud-prepare-is-sbud-prepare), after the boundary (host/native/io.lisp fnn-post-boundary; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-boundary); the boundary and the prepare are separate host calls, so the composition is over the host's order, stated, not one ACL2 function. Not covered: the signed composite (kind 4) and the peer-carried event producers, which carry their own R check (fn-owner-signed-event-boundary). Packet 1 (decided): the history gate charges an article its own figure, fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count (fn-sbud-article-figure, books/store-budget-article.lisp). fn-sbud-article-verdict-keeps-history: if fn-sbud-article-verdict-at PROFILE USED BYTES-USED PL GC is :admissible and RECORD is narrow with at most PL payload octets and GC groups, then fn-profile-replay-within-boundp PROFILE (+ BYTES-USED (len (fn-record-encode RECORD))): the bound the next open checks per file (host/native/io.lisp fnn-durable-records through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-replay-within-bound). Host: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict (native store post, before reservation). fn-sbud-prepare-under-article-budget-keeps-history: a fn-sbud-prepare that staged under fn-sbud-article-budget-for PROFILE BYTES-USED RECORD kept the history within H; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer pass that budget with the owner's carried committed octets (fn-owner-record-octets) to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare (= fn-sbud-prepare). fn-post-admitted-article-keeps-history composes the store-post sequence with PRF-123's keystone. fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-article-verdict: an upgrade keeps every article verdict (the figure does not read the profile).

proofs.title: One authored source, one identity: the host's tombstone-aware duplicate verdict keys on the poster's source at every clock, before and after reclamation
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-rcl-existing-action (books/store-reclaim.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action and fn-owner-prepare call, and fn-owner-existing-action-buffer through fn-rclb-existing-action (fn-rclb-existing-action-is-rcl-existing-action); host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt reaches them for the served POST and the operator post. fn-sr-an-injection-is-not-a-tombstone: no fn-inj-decide decision's octets are a tombstone (injected octets open with Path or Injection-, a refusal has none). fn-sr-a-retry-is-already-stored: the held payload is source S injected at clock A under Message-ID M and groups G; S injected at clock B under M and G is :duplicate. fn-sr-a-changed-source-is-a-conflict: a different source S2 under M is :conflict for any groups and clocks. fn-sr-the-tombstone-keeps-the-source: fn-rcl-tombstone-of of an injection is a tombstone whose source digest is SHA-256 of S, whose agent is the configured one and whose octet digest is SHA-256 of the injected octets. fn-sr-a-retry-after-reclaim-is-already-stored and fn-sr-a-changed-source-after-reclaim-is-a-conflict: the same two verdicts against the tombstone, the second up to a SHA-256 collision on the two sources (fn-rcl-collisionp, about 2^128 work, assumed not proved). The tombstone theorems are unreachable-in-composition until a program writes tombstones (store reclaim is not implemented). fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (PKT-166): the hybrid-author route's stored octets fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets, held at clock A, recomputed at any clock B under the same Message-ID and groups, are :duplicate; host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author asks fn-owner-existing-action before it commits.

proofs.title: The reader's search scope: the served XPAT reply over a range is XHDR's lines for exactly the served, matching numbers in it, and a withdrawn number is never a hit
proofs.statement: Over fn-nntp-step-pinned (books/nntp.lisp), which the served path reaches for every non-POST reader command (host/native/owner.lisp through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk, fn-served-step, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step-pinned, fn-nntp-post-step-pinned): fn-nntp-step-pinned-xpat-range-is-the-scope, for an open, well-formed, projected session with a selected group and a command line within the preflight whose keyword is XPAT, whose field is a header name or metadata item, whose second argument is a range and whose joined pattern parses, the step's result is fn-nntp-multi of the 221 initial line and fn-nntp-hdr-lines-for-numbers of the field over fn-nss-hits of the range's numbers in the served archive. fn-nss-hits-are-the-scope: a number is in that set iff it is positive, within the range's bounds, the group's served archive holds an available article at it, the field renders, and fn-nntp-xpat-matchesp accepts the rendered field. fn-nss-withdrawn-number-is-never-a-hit: a token the pinned step answers 423 withdrawn for (fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p) never names a hit, for any field, pattern or number list. tools/fn_web.py Backend.search and Backend.thread send exactly these commands and keep no index.
proofs.progress_note: Certified on hbox (planning/evidence/reader-daily-2026-09-25.md names the manifest); the native walk and tin session are in the same record.

proofs.title: Local-owner consumer poll and ack: a page is a read whose continuation never passes an unreturned matching event; ack writes only a forward in-scope declaration within the frontier, idempotently
proofs.statement: Subjects are the functions the host calls: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll calls fn-col-poll and fn-owner-consumer-local-ack calls fn-col-ack (books/consumer-owner-local), from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-consumer-local-serialized. fn-col-poll-scan-page-contract: for any event window, a :scan answer's continuation p is a natural with position <= p <= max(position, frontier) and p <= position + budget; an empty page's scanned prefix contains no group-matching article event and, when budget > 0 and position < frontier, p > position; a nonempty page's event is the window's event at p - 1 - position, it matches, and no earlier event in the window matches. fn-col-poll-is-the-index-window-scan-unfolds equates fn-col-poll's :poll answer with that selector over the carried index window (fn-col-poll-index-window), the continuation written into the owner-pinned scope cursor; fn-col-poll-is-a-page-or-a-refusal: it answers :poll or :refused, never a Store write proposal; fn-col-scope-entry-position-is-natural discharges the contract's natp premise. fn-col-ack-is-the-kernel-ack-unfolds equates fn-col-ack with fn-cp-ack under the pinned local principal, query version 1 and view 0. fn-cp-ack-writes-only-a-forward-declaration-in-scope: a :write is exactly (:ack cursor), in the recorded scope, not below the recorded position (nfix) and not equal to it, within the committed frontier; an in-scope equal position within the frontier is the :no-op. fn-cp-ack-after-its-commit-is-a-no-op: after fn-cp-apply of that ack, the same ack is a :no-op. Not claimed: that an acked position was served by a poll (an ack is a declaration), an unavailable gap (no native content reclamation reaches this profile), or independence of the byte and cursor ceilings.
proofs.progress_note: Lane consumer-e2 (2026-09-25), PKT-165 for the retaining-mode decision.

proofs.title: A ready base job is never starved by an older held or offered job on its contact, a transport result settles only its own attempt, a report or receipt is sent only by the durable record of its accepted transfer, and an encoder refusal settles its pending record
proofs.statement: fn-bpnj-step (books/bp-node-job-offer.lisp) is the step host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step calls; it equals fn-bpnp-step on every event but three (fn-bpnj-step-delegates-every-other-event). fn-bpnj-contact-next, asked before every base offer (fnn-bpc-drive-contact; fnn-bpnode-send-receipts), answers an offer while any queued job for the peer is ready (fn-bpnj-contact-offers-while-a-ready-job-remains), and the offer's event persists exactly that job's :attempting record with the :cl-send of its durable route (fn-bpnj-contact-offer-starts-the-ready-job). A transfer result names its attempt token: another token settles nothing (fn-bpnj-stale-job-result-settles-nothing), the current one proposes :finished for :accepted and :requeued otherwise (fn-bpnj-named-result-is-the-transport-outcome), and :forwarded is reported only at the durable answer to a pending :finished record of an :attempting job (fn-bpnj-step-forwarded-needs-a-durable-finished-record), so a queued report intent or job is not a sent one. A :refused answer settles the pending record (fn-bpnj-encoder-refusal-settles-the-pending-record). The new arms keep the guard premises and the lifecycle invariant (fn-bpnj-step-preserves-guard-premises, fn-bpnj-new-arms-preserve-the-lifecycle-invariant). Under A-BP-CONTACT the host's first ask is an offer and the contact offers a ready job within its prefix of keys at or ahead of it (fn-bpnj-contact-offers-a-ready-job-under-a-bp-contact). Covered scope: base FNBS jobs (requests, receipts, status reports); the held-bundle forwarding path (kind 8) keeps its own session scan and stale-callback handling (fn-bpnp-forward-result-*). Not covered: token monotonicity across every served event and restart; freedom of :finished proposals on non-base events.

proofs.title: Pull over TLS as the node's own principal: the feed's protected preamble gates the pull round, a clear credential without the loopback-lab exception is refused before any dial, and the cursor's cut theorem transfers
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls (fn-pull-plan-profile-path, fn-pull-session-begin through fn-pull-session-begin-pair, fn-pull-session-step through fn-pull-session-step-pair, fn-pull-session-close-effects, fn-pull-session-close; books/peer-pull-session.lisp) and the plans host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-pull-plans reads (fn-pull-plans, now carrying the transport security and the outbound credential policy). fn-pull-session-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login: for a plan whose fn-pull-plan-verdict is :tls, the feed-connection observations of the session driven by ANY host events (fn-pull-session-obs, which is fn-fc-drive of the session's initial machine over the events it fed: fn-pull-session-obs-is-the-machine-over-its-trace) satisfy fn-fc-gate-okp from the start stage -- PRF-051's fn-fc-offers-and-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login instantiated, not restated: no AUTHINFO before a 382 and the host's verified-TLS report, no :ready (the only transition that sends DATE and lets the round step) before a 281 when a credential is carried. fn-pull-session-refuses-a-clear-credential-without-the-lab-exception: a clear transport with a credential, without both the profile's explicit clear-text permission and a loopback host literal, has verdict :refused-clear-credential, no profile path (the secret is not read), begin effects exactly the cursor's journal record and (:close) (no :dial), a session that answers every later event with nothing, and a close equal to the cursor fn-pull-begin asks with. fn-pull-begin-ready-is-the-round-after-the-greeting: the round a session enters at :ready is the round fn-pull-begin reaches on a 200/201 greeting, sending the same DATE; fn-pull-begin-ready-cursor-fields. fn-pull-session-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut: PRF-100's fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut (statement unchanged) transferred to the session: after the begin, after any events (the TLS preamble included) and after the close records, the FNPL journal replays to that cut's cursor. Trusted, not proved (A-HOST, as PRF-051): the host reports (:tls-up) only after fnn-tls-connect verified the chain against the plan's trust anchor and the plan's server name; the loopback-lab exception is a local policy for the lab, never a general secure-peering claim.

proofs.title: BP fragment reassembly without a family-size ceiling: the executed reassembler equals the uncapped index-wise reference on every input, in work linear in the octets received, and the node's family query and selector run it
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-bpfw-reassemble FS TOTAL (books/bp-fragment-sweep.lisp, logic mode, guard t, guard-verified): a merge sort of the fragments by offset, then one tail-recursive sweep over positions 0..TOTAL-1 keeping only the suffixes of the extents covering each position, then the reference's outcome scan. The node's fn-bpnf-fragment-query (books/bp-node-fragment-family.lisp) calls it; fn-bpnf-family-plan calls the query; fn-bpnf-family-next, which host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-fragment-progress calls through fnn-core, selects the family, and the host then steps (:family arrival observation) through fnn-bps-foundation-step. fn-bpfw-reassemble-is-spec: for every FS and TOTAL, fn-bpfw-reassemble equals fn-bpfw-spec, the reference fn-bpf-reassemble's own definition with *fn-bpf-max-length* (65538) and *fn-bpf-max-fragments* (64) removed from its input recognizer (fn-bpfw-inputsp: well-formed fragments, a positive total, one total for all). fn-bpf-reassemble-is-capped-spec: fn-bpf-reassemble equals fn-bpfw-spec when TOTAL <= 65538 and (len FS) <= 64, and (:invalid :bounds) otherwise. fn-bpfw-exact-canvas-reassembles: under fn-bpfw-inputsp, a family whose index-wise canvas is an octet list reassembles to (:ok canvas). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-uncapped: for the sender's plan fn-bpfs-plan of a whole parent answering :fragments, fn-bpfw-reassemble of the fragments' views answers (:ok payload) for every payload length and fragment count. fn-bpnf-fragment-query-is-reference (restated): the node query equals fn-bpfw-spec over the family's cells. fn-bpnf-family-next-memo-is-aux: the executed selector (the :exec branch of fn-bpnf-family-next), which plans each family at most once per call, equals the per-member selector (anchor included) under its invariant, established with an empty tried list at the call. Scope: the reassembler has no data ceiling, but a family is still bounded upstream by the held-image cap *fn-bpnf-max-held-image*, the bundle decoder's 1 MiB input, the ADU record's 65538 octets and the machine's slots and octet budget (P5 of planning/design-2026-09-25-bounds.md); the representation is octet lists (no D27 concrete twin); the merge in the sort recurses to the fragment count. Jobs (books/bp-node-fragment-jobs.lisp): fn-bpnf-family-jobs-agreep HELD says every active fragment row carries exactly the reassembly job (job state (:dispatch-pending), no dispatch record, no next hop, no kind-8 attempt). fn-bpnf-family-apply-conserves-jobs: under it, a :ready kind-18 application (the one rule live completion and replay call) consumes only rows whose one job was reassembly, installs a whole row carrying (:dispatch-pending), and the new held list satisfies the relation. fn-bpnp-step-family-events-keep-jobs-agreeing: fn-bpnp-step (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step) on (:family A OBS) and on (:persist-result EPOCH OP RESULT) while a kind-18 operation is issued preserves the relation through every wrapper of the served step. Established by the empty held list of a cold start (fn-bpnf-family-jobs-agree-when-empty); preservation over recovery replay and over the dispatch, forward, delivery and deletion arms is not proved (open).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-lifecycle (2026-09-25, wave 2), PKT-171. Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-fragment-sweep-tests (a 70000-octet ADU in 100 fragments, out of order and overlapping, every outcome against the spec, one witness per hypothesis of fn-bpfw-exact-canvas-reassembles) and tests/acl2/bp-fragment-send-tests (the 100-fragment and 70000-octet plans the capped reference refuses; a must-fail per hypothesis). Native: tests/test_bp_fragment_node_native test_seventy_fragments_across_a_kill_reassemble_once. See the record for the manifest and native SHAs.

proofs.title: The reclaiming pack `store reclaim` publishes rewrites only unheld legacy article records to their tombstones, stays a pack, converges, and frees exactly the octets admission counts
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-rclp-decide (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-reclaim-decide, called by host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-reclaim-observe). fn-rclp-decide-publishes-the-rewrite: when the answer is :reclaim, its steps are *fn-rclp-steps*, dry is nil, the history is one selected pack (lower = len records), some record is rewritten, and the published summary octets are fn-cc-encode of the fn-cc-capture of fn-rclp-events of the committed records. fn-rclp-events-keep-the-summary-shape: fn-cc-octet-event-listp of the rewrite equals fn-cc-octet-event-listp of the history, for every sequence, lower and upper, no hypothesis. fn-rclp-event-decodes-to-the-tombstoned-record: a rewritten event decodes to the record with every field equal but the payload, which is fn-rcl-tombstone-of the old payload, and the charge, which is the history unit *fn-rclp-history-unit* (1). fn-rclp-rewritten-charge-is-the-history-unit: the charge a rewritten event carries into the ledger is the history unit, an unrewritten event carries its own; fn-rclp-freed-charge-account sums the released charge over the list. fn-rclp-events-never-touch-a-held-article: if the I-th event's record's article is named by an obligation of fn-rcl-obligations h, or its verdict needs its payload (fn-rcl-verdict-heldp), or the rule is keep-forever, the I-th event is byte-identical. fn-rclp-events-keep-every-other-kind: an event that does not decode as a legacy record (accepted-statement composites and every other kind) is byte-identical. fn-rclp-a-reclaimed-event-stays-reclaimed: a rewritten event is not rewritten again under any context; fn-rclp-events-idempotent under the same context. fn-rclp-freed-is-the-admission-count: for a rewritten event the fn-store-event-encode lengths the admission gate sums (fn-sbud-record-octets) fall by exactly the event's length less its replacement's; fn-rclp-freed-octets-account sums it over the list. fn-rclp-keep-forever-writes-nothing: under keep-forever the answer is never :reclaim. The operator keystones: `store reclaim` and `store reclaim --dry-run` are exactly the :reclaim and :reclaim-dry-run native actions.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the replay correspondence of the reclaimed record (the open of the reclaiming pack equals fn-rcl-reclaim-state of the open of the history: PRF-088's own open step); guard verification of books/store-reclaim-pack (all :verify-guards nil, called through a :program host wrapper); holders from feed state, FNBS rows and BP obligations are not read (the BP journal is a separate namespace; the offline verb reads the Store's consumer projection only); chained packs for N above one pack (4,096 events, 4 MiB). Lane reclaim-lifecycle-2 (2026-09-26): PKT-169 retired by PRF-129 (fn-smr-admission-keeps-the-reserve, fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-disk); the retention charge falls to the history unit on reclaim (fn-rclp-rewritten-charge-is-the-history-unit).

proofs.title: The operator's health verdict: eight states, each decided by the status report's sources, one line and one exit code each
proofs.statement: Over fn-nh-verdict (books/native-health.lisp), which fn-nh-offline-report, fn-nh-fenced-report and fn-nh-live-report render and host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-health-host-offline, fn-native-health-host-fenced and fn-native-live-status-host-answer call (host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-health-report; host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer): fn-nh-verdict-states, the verdict has eight outcomes in *fn-nh-states* order, each :held, :clear or :unobserved exactly as the report's sources decide: fenced from the host's fence observation; exhausted from the headroom at the transaction-id or ledger codec ceiling; unqualified-profile from fn-bs-profile-validp and the development profile; space-pressure from free headroom below the operator's [alerts] headroom_min_percent on transactions, history octets or retention charge, when not exhausted; no-route from held :forward obligations with an empty fn-bprt-table; stranded-transfer from feed entries dropped at their retry bound; unavailable-peer from feeds with pending work and no connection; receipt-debt from held :forward obligations; a source not observed is :unobserved. fn-nh-exit-code-decodes: the exit code names the first held state (fn-nh-code-state) and is 0 exactly when no state is held or unobserved. fn-nh-report-exit-of-render: the code the host returns, read back from the rendered octets by fn-nh-report-exit (fn-native-health-host-exit, fnn-operator-execute-health), is the verdict's code for every verdict of at most eight outcomes. fn-nh-first-held-monotone: a verdict holding every state another holds has a first held state no later. fn-nh-pressedp-monotone: more use or a higher threshold never clears pressure. fn-nh-live-report-is-the-store-report: with the carried octet sum valid, the owner's report is the verdict over its Store's own committed octets, configuration and feed table. fn-nh-fence-of-route: an uncertain control-socket route is always fenced; otherwise the clone fence and the lock decide.

proofs.title: Every record a producer can stage is within the profile's R at any sequence, transaction ID, generation and stamp width, and the frontier frame carries u64 with every format-2 frame read unchanged
proofs.statement: fn-record-encode-producer-length-bound (books/records-seam.lisp, the seam constraint discharged by fn-record-impl-encode-producer-length-bound in books/records-canonicality.lisp and by both attachments): if a record's charge is at most 2^32 - 1, its encoding is at most fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count -- the 1 083-octet ceiling every saved profile's R was checked against -- whatever the width of its sequence, transaction ID, generation and stamp (the ceiling counts five-octet heads for the schema octet, the group count, the Message-ID, the three metadata strings and every group name, which encode at least 17 octets shorter; four eight-octet heads need 16). fn-bs-profile-admits-every-producer-record (books/record-width-producers.lisp): under an admitted profile such a record within A and G encodes within R, with no narrowness premise (PRF-086's fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record is the narrow case). fn-sn-prepare-stages-an-article-record-within-its-ceiling: a record fn-sn-prepare stages from fn-sn-article-record with a u32 charge is within the ceiling of its own payload and groups; fn-bpi-staged-record-fits-the-producer-ceiling: the same for the BP ingress producer (policy charge u32). fn-sbud-article-verdict-keeps-history-at-producer-width and fn-sbud-prepare-under-article-budget-keeps-history-at-producer-width (books/store-budget-article.lisp): an article admitted by the article verdict (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict) or staged under the served budget (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare -> fn-sbud-article-budget-for) keeps the committed history within H at any producer width. Frontier format 3 (books/byte-store-frame.lisp): fn-bs-frontier-impl-round-trip over every n <= 2^64 - 1 (the host's fn-store-metadata-frontier-frame/-decode through the scan seam's attachment), and fn-bs-frontier-decode-extends-format-2: every octet string the frozen format-2 reader fn-bs-frontier-v2-decode accepts, the format-3 reader fn-bs-frontier-decode-impl reads to the same transaction ID, so every saved frontier file opens unchanged. The allocator's successor fn-bs-frontier-next still stops at 2^32 - 1: the file machine (fn-sf-statep), the observed open (fn-sn-open-observed), the checkpoint (fn-checkpointp, fn-checkpoint-restore) and its TREE naturals (fn-cpc-treep) and the consumer candidate bound read u32, which is PKT-244.
proofs.progress_note: Certified with teeth (persvati, w25, 2 jobs, 300 s): run-20260926T010201Z-edf7 (certify-20260926T010233Z-3422722: 562 of 565 passed; the three reds were this lane's test books, fixed in 9104f415) and run-20260926T011811Z-b295 (certify-20260926T011837Z-3569115: those three passed). Native served-POST gate on the a9ed4dc2 developer image (SCN-072). The allocator past 2^32 - 1 and the stamp past 2106 wait on PKT-244.

proofs.title: The operator walk: no store is a refusal (exit 6) before any open, a MODE STREAM refusal stops the dial, and a snapshot rollback's loss is counted
proofs.statement: Over fn-native-operator-store-outcome (books/native-operator.lisp), which host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-store-outcome calls through fn-native-operator-host-store-outcome on every accepted plan before fnn-operator-dispatch-plan executes it: fn-native-operator-absent-store-is-refused, an accepted plan whose native action opens a store (fn-native-operator-result-needs-storep), over an observation that found none of *fn-nop-store-markers* beside the configured root, is refused with reason :no-store, exit code 6 (*fn-nop-no-store-exit*) and native action :none, so no open is attempted and the outcome is never the fault code 4; fn-native-operator-store-outcome-passes-a-present-store, with any marker observed or a plan that needs no store the plan passes unchanged. Over fn-fc-step, fn-fc-streaming-refusal-p and fn-fc-dial-allowedp (books/feed-connection.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-reply-chunk and fn-owner-feed-has-queued call (host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-reply-step, fnn-feed-dial-plan): fn-fc-mode-stream-refusal-stops-the-dial, a complete peer line other than 203 in the :mode phase (RFC 4644 section 2.3) is a refusal that closes the connection, is classified as a streaming refusal, and once the owner records the peer with :mode-stream-refused the dial is not allowed for that peer whatever it has queued; fn-fc-dial-allowedp-of-put-other, other peers keep their dial. Over fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss: fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss-counts-the-suffix, :loses exactly when the first list is an element-wise prefix of the second, and the count is the number of elements after it. Until 2026-09-26 the host handed it (sequence . file length) descriptors, which is not a history comparison (gpt-6's answers section 7); the verb's history claim is PRF-141, over exact committed records, and this lemma is the list-level function PRF-141's fold equals.
