proofs.title: Admission keeps the maintenance reservation (one release record) and maintenance's temporary space is checked against the disk
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-smr-verdict-at (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-publication-verdict, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-preflight-publication for every non-article Store record: retention, identity, consumer and topic events, BP admission's included; and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-publication-verdict), fn-smr-article-budget-for (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, the served POST and BP transit prepares, handed to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare), fn-smr-article-verdict-at (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict, the developer store post), fn-cverb-decide (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-compact-decide) and fn-rclp-decide (fn-store-reclaim-decide). The reservation fn-smr-roomp profile used bytes is (fn-sbud-verdict-at profile :release used bytes) = :admissible. fn-smr-admission-keeps-the-reserve: if fn-smr-verdict-at admits a record of kind K /= :release at (used, bytes) and octets is a natural at most K's publication ceiling, fn-smr-roomp holds at (used+1, bytes+octets). fn-smr-prepare-keeps-the-reserve: if fn-sbud-prepare with budget fn-smr-article-budget-for (profile, the prepare's committed count, bytes, record) changed the configured owner and the record is narrow, fn-smr-roomp holds at (count+1, bytes + len (fn-record-encode record)) and the history is within H. fn-smr-article-verdict-keeps-the-reserve: the same for fn-smr-article-verdict-at and a narrow record within the asked counts. fn-smr-reserve-admits-the-release: where the reservation holds, fn-smr-verdict-at admits :release. fn-smr-admission-is-within-the-profile: every admission passes fn-sbud-verdict-at. fn-smr-roomp-antitone-in-octets and fn-smr-roomp-is-within-the-bound. fn-smr-admitted-profile-starts-reserved: an admitted profile holds the reservation at (0, 0). fn-smr-profile-upgrade-keeps-the-reserve. fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-disk: a :compact pack decision implies the sealed next link of the chain (fn-ccc-encode-link of fn-ccc-capture-link above the chain boundary, plus frame trailer, for every lower frontier, predecessor generation and digest) is at most the host-observed free octets, which the host observes again before every link (pack-chain-join); fn-rclp-pack-fits-the-disk: the same for a :reclaim answer's summary octets.
proofs.progress_note: Lane reclaim-lifecycle-2 (2026-09-26). Open: the free-octet observation is the host's statvfs, an environmental fact not modelled (a concurrent writer can take the space between the observation and the write; the write then fails before the selection, which the pack publication cuts cover). The BP namespace's own reservation is the FNBS debt cover (books/bp-node-debt.lisp), not restated here. Every book under 10 s.

proofs.title: A relay takes custody only over an admitted channel: a bundle whose channel admission was refused is refused at reception with the admission's reason, before any FNBS step
proofs.statement: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-receive calls fn-bpaj-admitted-receive-event (books/bp-channel-ingress.lisp) with the admission answer of fnn-bps-tcpcl-admission (fn-owner-bp-tcpcl-ingress, i.e. fn-bpaj-tcpcl-ingress-result over the live owner configuration) and hands fnn-bps-foundation-step only its :ready answer. fn-bpaj-refused-channel-takes-no-custody: when the admission answer is not :admitted, the answer is exactly (:refused REASON) with the admission's own reason (fn-bpaj-channel-refusal-reason) and is not :ready, so no kind-5 custody row is proposed and hence no forwarding job, :attempting record, fragment family or owed receipt follows from that bundle. fn-bpaj-admitted-channel-receives-under-its-ingress: an admitted channel's answer is fn-bpnf-receive-wire-event under the admitted ingress, whose principal is the policy's selection (fn-bpaj-admitted-ingress-binds-announcement-and-selection). D23 (planning/decisions.md), mandate section 4 'Offline forwarding'; retires PKT-170.

proofs.title: The payload arena abstracts to the list of sealed payloads; a sealed handle is immutable and never reused; commit and open establish the same relation with the history
proofs.statement: fn-arena (books/payload-arena.lisp) is an abstract stobj whose logical value is the list of sealed payloads, oldest first (fn-arn-payload-listp), and whose executable is one resizable (unsigned-byte 8) array holding every payload back to back with an offset and a size per handle. The abstraction relation fn-arena$corr (the concrete object well formed, the fill and the count within their arrays, every handle's range below the fill, and the slices in handle order the logical list) is established by the creator and preserved by every export (the {correspondence}, {preserved} and {guard-thm} obligations, stated as defabsstobj-missing-events prints them and proved before the defabsstobj). fn-arena-seal-buffer{correspondence}: copying the octet buffer's cells in place at the fill and recording the range as the next handle corresponds to append of the buffer's value, an export taking a second stobj. KEYSTONES: fn-arena-seal-keeps-sealed and fn-arena-seals-keep-sealed say a handle that is a natural below the count reads the same octets after one seal and after any sequence of seals; fn-arena-seal-new-handle and fn-arena-seal-count say a seal's new handle is the old count, denotes the sealed octets, and the count grows by one (no hypothesis). fn-arn-store-corr (the arena is the history's payloads oldest first, fn-arn-payloads-of over fn-sf-records' commit order) is kept by a commit's seal (fn-arn-store-corr-of-commit) and established by an open's seals from the empty arena (fn-arn-store-corr-of-open, no hypothesis). Every executable function is guard-verified. No host entry calls the arena yet: the record's payload field must become a handle first (planning/evidence/rep-wave-d-2026-09-25.md section 3), so the subject is the base of that program, not a served path.
proofs.progress_note: Lane rep-wave-d (2026-09-25): the arena and its theorems certified on persvati (run-20260926T002605Z-febf, 1.17 s and 0.77 s at two jobs). The host join (the seal at the served POST's finish, the handle in the record) is the model change of the record's payload field, a coordinated freeze the record's section 3 lays out; until it lands the served path holds the list and no representation improvement is claimed.

proofs.title: A BP verb's run class is ACL2's, with one exit code per class; a BP node's held rows and held octets are the operator's profile, a saved profile opens, and replay past the profile is refused by name, never truncated
proofs.statement: Part 1 (books/bp-run-class.lisp, books/bp-node-run-class.lisp). The host records evidence with fn-bprc-note: the reason of each (:forward-refused W A G REASON) effect through fn-bprc-effect-evidence (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-drive-effects, :process scope), each TCPCL session's outcome and fence flag through fn-bprc-session-evidence (host/native/bp.lisp fnn-bp-exit-code, fnn-bp-session-word), each publication classification through fn-bprc-publication-evidence, and the article verdicts its tally counted through fn-bprc-with-articles; it renders fn-bprc-run-exit-code (fnn-bps-exit-code, fnn-bp-exit-code, the bp-node serve result) and, for every fnn-store-indeterminate, the fenced code (fnn-bp-verb). fn-bprc-exit-code-separates-the-classes: the five classes :accepted 0, :refused 1, :fenced 3, :interrupted 6, :not-connected 7 answer five codes. fn-bprc-fence-is-never-masked: once :fenced is recorded, whatever was recorded before or after, the class is :fenced. fn-bprc-connection-local-never-fences: from the empty record, words among :failed, :uncertain, :refused, :accepted and nil never make the class :fenced. fn-bprc-uncertain-article-fences. fn-bpnrc-job-result-class-is-the-transport-class: under PRF-120's hypotheses (fn-bpnj-named-result-is-the-transport-outcome), the class of the effects of the durable answer to a named job result is fn-bprc-transfer-class of its outcome: :accepted, :refused, :interrupted for :uncertain, :not-connected otherwise. Part 2 (books/bp-node-profile.lisp, books/bp-node-profile-replay.lisp). fnn-bps-open reads bp-node-profile through fn-bpnpf-read and opens the machine with fn-bpnf-initial-state under its rows and octets. fn-bpnpf-read-of-octets: for every profile fn-bpnpf-validp admits (each field a machine limit, 1..2^24), the file's octets read back as exactly that profile. fn-bpnpf-valid-profile-opens: every valid profile opens a machine whose max-jobs and max-octets are the profile's. fn-bpnpf-write-never-lowers: bp-node profile publishes only a profile that raises or keeps every field. fn-bpnpf-replay-past-the-profile-is-refused: after any prefix that replays :ready to a held list the profile has filled, a well-formed received row makes fn-bpnf-family-replay-rows-aux over the whole journal answer (:fault :held-beyond-profile). Scope: the ADU, bundle-decoder and held-image ceilings are still constants (PKT-276); the Store profile's max-bp-rows is not read; the class does not yet separate expiry, no-route, busy delivery or a clock-domain change (PKT-276).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-lifecycle-3 (2026-09-26, wave 2), PKT-276. Teeth: tests/acl2/bp-run-class-tests (the five codes; a must-fail per hypothesis of the separation; the fence among mixed evidence; the class of each outcome over the reachable attempting state of PRF-120's teeth, the stale attempt and the pending state as hypothesis removals), tests/acl2/bp-node-host-tests (the mixed article/session cases), tests/acl2/bp-node-profile-tests (the 128-row profile round trip, a zero-row and a 2^24+1-row profile, a configuration-less open, a lowering write refused, replay of two durable kind-5 rows under one row of profile answering :held-beyond-profile and under two :ready). Native: the six BP modules' expectations and SCN-067 under a 128-row profile; see the record.

proofs.title: The BP receiver binds a signed article its Store committed and never submits it a second time: the first durable commit is the only submission, and the verdict the delivery is bound to is the receiving Store's own
proofs.statement: host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-request-action calls fn-bpaj-dispatch-fast (books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp) over the owner's bound Store for host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-action, before every step of fnn-bpapp-accept-locked; host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install and fn-owner-app-record call the lookup it uses, fn-bpaj-transit-record-lookup-fast. A signed article is committed as a kind-4 composite (fn-stxa-p) carrying the article record and the receiving Store's kind-2 verdict; the Store binding now reads a history's article records (fn-bpr-article-records, books/bp-receipt.lisp: a plain record, or the record a composite carries, as replay installs it). Both keystones are stated over the Store the host dispatches over (books/owner-store-indexed.lisp, fn-osi-live-store: the Store of the owner host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended installs, after any sequence of the owners the host installs), with no index premise: fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed (PRF-144) discharges it; the -under-index lemmas of books/bp-signed-binding.lisp are the refinement layer. fn-bpaj-dispatch-never-resubmits-a-stored-article: when the live Store's article records contain an article record whose Message-ID is the one the dispatcher reads (fn-bpaj-dispatch-msgid: the relaying agent's check for a transit intent), the dispatcher does not answer (:submit). fn-bpaj-dispatch-binds-the-stores-own-record: a (:bind RECORD) answer names an article record for that Message-ID, accepted by the receiver's Store check, that is the article record of an event of the Store's own history, and when that event is a signed composite the composite binds its verdict to exactly RECORD (fn-stxa-bindsp). The request carries no verdict. Cites PRF-128 (the channel is admitted first), PRF-127 (relaying keeps the authored source), PRF-117 (the D23 source decision) and PRF-026 (a kind-4 completion records its verdict); D23, D25. Retires PKT-247.
proofs.progress_note: CHANGED 2026-09-26 (PRF-144, lanes signed-history-index and signed-history-index-2): the dispatcher's lookups read the Store's Message-ID index; the keystones are stated over the live owner's Store, where the index relation is a theorem (fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed), not a hypothesis.

proofs.title: Relaying cannot change who wrote an article: the stored transit projection keeps fn-hc-authored-source on the NNTP and BP routes
proofs.statement: fn-rs-authored-source-is-the-walk (books/relay-source.lisp): for every octet list the parser accepts, fn-hc-authored-source of the parsed article equals fn-rs-source-walk (the reserved-field line walk) of fn-pu-strip of the octets, so the authored source is a function of the octets with Path and Xref stripped. fn-rs-relaying-keeps-the-authored-source (books/relay-source-routes.lisp): when the parser accepts both OCTETS and fn-peer-relayed-octets CFG PEER OCTETS, their authored sources are equal (with fn-peer-relayed-octets-change-only-path-and-xref). fn-rs-a-transfer-is-wanted-only-if-both-parse: fn-peer-decide-transfer answers :want only when both parse. fn-rs-a-wanted-transfer-keeps-the-authored-source: on :want, the payload fn-peer-injection-arguments stages (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take through fn-peer-transfer) parses and has the received article's authored source. fn-rs-a-bp-transit-keeps-the-authored-source: when fn-bpaj-transit-plan (host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install) answers :submit, the request's article and fn-bpaj-transit-stored-octets both parse and have the same authored source. No hypothesis beyond the host's own decision on the two route keystones. Scope: bytes, not signatures (PRF-117 and books/injection-path.lisp own A's injection).

proofs.title: The state checkpoint's file octets, written as a plan over the octet buffer, are the octets the list codec specified
proofs.statement: books/store-checkpoint-buffer.lisp. fn-sccb-plan (the host-called entry: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sco-publish-plan, called by host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-state-checkpoint, the `store checkpoint' verb) writes the checkpoint value's postfix program forward into the octet buffer once (fn-sccb-renc) and returns a plan of (HEADER A B TRAILER) per FNSC segment. KEYSTONE fn-sccb-plan-is-file-octets: (implies (fn-sccb-treep c) (equal (fn-sccb-plan-octets (mv-nth 0 (fn-sccb-plan c seg st)) (mv-nth 1 (fn-sccb-plan c seg st))) (fn-scc-file-octets c seg))): the plan's octets over the buffer it leaves (the header, the buffer's cells A..B and the trailer, per frame: fn-sccb-plan-octets, which host/native/io.lisp fnn-plan-octets transcribes) are fn-scc-file-octets of the same value and segment size, so the file on disk is the file the list codec specified and the reader (fn-scc-decode-segments) is untouched. fn-sccb-renc-is-program: the writer is append of fn-scc-program with no hypothesis. fn-sccb-plan-refuses-what-the-codec-refuses: where the list codec answered :unencodable the plan does. fn-sccb-treep-encodes-octets: fn-sccb-treep (fn-scc-treep with every leaf's octets octets) is exactly the domain whose file is octets; the plan refuses the tree whose length needs 256 digits, which the list codec encoded to a list the host's byte vector could not hold. Every executable function is guard-verified. What it does not say: anything about the reader, or that the host writes the plan's octets (A-HOST, as for every buffer boundary).
proofs.progress_note: Lane rep-wave-d-2 (2026-09-26): certified on persvati (run-20260926T035337Z-d860, no book over 10 s at two jobs; run 1 found the book at 20.2 s and the leaf codecs were closed in the hints; run 2 preceded the accumulator forms that the stack exhaustion on hbox demanded). The id was assigned by the brief to the records-shape freeze's correspondence theorems; that freeze did not start (its interface needs PKT-293), and the lane's one certified keystone is registered here; the coordinator renumbers at merge if it prefers.

proofs.title: A BP node's ADU octets and bundle octets are the operator's profile, the held image's bound is its held octets, and the ADU, bundle and held-image codecs are widths that never cap below a profile
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-profile.lisp: profile 2 is (ROWS OCTETS ADU BUNDLE), each a machine limit (1..2^24). fnn-bps-open reads bp-node-profile through fn-bpnpf-profile-read. fn-bpnpf-profile-read-of-octets: every valid profile 2 written by fn-bpnpf-profile-octets reads back as exactly itself. fn-bpnpf-profile-read-of-format-1: a format-1 frame of a valid (ROWS OCTETS) reads as (ROWS OCTETS 65538 1048576), and no file is the default. fn-bpnpf-profile-read-is-valid. fn-bpnpf-profile-write-never-lowers: a write bp-node profile publishes (fn-bpnpf-profile-write-octets) reads back as written and raises or keeps each of the four fields. books/bp-node-profile-admission.lisp: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-receive calls fn-bpnpf-admitted-receive-event with the profile in force. fn-bpnpf-admission-within-profile-is-the-channel-answer: with a valid profile, a wire within the bundle octets and (if :ready) a bundle whose ADU (a fragment's total ADU length) is within the ADU octets, the answer is fn-bpaj-admitted-receive-event's (PRF-128). fn-bpnpf-admission-ready-is-within-profile: a :ready answer has a valid profile, a wire within its bundle octets, an ADU within its ADU octets, and is the channel answer. fn-bpnpf-admission-refuses-beyond-the-profile: on an admitted channel, a wire past the bundle octets is (:refused :bundle-beyond-profile) and a :ready bundle whose ADU is past the ADU octets is (:refused :adu-beyond-profile). fn-bpnpf-profile-within-codec-widths: every profile field is within its codec's width (*fn-bpa-max-octets*, *fn-bpb-max-data*, *fn-bpb-max-input*, *fn-bpnf-max-held-image* = 2^24; *fn-bpn-lifecycle-max-payload* = 2^24 + 3072). books/bp-node-profile-replay.lisp: fn-bpnpf-replay-past-the-octets-is-refused: after any prefix replaying :ready, a well-formed received row whose image does not fit the profile's held octets beside the held rows makes fn-bpnf-family-replay-rows-aux over the whole journal (:fault :held-beyond-profile). books/bp-adu.lisp: the ADU's fields are record items (fn-record-item-encode: the generic CBOR bytes at or below 65,535 octets), the article width is *fn-bpa-max-article* = 2^24 - 2106, and fn-bpa-round-trip and fn-bpa-encoding-bound hold at that width (their statements unchanged). books/bp-limits.lisp: fn-bpn-limits-compose-at-the-codec-widths replaces fn-bpn-limits-compose. fn-bpfw-reassemble-is-spec (PRF-121) is unchanged. Scope: the sender machine's job image stays the plain :blob (131,072); decoding a held family image at replay is one step linear in its octets, not a resumable quantum (PKT-294).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-lifecycle-4 (2026-09-26, wave 2), PKT-276's codec items, PKT-294. See the record.

proofs.title: The state checkpoint read from the octet buffer decodes to the value the list decoder gives: the buffer decode of the writer's plan is the value, and on any plan it is the list decode of the frames' octets
proofs.statement: books/store-checkpoint-reader.lisp. fn-sccr-decode-plan (the host-called entry: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sco-decode, called by host/native/io.lisp fnn-state-checkpoint-load at the store's open after fnn-state-checkpoint-plan has read the file's chunks into the octet buffer) reads a plan of (HEADER A B TRAILER) per FNSC segment, the chunk as the buffer's cells A..B, and decodes the postfix program by index (fn-sccr-run, the stack machine reading the buffer; a payload leaf is fn-sccb-slice-acc of its range, the record's own octet list, built once). KEYSTONE fn-sccr-decode-of-plan: (implies (and (fn-sccb-treep c) (< (+ 1 (len (fn-scc-encode c))) *fn-scc-u64-bound*) (< (fn-scc-value-sequence c) *fn-scc-u64-bound*)) (equal (fn-sccr-decode-plan (mv-nth 0 (fn-sccb-plan c seg st)) (mv-nth 1 (fn-sccb-plan c seg st))) (list :ok c))): the buffer decode of the writer's plan over the buffer it leaves is the value, the inverse of fn-sccb-plan-is-file-octets (PRF-133). The twin fn-sccr-decode-plan-is-decode-segments: for a well-shaped plan (fn-sccr-planp: 37-octet headers, 32-octet trailers, ranges within the buffer, contiguous) and any buffer contents, corrupt ones included, (equal (fn-sccr-decode-plan plan st) (fn-scc-decode-segments (fn-sccr-plan-segments plan st))), the frames' octets being fn-sccb-frame-octets, what the host's file bytes are; the verdicts (:header, :segment, :truncated, :tree, :value) agree, and a mis-shaped plan is (:refused :layout), a verdict the list decoder never gives (fn-sccr-decode-plan-refuses-layout-by-definition, the branch by definition). fn-sccr-run-is-run: the index machine over the cells [i, end) is fn-scc-run over that slice. fn-sccr-admitted-within-bounds: a segment ACL2 admits (fn-sccr-admit-segment, called per segment before the host reads it, host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sco-segment-admit) has the extent the codec sizes it, within the profile's segment bound and, with the running total, within the file bound fn-sccr-file-read-bound (three times max-history-octets plus one segment's framing); a refusal is named :exceeds-bound, which fn-sco-select maps to (:full-replay :checkpoint-exceeds-bound). Every executable function is guard-verified. What it does not say: that the host's plan holds the file's bytes (A-HOST, as for every buffer fill); anything about the seal's digest beyond fn-frame-trailer being closed (the seal reads each chunk once as a transient list of at most one segment, as the writer does); or that the file bound admits every checkpoint of an admitted history (it is a policy from the profile: past it the journal replays).
proofs.progress_note: Lane rep-wave-d-3 (2026-09-26): certified on persvati (run-20260926T051724Z-bab6, ACL2 8.7 w25/acl2-literal, 2 jobs, 300 s: passed 6, failed 0, no book over 10 s) after every form was admitted in the REPL; the twin fn-sccr-decode-plan-is-decode-segments is the book's one costly proof. The native checkpoint module and the reopen rows are in the record.

proofs.title: A re-signed carrier of an accepted signed source is a D25 conflict at the signed control route; only the saved artifact is already stored
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-rcl-existing-action (books/store-reclaim.lisp), which host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author asks through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action on the octets fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets computes, before it commits. fn-sr-a-re-signed-carrier-is-a-conflict (books/consumer-artifact-retry): the held payload under Message-ID M is fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets of source S, principal P, keys K and signatures S1 at clock A; the same S, P and K with signatures S2 different from S1, at any clock B and for any groups, both plans naming M, is :conflict. It instantiates fn-sr-a-changed-source-is-a-conflict (PRF-117) through fn-cra-a-re-signed-carrier-is-other-octets: two rendered carriers (fn-hc-render-at-most) of one source, principal and key set with different signatures are different octets (folding inserts only octets outside the base64 alphabet, base64 round-trips, and the canonical carrier decodes to exactly its signatures, fn-hc-decode-at-of-encode-at). The same artifact resent is :duplicate by fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (PRF-117, cited, not restated). Together they are the fn side of CNS-003: a client that resends its saved artifact gets D25's duplicate; one that re-signs gets a conflict. Not claimed: that the two Message-ID and the two nonempty-octet hypotheses are necessary (they are the instantiated keystone's; no conclusion-failing witness exists at the fixture and the weakened theorem is not proved), anything about the Python consumer (an external client), or that a revoked author's resend reaches D25 (the enrolment check refuses it first; PKT-322).

proofs.title: An accepted key statement whose key change a crash cut finishes at the restart under its own admission context, never under today's configuration
proofs.statement: fn-ks-accepted-statement-finishes-under-its-admission-context: when every record of the admission journal CONFIGS is at or before the statement EVENT's txid, CONFIGS replays (fn-config-replay RESERVED CEILING CONFIGS is not :fault), and every record of MORE is later than the txid, fn-ks-recover-recorded (fn-ks-cut RECORDS SNAPSHOTS EVENT) (append CONFIGS MORE) OBSERVED ED ML SEQUENCE TXID STORE-GENERATION equals fn-ks-accept RECORDS SNAPSHOTS EVENT under the authorities of CONFIGS' replay (the live grants the acceptance read). Subject fn-ks-recover-recorded, the open's recovery: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover -> fnn-owner-key-statement with AT-OPEN, rows host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-rows = fn-ks-statement-rows (books/key-statements.lisp). Built on fn-ks-recorded-recovery-completes-the-cut and fn-ks-reopen-is-blind-to-later-configuration (PRF-124). No true-listp hypothesis (a replaying journal is a true list, fn-ks-config-replay-needs-a-true-list). Teeth: tests/acl2/key-statements-tests.lisp (grant at the txid, cut, revoke one txid later: recovery enrols; one must-fail per hypothesis). Not covered: a journal missing records through the txid is unreachable, not refused by a theorem here (the open faults :config-sequence; no transition removes a configuration record); the host-to-model correspondence of fnn-owner-key-statement is by construction (it calls fn-ks-plan/fn-ks-execute over the same rows), not a theorem.

proofs.title: One BP arrival's fragment selection reads the held rows' primary blocks and re-encodes and plans only rows whose family holds its offset-zero fragment, answering what the reference selector answers
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-fragment-step.lisp: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-fragment-progress (called after every accepted arrival by fnn-bps-receive and at open by fnn-bps-open) calls fn-bpnf-family-next, whose :exec (guard verified in books/bp-node-fragment-guards.lisp) is (fn-bpnf-family-select st (fn-bpnf-held-list st) observation nil (fn-bpnf-zero-family-keys (fn-bpnf-held-list st))). fn-bpnf-zero-family-keys collects, from each row's primary block alone, the family key (principal, ADU key, coherence key) of every candidate row (fn-bpnf-fragment-candidatep: primary block, fragment flag, not deleted, not consumed; fn-bpnf-active-fragment-is-candidate) at offset zero. fn-bpnf-family-select-is-aux: for HELD a subset of the held list, TRIED a list of family keys every active held row of which has a plan that is not ready (fn-bpnf-family-keys-not-readyp, true of nil), and ZERO those offset-zero keys, the select equals fn-bpnf-family-next-aux, the reference selector (the anchor included); with fn-bpnf-family-next-memo-is-aux both equal the memo it replaces. fn-bpnf-family-without-zero-key-is-not-ready: a held active row whose family key has no offset-zero candidate has a plan that is not ready (from fn-bpnf-family-without-offset-zero-is-not-ready, PRF-134). Work, counted over the select's own control flow: fn-bpnf-family-select-plans-bound: the rows the select re-encodes (fn-bpnf-active-fragmentp, whose fn-bpnf-heldp re-encodes the bundle) and plans (fn-bpnf-family-plan-at, whose reassembly is linear in the family's octets, PRF-121) are at most the candidate rows whose family key is in ZERO; fn-bpnf-family-select-steps-bound: a call that plans no row makes at most |held| * (1 + |zero| + |tried|) header steps (one visit and the key comparisons of its two membership tests per row). So an arrival into a family whose offset-zero fragment is not held re-encodes no held row. Scope: the maintained relation is the call's own (TRIED, established empty at each host call and preserved by each step of the walk); nothing is carried across calls. A family whose offset-zero fragment is held is planned on every call until it is complete (its plan is linear in its octets): a family arriving in offset order costs its octets per arrival (PKT-308). The session's post-arrival scans ask every held row the same kind of question: books/bp-app-handoff.lisp fn-bpah-local-pendingp (per row in fn-bpah-select-oldest-at and -uncertain-at, host fnn-bpnode-dispatch-pending) and books/bp-report-observe.lisp fn-bpn-report-observe-held (per row in fn-bpn-report-observe-next, host fnn-bpnode-observe-reports) now have an :exec (mbe, guard verified; their :logic bodies and every statement about them unchanged) that reads the row's primary block first: fn-bpnf-held-nonfragment-headerp and fn-bpnf-held-administrative-headerp (books/bp-node-foundation.lisp). fn-bpah-local-pendingp-has-a-nonfragment-header and fn-bpn-report-observe-held-needs-an-administrative-header state why the prefilter refuses only rows the definition refuses (with fn-bpnf-heldp-primary-blockp: a held row's primary block is a block), so a fragment row costs those scans its header, not a re-encoding. The expiry scan books/bp-report-deletion.lisp fn-bpn-report-find-expired-held (host fnn-bpnode-delete-expired, after every session) asked fn-bpnf-heldp twice per row (fn-bpn-report-held-delete-pendingp and fn-bpah-held-expiry); its :exec asks first fn-bpah-held-expiry-header (books/bp-app-handoff-time.lisp: the same clock decision read from the primary block and the anchor), and fn-bpah-held-expiry-header-of-held equates it with fn-bpah-held-expiry on every held row, so a live row costs the scan its header. The receive step's own per-row work (fn-bpnf-held-octets walks each held wire's length, fn-bpnf-find-held compares keys) is outside these theorems.

proofs.title: store rollback-check --snapshot: an earlier state of this history exactly when the snapshot's committed records are this store's first records, compared octet for octet, and the count is the records after them
proofs.statement: books/native-operator.lisp. host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-rollback-snapshot acquires both stores read-only under their shared writer locks (fnn-acquire; a store an owner holds is refused, never read unlocked) and holds both while it reads each committed history as the open reads it (fnn-rollback-history: fnn-durable-records from the selected pack's lower bound, the pack's records through *fnn-pack-recover-callback*, i.e. fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe, then the suffix files; fnn-check-history-marker over the count) and calls fn-native-operator-history-start, then fn-native-operator-history-step once per snapshot record with the store's record at the same position (CUR-PRESENT nil past the store's end), then fn-native-operator-history-verdict with the store's record count (through the fn-native-operator-host-history-* wrappers). Both theorems are stated over that composition, V = (fn-native-operator-history-verdict (fn-nop-history-run (fn-native-operator-history-start) snap cur) (len cur)), fn-nop-history-run being the host's loop. KEYSTONE fn-native-operator-history-loss-is-ancestry: (and (iff (equal (car V) :loses) (equal (append snap (nthcdr (len snap) cur)) cur)) (implies (equal (append snap (nthcdr (len snap) cur)) cur) (equal (cadr V) (len (nthcdr (len snap) cur))))): the verb answers :loses exactly when the store's history is the snapshot's records followed by more records, and the count is the number of those records; otherwise (:refused :snapshot-not-a-prefix). fn-native-operator-history-loss-is-snapshot-loss: V equals fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss (PRF-130's list-level function). Events are exact record octets: no sequence number, length or file size is compared, as a filter or as a count, and no collision assumption is used. Every executable function is guard-verified (guard t). What it does not say: that the host's loop makes exactly these calls (host code, source-checked by tests/test_native_rollback_history.py); anything about the configuration history, which a restore also replaces; that the snapshot is the newest earlier state; or freshness (a store-local comparison is not an anti-rollback witness, mandate 5.6).

proofs.title: The owner's admission and a BP contact's job selection cost what the request costs: the contact's selection is one traversal of the job list, equal to the two lookup scans (part 2, certified); the Store's maintained record count and octets (part 1) are held for a continuation
proofs.statement: Part 2. fn-bpnj-contact-next (books/bp-node-job-offer.lisp; host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact and host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-send-receipts call it before every offer) reads the gate, then traverses the job list once (fn-bpnj-scan), and equals the former two-scan answer over fn-bpnj-select and fn-bpnj-held on every state (fn-bpnj-contact-next-is-the-two-scan-selection), so PRF-120's theorems keep their statements; the scan's ready and held components are the lookup scans' from any examined prefix (fn-bpnj-scan-finds-the-selected-job, fn-bpnj-scan-finds-the-held-job), and under the machine's key uniqueness (fn-bpn-job-listp, the jobs field of fn-bpn-machine-statep) every job is its own entry, so the one confirming lookup succeeds at once (fn-bpnj-unique-keys-make-every-job-its-own-entry). Part 1 (the owner's committed record count and octets as maintained Store state, equal to the fold) is not delivered: the attempt at 7f615571 extended the octets inside fn-sn-io through the constrained record encoder, which defconst evaluation cannot run; the continuation carries the count in the Store and advances the octet cache through the event index (planning/evidence/hot-path-scans-2026-09-26.md). Not covered: the per-contact drain still re-scans from the head per offer (PKT-324).

proofs.title: The Store's capacity is a resource vector maintained by every admission: a release per open undertaking and the maintenance release stay admissible, and every admitted history of mixed record kinds is within H and T
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-cvec-verdict-at (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-publication-verdict, every served non-article Store record, BP admission's retention included; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-publication-verdict), fn-cvec-article-budget-for (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, the served POST and BP transit, handed to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare), fn-cvec-article-verdict-at (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict), fn-cvec-debt-extend (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-record-debt, the carried (K . DEBT)), fn-cvec-config-generations (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-native-admin-authorize, handed to fn-native-admin-publication-authorize). The vector fn-cvec-roomp profile used bytes debt is fn-smr-roomp at (used+debt, bytes+debt*R), R the release ceiling 4096: the profile's gate admits debt+1 release records in turn. DEBT is the history's open undertakings (fn-cvec-record-debt: +1 per :undertake, -1 per :release), equal to the carried cache when valid (fn-cvec-debt-extend-is-the-record-debt) and moving as the ledger's :forward pins do (fn-cvec-admit-forward-adds-one-debt, fn-cvec-release-forward-removes-one-debt). Established at init (fn-cvec-admitted-profile-starts-held); preserved by every admitted non-release record with the debt its own undertaking adds (fn-cvec-admission-keeps-the-vector), by a release against an open debt (fn-cvec-release-keeps-the-vector), by the served article prepare (fn-cvec-prepare-keeps-the-vector) and the developer article verdict (fn-cvec-article-verdict-keeps-the-vector, and at any producer width with a u32 charge fn-cvec-article-verdict-keeps-the-vector-at-producer-width), by a reclaim (fn-cvec-roomp-antitone-in-octets) and a profile upgrade (fn-cvec-profile-upgrade-keeps-the-vector). fn-cvec-roomp-discharges-every-debt: where it holds, the j-th release (j <= debt) is admitted after j releases of at most R octets. The composed statement fn-cvec-admitted-history-keeps-the-vector / -from-init: a history of mixed record kinds each admitted at its prefix by the gate of its kind (fn-cvec-history-admittedp; an article within its figure under a u32 charge, PRF-126; every other kind within its publication ceiling, a premise its producer's codec discharges; a release only against an open debt) leaves the vector holding at the committed count, the actual committed record octets fn-sbud-record-octets and the history's debt, and is within H (fn-profile-replay-within-boundp) and below T. With no debt the vector and the gate are PRF-129's except for :undertake (fn-cvec-roomp-without-debt-is-the-reserve, fn-cvec-verdict-without-debt-is-the-reserve-gate). The charge component is pre-paid (fn-cvec-release-never-raises-the-charge). fn-cvec-config-publication-keeps-the-release-generation: a configuration record other than the retention rule is accepted only below max-config-generations.
proofs.progress_note: Lane capacity-vector (2026-09-26). The disk component is an environmental assumption (the observed free octets are not owned; a failed write is refused or uncertain, never torn). The history-level equality of the record debt with the ledger's :forward pin count is proved per transition, not over replay. Producers outside PRF-123/126 (the signed composite, peer-carried records) meet their kind's ceiling by their codec, a premise here.

proofs.title: A friend's invitation configures the inviter at the invitee: the accept's one configuration record sets the inviter peer from the invitation's signed address before the enrolment, and a crash between the two resumes as the enrolment without a second record
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-accept-record-configures-the-verified-inviter: a (:configure DELTAS) from fn-pinv-accept-record-plan RECEIVED OBS ED ML SNAPSHOTS PEERS (books/peer-invite.lisp; host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-accept calls it through host/peer-invite-host.lisp fn-pinv-host-accept-record-plan) has the invitation bound (fn-pinv-bound-document-p: the carrier verifies under the key set its body names and the inviter is its genesis principal), the inviter not enrolled with those keys in SNAPSHOTS, an Inviter-Port that is a port, the peer fn-pinv-inviter-peer (named and path-identified by Inviter-Path, transport (:nntp 1 Inviter-Host Inviter-Port (:clear)), inbound Groups, no outbound half) fn-cfg-peerp with auth (:principal INVITER-HEX), no row of PEERS under its name, and DELTAS = (fn-cfg-set-peer-delta peer). fn-pinv-accept-record-fold-configures-the-inviter: over fn-cfg-apply V GEN STAMP DELTAS (the fold fn-cfg-apply-record runs when the owner completes the publication) the peers table holds exactly the peer's rows under its name, and the accept record plan over the folded peers table is the accept plan, which is :enrol (the crash point after the record resumes as the enrolment, never a second record). Not covered: TLS words and the outbound half (the operator's peer add of the same name), the signature primitives (A-CRYPTO), that the address the inviter signed is reachable.

proofs.title: The limits of a public reader port as the host calls them: admission bounded by the total and per-address rows in force, a step budget per quantum that waits and never refuses, the none anonymous policy gating every reader and posting command 480, and no limit or reconfiguration dropping a connection
proofs.statement: books/public-exposure.lisp. The host calls: fn-exp-open through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-exposure-open from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client at every accept (it admits or refuses and opens the owner connection in the same call, over fn-ocfg-open / fn-ocfg-open-peer with the pinned AUTHINFO configuration fn-exp-pinned-acfg); fn-exp-charge through fn-owner-exposure-charge from fnn-owner-exposure-wait before every served step; fn-exp-observe through fn-owner-exposure-observe inside fn-owner-chunk after every served step; fn-exp-idle through fn-owner-exposure-idle on every receive timeout; fn-exp-release in the serve loop's unwind; fn-exp-health-lines through host/native-live-status-host.lisp for `health'. The limits are fn-exp-limits over the LIVE configuration value (rows written by `policy set', books/native-admin.lisp :set-exposure / :set-policy), the run's max_connections, ACL2's reading of the bound listener (fn-exp-address-publicp) and `[auth] required'. KEYSTONES: fn-exp-open-admits-within-the-limits-in-force (an open that returns an id happened only with the owner below the total and the address below its per-address limit in force, and leaves the address at most one higher and within that limit); fn-exp-open-never-exceeds-a-limit-in-force (no open carries an address past max(before, limit): a lowered limit closes nothing and admits nothing more); fn-exp-charge-bounds-steps-per-quantum (under a positive steps row a step proceeds only below the budget and leaves the address's count for the quantum within it; exhaustion is (:defer MS), never a close: fn-exp-charge-waits-and-never-closes); fn-exp-anonymous-none-gates-every-restricted-command (under the none policy the pinned configuration requires authentication, and for any session carrying it with no subject every restricted command -- POST included -- is 480, no submission, session unchanged: composed with books/nntp-auth.lisp's fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed); fn-exp-limits-never-drop-a-connection (for any limits, open, charge, observe and idle keep every registered connection; only release removes); fn-exp-idle-closes-only-silence and fn-exp-observe-closes-only-on-a-failed-login (the only two closes the book asks for). NOT covered: that the pinned configuration IS the session's (fn-auth-open-session and served.lisp's fn-served-peer-and-reader-open-under-the-same-policy state it; no composed theorem over fn-ocfg-open is proved here); that the host's loop makes exactly these calls (source, and the native campaign tests/test_native_public_exposure.py); a read-only anonymous level and a public-groups level (need an nntp-auth change, 281 dependent books: deferred, PKT-405); TLS renegotiation and handshake cost (OpenSSL, host trust); what happens behind a reverse proxy (every client one address).

proofs.title: The implicit-TLS listener is offered only beside its certificate and runs the STARTTLS session after the handshake; the operator's inspect answer is the store's lookup
proofs.statement: Over fn-served-dispatch (books/served.lisp), which books/owner.lisp fn-own-read-step calls for the host's fn-owner-tls-established, on the connection fn-served-open-group-indexed makes, which fn-own-open calls for the host's fn-owner-open (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client, implicit mode, after SSL_accept): fn-served-implicit-tls-is-the-starttls-session, under a well-formed policy (fn-auth-configp) with TLS available, STARTTLS on the opened connection emits the (:starttls) handshake effect, and the connection after the (:tls-established) event alone equals the connection after STARTTLS and then that event; fn-served-implicit-tls-session-is-protected, the event emits nothing, records the TLS layer and owes no handshake. Over fn-native-operator-result-run-implicit-tls-port (books/native-operator.lisp), which host/native/operator.lisp reads through fn-native-operator-host-result-run-implicit-tls-port to decide whether fnn-owner-run binds the second listener: fn-native-operator-implicit-tls-listener-needs-its-certificate, a port is offered only for an accepted run plan that is not --once, with certificate and key octets present, in 1..65535 and not the plaintext port. Over fn-native-operator-inspect-report, which host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-inspect calls with fnn-bridge-lookup-found-p's boolean: fn-native-operator-inspect-report-is-the-lookup, exit 0 and :accepted exactly when the store binds the Message-ID, exit 1 and :absent otherwise, and the printed line is the verdict's. The loader admits tls_port only beside tls_cert and tls_key and on another port (fn-ncfg-tls-port-okp, books/native-config.lisp), and native-config-show's round trip carries it.
proofs.progress_note: Certified on persvati (runs of 2026-09-26, manifests above) and observed natively on the r3 images; the live (owner-running) inspect answer is PKT-410.

proofs.title: A chain of packs reconstructs the history: contiguous digest-linked links compose one prefix, compaction extends it over the uncovered suffix, the open over the walked chain answers the history, reclaim and publication cuts keep it
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/checkpoint-host.lisp calls for host/native/checkpoint.lisp (fnn-pack-walk, fnn-pack-extend-chain, fnn-pack-recover-records, fnn-pack-retire-older-generations): fn-ccc-links-okp-composes-a-prefix (a walked chain is BOUNDARY exact Store events from sequence 0 under the newest frontier); fn-ccc-capture-extends-the-chain (fn-ccc-capture-link from the chain's boundary, frontier, generation and digest yields a link that, consed on, is again a chain whose records are a prefix of the history and strictly longer; the old chain is its tail); fn-ccc-capture-link-succeeds (it succeeds on a valid suffix); fn-ccc-chain-reconstructs-the-history (fn-ccc-observe-chain over the decoded chain and an observation holding, for every sequence from some N at or below the chain's boundary to the end of H, the record H holds there answers (:ok H frontier) when the chain's records are a prefix of H and the suffix is valid: no reclaimed file is needed, and the served view replays exactly these records); fn-ccc-reclaim-preserves-reconstructed-history (PRF-073 over a chain); fn-ccc-retire-plan-keeps-the-chain; fn-ccc-publication-crash-walks-old-or-new-chain (under the marker-old-or-complete-candidate and files-kept facts of the pack program, the walk reads the old chain or the new link on it); fn-ccc-links-count-within-boundary (walk fuel T suffices); fn-cverb-pack-decision-capture-succeeds restated over the chain capture. Joined with the reclamation work (pack-chain-join, 2026-09-26): fn-rclp-reclaiming-pack-is-a-first-link (books/store-reclaim-pack.lisp; when fn-rclp-decide answers :reclaim, the summary it hands host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-pack-publish-generation is, through fn-ccc-link-of-summary, a valid first link with no predecessor whose boundary is the selected chain's coverage and the whole committed history); the compact verb's temporary-space figure is the next link's (fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-disk, PRF-129). The between-links cut (pack-chain-link, lane pack-chain-cut): fn-ccc-chain-program is fnn-pack-extend-chain's link as a program (:publish, :select, then the cut); fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-walks-the-extended-chain (at the Nth cut the state is the selection's, from the lemma fn-ccc-chain-cut-state-is-previous-state that a :cut leaves the preceding step's state; the marker names link N and the walk from it reads links N..1 on the chain selected before, when the host's chain names each predecessor, its generations are distinct and its entries are the host's triples); fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-reopens-to-the-history (the reopen there answers the history under fn-ccc-chain-reconstructs-the-history's hypotheses over that chain).

proofs.title: A control article is offered to every peer whose outbound wildmat matches its Newsgroups names or its filing group, and an ordinary article's feed scope is unchanged
proofs.statement: fn-own-submission-offers-a-control-article-under-its-newsgroups-and-filing-group: for an owner O with a submission in flight whose octets classify :control (fn-own-feed-control-of, equal to fn-ctl-classify-octets whenever the article parses: fn-own-feed-control-of-is-the-filing-classification), a peer NAME of the feed table (fn-own-feed-tablep, fn-own-feed-entry-of) with an outbound half whose wildmat matches a group of the article's Newsgroups (fn-own-feed-groups-of) or its filing group (fn-ctl-filing-group of the verb), whose path-identity the Path does not name, which is not the origin and whose queue does not hold the Message-ID, is a member of fn-own-submission-targets O (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp; the host's intent calls it through fn-icar-submission-targets, equal to it, at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent, and the durable enqueue fn-own-feed-durable through fn-own-outcome, fn-own-control-outcome and fn-own-transit-outcome). fn-own-submission-target-of-a-control-article-is-in-its-scope: every target of a control article matches its base groups, its Newsgroups names or its filing group. fn-own-sub-feed-groups-of-an-ordinary-article: a submission whose octets do not classify :control has exactly its base groups. Not covered: the pull side (NEWNEWS serves by the filed group), the receiving node's acceptance of the cancel (PRF-097/C3's), RFC 5537 section 5.3's advice that a cancel's Newsgroups equal its target's (the author's, not checked).

proofs.title: The operator's `keys redecide MSGID` decides a stored key statement as a new acceptance under the grants in force at its own txid, repeats nothing at the next open, and is refused by name for a Message-ID that names no stored statement or a statement already acted; and the transit refusal class the owner prints is the seven-class admission verdict's refusal arm
proofs.statement: Subject fn-ks-redecide / fn-ks-redecide-plan / fn-ks-redecide-event (books/key-statements.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-redecide-find/-plan/-event compute over the owner's Store records, keyring snapshots and live authorities rows, called by host/native/keys.lisp fnn-keys-owner-redecide under the owner mutex (control request 12, `operator CONFIG keys redecide MSGID`). (1) fn-ks-redecide-decides-under-the-configuration-at-its-own-txid: when every record of the journal CONFIGS is at or before TXID and CONFIGS replays, the redecide under the replay's authorities (the live rows the host passes) equals the redecide under fn-ks-redecide-rows TXID CONFIGS (fn-ctl-config-at the redecide's own txid). (2) fn-ks-reopen-after-a-redecide (no hypotheses): the open's recorded recovery fn-ks-recover-recorded of the redecided state, under any journal and any coordinates, is the redecided state when the redecide committed a kind-3 change and the recovery of the unchanged state otherwise, so PRF-124 and PRF-140 carry over. (3) fn-ks-redecide-of-no-stored-statement-is-refused-by-name and fn-ks-redecide-of-an-acted-statement-is-refused-by-name: the plan is (:refused :not-a-key-statement) / (:refused :already-acted) and the state is unchanged. (4) fn-ks-redecide-of-an-unacted-statement-is-its-acceptance-decision: for a stored statement that has not acted, the plan and kind-3 event are fn-ks-plan and fn-ks-execute of it, so the PRF-098 keystones over them apply. (5) fn-ks-a-redecide-that-acted-is-refused-the-second-time: after a redecide that acted, when the statement's verdict generation precedes the keyring's next generation, the same MSGID is refused :already-acted under any grants. The record is the kind-3 change itself at the redecide's coordinates (no re-filed composite, no new record kind, no cut). Teeth: tests/acl2/key-statements-tests.lisp section PRF-166 (decline, later grant, redecide at a later txid; one must-fail per hypothesis; the generation hypothesis's removal is a CORRUPTED-STATE witness). Not covered: live rows = replay of fn-sn-config-history is the owner's maintained relation (P6/PRF-028, uncertified at the current digest), not proved here; the host-to-model link of fnn-keys-owner-redecide is by construction (it calls the named functions), as PRF-098. (6) fn-pcb-admission-verdict-refusal-arms-are-the-refusal-class (books/peer-carriage.lisp, PKT-240, no hypotheses): fn-pcb-verdict-refusal-class of fn-pcb-admission-verdict equals fn-pcb-refusal-class on every input; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-refusal-class, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-transit-class inside fnn-owner-attempt-transit, computes the former. Witnesses for all seven verdicts in tests/acl2/peer-carriage-tests.lisp.

proofs.title: One fn-wide outcome classification and one ACL2 code map: every native command exits code(classify(f, x)), the seven classes' codes are disjoint and fixed, a fence is the only 3 in every family, NO-STORE and the clock-undecided decode are refusals, and CONFLICT is a refusal that keeps every earlier FNCT octet
proofs.statement: books/outcome-class.lisp: *fn-outcome-codes* maps :accepted 0, :refused 1, :fenced 3, :fault 4, :usage 5, :interrupted 6, :not-connected 7; fn-outcome-code reads it. fn-outcome-code-separates-the-classes: distinct classes have distinct codes. fn-outcome-code-table-by-definition: the seven codes are (0 1 3 4 5 6 7). fn-outcome-code-is-fenced-iff-fenced: over classes, the code is 3 exactly for :fenced. Families: host conditions (fn-outcome-of-host-condition, called by host/native/io.lisp fnn-exit-code-for; the +fnn-exit-*+ constants are fn-outcome-code of their classes): fn-outcome-host-condition-fences-iff-indeterminate. Operator (fn-native-operator-exit-code = fn-outcome-code of fn-native-operator-outcome-class, called through fn-native-operator-host-result-exit-code by host/native/operator.lisp): fn-native-operator-exit-is-fenced-iff-uncertain; fn-native-operator-absent-store-is-refused now concludes exit (fn-outcome-code :refused), 1. Control (fn-native-control-status-exit-code, called by the operator post and hybrid clients): fn-native-control-exit-is-fenced-iff-uncertain; topic control fn-thlc-outcome-class. BP (fn-bprc-exit-code is fn-outcome-code; host fnn-bp-exit-code, fnn-bps-exit-code, fnn-tcl-exit-code): fn-bprc-run-exit-code-is-fenced-iff-fenced; bp decode (fnn-command-bp-decode renders fn-bprc-decode-exit-code): fn-bprc-decode-never-fences, the clock-undecided verdict exits 1. CONFLICT (PKT-246): :conflict appended to *fn-nctrl-statuses*; fn-native-control-conflict-is-a-refusal: for an owner control result in the admitted range, the completion status (fn-native-control-completion-status, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission for the operator post and hybrid-author) is :conflict only for an owner refusal of D25's :conflict word, it classes :refused and exits 1, and any other word passes the result through; fn-nctrl-conflict-keeps-every-earlier-octet: each status of *fn-nctrl-statuses-before-conflict* is sealed exactly as the enumeration before :conflict seals it. The round trip of :conflict and the older decoder's :bad are executed witnesses (the seal's digest is A-CRYPTO's constrained function in proofs).

proofs.statement: fn-hsig-injected-carrier-unserved-group-is-refused-by-name (books/hybrid-store-injected.lisp, KEYSTONE): for a signed source whose carrier the injecting agent admits under some served group list G1 (fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets non-nil under (fn-inj-make-config allow agent G1 max)) and a list of group names G2 (fn-inj-group-namesp), under G2 with the same agent, bound and clock: when every group the admitted decision names is in G2, fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets is the same octets and fn-hsig-injected-carrier-reason is nil; otherwise the octets are nil and the reason is :unknown-group. The host (host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author) calls fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets with the owner's live post configuration (fn-owner-live-post-config, the served groups of the configuration) and, when it is nil, answers (fn-nhc-author-refusal :carrier (fn-hsig-injected-carrier-reason ...)); fn-nhc-author-refusal-names-an-unserved-group: that word is :unknown-group exactly for the reason :unknown-group; fn-nhc-author-refusal-is-a-named-refusal: every word of every arm (enrolment, source fields, carrier, filing, event) is a control status whose class is :refused and whose exit code is 1. The owner of the unserved-group decision is the injection decision (fn-inj-decide's :unknown-group arm, reached through fn-hsig-injected-carrier-plan), not fn-own-control-decision: the carrier arm refuses before the bound submission, so the fnn-fault at the group-code lookup is not reached for an unserved group. KEYSTONE fn-replay-identity-step-never-admits-a-pre-c1-control-record: from any context the identity step (books/replay.lisp, unchanged) answers a context that is not :ok at the same cursor. KEYSTONE fn-replay-never-faults-on-a-pre-c1-control-record, over fn-sopc-classified-open (the function host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended calls on every open, full replay and checkpoint): when the identity fold of the prefix is :ok and the next record, at its own sequence, is such a record, the open of the history is (:refused :pre-c1-control-record TXID MSGID); fn-sopc-checkpoint-open-names-what-the-full-open-names carries it to the checkpoint open. proofs.title: A signed POST's identity prepare and a signed-entry lookup cost what the request costs, not what the history holds: the prepare stages without replaying the appended history, and the BP receiver's Message-ID lookups read a maintained index
proofs.statement: Part 2, the incremental identity prepare. host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-identity (called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit for every signed POST's kind-4 composite and every keyring snapshot) installs fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity, whose store step fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity stages through fn-spc-stage-record: the specification's candidate predicate without fn-sf-history-recoverablep over (append records (list event)) (O(N*L) per signed POST, PKT-223). fn-spc-related-identity-candidate-is-recoverable (books/store-prepare-correspondence.lisp): in a :reserved state satisfying fn-snt-relation, a candidate the prepare's gate has applied to the live node (consp (fn-replay-apply-record node event)) leaves the appended history recoverable at the frontier (by fn-snt-deferred-preparation-outcome). KEYSTONES fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity-is-sn-prepare-identity-under-relation: (fn-snt-relation s) implies (fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity s event) = (fn-sn-prepare-identity s event); fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-ocfg-step-under-relation: (fn-own-relation (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) implies (fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity oc event) = (fn-ocfg-step oc (list :store (list :prepare-identity event))). The premise is the article prepare's (fn-opc-prepare-equals-owner-event-under-relation): fn-own-relation conjoins fn-snt-relation, established at observed open and preserved by the owner transition family. They replace the hypothesis-free equalities of carry-kind, which held only because the function replayed. Cites PRF-117 (the D23 source decision) and fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (a signed retry is the D25 duplicate) unchanged: the verdict the prepare stages is the specification's. Part 1, the Message-ID index. The Store's derived event index (fn-sn-event-index, books/consumer-event-index.lisp) is a pair: the sequence trie and a Message-ID trie from each Message-ID to the article records the history commits under it (a plain record, or the record a kind-4 composite carries, decoded once when added: fn-cei-event-article), in history order. fn-cei-put extends both halves, so fn-sn-io's record-directory append (the one transition that grows the history) maintains it and every open's fn-cei-build establishes it. KEYSTONE fn-cei-msgid-records-of-correspondence: (stringp msgid) and (fn-cei-correspondencep index events) imply (fn-cei-msgid-records msgid index) = (fn-cei-article-records-for msgid events), the fold over the history; the correspondence is the maintained relation fn-ceis-indexedp (books/consumer-event-index-store-invariants.lisp: the index is fn-cei-build of the Store's history in every phase; fn-ceis-relatedp is its crash-tolerant weakening), established by fn-sn-initial (fn-ceis-initial-indexed) and preserved by fn-sn-io (fn-ceis-io-preserves-indexed: the record-directory append extends the index by the appended event), the five prepares, finish and recover. fn-bpaj-indexed-records-are-the-walk (books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp), the refinement lemma: under fn-ceis-indexedp the index answer is fn-bpaj-record-for-msgid's walk. fn-bpaj-record-lookup-fast, fn-bpaj-transit-record-lookup-fast and fn-bpaj-store-record-accepted-fast (host: host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-request-action through fn-bpaj-dispatch-fast; host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install and fn-owner-app-record) read the index; their -is-checked equalities carry fn-ceis-indexedp as refinement lemmas. Part 3, the relation carried at the host's live owner (books/owner-store-indexed.lisp, lane signed-history-index-2). KEYSTONE fn-osi-open-installs-indexed-store, no hypothesis: the owner host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended installs on every open path (fn-osi-open: fn-ock-recover-extended of the extended checkpoint; through fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover, fn-ock-install over fn-cpo-open-observed, whose opened Store carries fn-cei-build of the history it read) has an indexed Store. fn-osi-host-step-keeps-indexed: every owner host/owner-host.lisp installs (fn-ocfg-step for every owner event but the kernel crash, which the host never issues; fn-rcon-ocfg-io; the carried prepares fn-pcar-sbud-prepare and fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity; fn-ccar-ocfg-complete; fn-ccar-own-finish; fn-ocl-publish; fn-own-configure; fn-osb-install; fn-own-with-feeds; fn-own-transit-outcome; fn-acar-own-outcome; fn-ocfg-open, -open-peer, -read-step, -fault, -observe; fn-exp-open; fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix) keeps it. KEYSTONE fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed, no hypothesis: the Store of every owner the host reaches from its open by those transitions (fn-osi-live-store) is indexed; host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-accept-locked binds exactly that Store (fn-owner-app-bind-receipt-store) before each fn-bprj-request-action. fn-osi-live-dispatch-fast-is-checked and the live store-record, lookup and transit-lookup equalities hold over it with no index premise, and PRF-132's keystones are stated over it. Retires PKT-223, PKT-291 item (2) and PKT-330 item (3).

proofs.title: HDR :fn-enrollment over the host-called read is the pinned keyring view's enrollment of the recorded verdict's principal
proofs.statement: fn-own-read-hdr-fn-enrollment-is-the-pinned-enrollment (books/owner-enrollment-read.lisp): for a read of owner connection ID of O whose octets frame nothing before the last and whose last octet frames exactly the command line `HDR :fn-enrollment <msgid>` (the fn-octl-reader-hyps reader premises, one Message-ID argument that is an octet list), on a connection with buckets whose pinned Message-ID trie holds that Message-ID, (car (fn-own-read O ID OCTETS)) is the one-line HDR reply `0 ITEM` with ITEM = fn-enr-item of the connection's pinned verdict for that Message-ID (fn-stx-reader-lookup over fn-own-conn-verdicts) against the connection's control pin (fn-own-conn-control), whose keyring slot is the view's fn-own-view-keyring. fn-enr-item (books/nntp-enrollment.lisp) names the verdict's 32-octet principal and the state of its newest snapshot in that keyring (fn-hl-current-for-principal, fn-hl-history-row): active when the row is :active at the verdict's generation, retired when :active at another generation, revoked when the row is the tombstone; unenrolled with no snapshot; none no-keyring-view / no-record / no-principal otherwise (fn-enr-item-of-an-enrolled-principal). Host line: host/native/owner.lisp (fnn-owner-action 'fn-owner-chunk ...) -> host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix = fn-ocfg-read (fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read) -> fn-own-read. Supporting: fn-nntp-hdr-fn-enrollment-is-the-pinned-enrollment (the pinned dispatcher's arm), fn-nntp-enrollment-hdr-response-is-the-pinned-enrollment, and fn-own-reader-opened-after-completion-pins-the-finished-keyring (a reader opened after the owner's (:complete) pins the keyring fn-sn-finish produced, with fn-hls-finish-identity-current-enrollment the chain from a durable kind-3 record).
proofs.progress_note: Implemented as PKT-175's default (a) by lane reader-2 (2026-09-26); certified by persvati run-20260926T101927Z-0d72 (certify-20260926T101956Z-272280: 332 passed, 0 failed, 2 jobs; books/owner-invariants 11.8 s, over D26, open in PKT-437). proofs.title: An invitation code redeems at most one account, once, across a crash: the accounts slot keeps a redeemed row the same row, the redeem plan stages only an admitted delta and resumes as already redeemed, and a redeemed account's credential is in the connection's snapshot
proofs.statement: Over the configuration the owner replays at open (fn-config-replay-loop; the records fn-owner-reconfigure-complete publishes through fn-ocl-publish), a code's redeemed row in the tenth slot (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-accounts) is the same row after every later acceptable record (fn-acct-redeemed-row-stays-across-replay; per admitted delta list fn-acct-redeemed-row-stays), and fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses a redeem of a redeemed digest unless it carries exactly that row (fn-acct-redeemed-refuses-another-redeem). The redeem plan fn-acct-redeem-plan (books/accounts.lisp; a pure function of the configuration value, the stamp, the code, the login, the password, the host's salt observation and whether the snapshot already names the login) plans :redeem only of a delta the configuration admits at every generation and ledger, which redeems the code under that login with the verifier fn-authsec-enrol computes (fn-acct-redeem-plan-is-admitted-and-redeems); after that delta is applied the same code, login and password plan (:already-redeemed) under any later stamp, salt and snapshot (fn-acct-redeem-plan-after-its-redeem-is-already-redeemed: the crash after the publication's root barrier and before the reply); another login is (:refused :account-redeemed) (fn-acct-redeem-plan-refuses-another-login); an unknown code plans neither (fn-acct-redeem-plan-of-an-unknown-code-stages-nothing). The row keeps the verifier as text and fn-acct-text-verifier-of-verifier-text is the representation's round trip. The connection's credential snapshot fn-auth-config-with-accounts (books/nntp-auth.lisp; host-called through books/owner-config.lisp fn-ocfg-open from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open, and fn-ocfg-open-peer from fn-owner-open-peer) is a configuration, keeps the operator's credential for a login auth.toml names, and otherwise finds the redeemed row's credential (the login's local principal fn-acct-local-principal, the row's verifier, posting); composed with fn-auth-step-principal-login-binds-exactly-the-unique-match (cited) a redeemed account's 281 installs exactly that principal. The wire (friends-accounts-2), over fn-auth-step-pinned (the dispatcher books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls, reached by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read, and by the owner's re-entry fn-owner-account-outcome, host/native-admin-host.lisp, through fn-ocfg-read-step): XREDEEM before a TLS layer on a protected-only listener answers 483 and changes nothing (fn-auth-step-pinned-xredeem-before-tls-is-483); after 381, XREDEEM PASS PASSWORD answers nothing and holds the session (handshakingp, so the served fold stops) with exactly the cached code, login and password and no subject (fn-auth-step-pinned-xredeem-pass-holds-for-the-owner; a hold binds nobody and keeps the role, fn-auth-step-redeem-hold-keeps-the-role); a holding session answers the owner's (:account-outcome WORD) 281 exactly when WORD is :bound, else 482, and leaves the hold (fn-auth-step-pinned-redeem-outcome-answers-the-word). The owner's plan (host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-acct-host-owner-redeem-stage, run by host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-account-redeem under the owner mutex inside fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked) is fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan over the live configuration: where fn-acct-redeem-plan redeems, it redeems exactly while the credential table is under the profile's max-credentials, else (:refused :account-credential-bound) (fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound); the word fn-acct-redeem-word is :bound only for a resume or a :redeem whose publication answered :accepted, i.e. after fn-owner-reconfigure-complete installed the durable record (fn-acct-redeem-word-is-bound-only-after-a-durable-redeem); an unknown code stages nothing and is refused (fn-acct-redeem-word-of-an-unknown-code-is-refused); after its redeem is published the same request is (:already-redeemed) and :bound under any later stamp, salt, snapshot, count and bound (fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan-after-its-redeem-is-bound: the crash cut FN_ACCOUNT_TEST_STOP_AFTER_PUBLISH). Not covered: the lift of the wire keystones through fn-served-step's fold to fn-own-read (the fold's stop on handshakingp is books/served.lisp's, cited); that a guessed code finds no row is the crypto seam's preimage resistance (A-CRYPTO); P6's publication theorems are PRF-028's (uncertified at the current digest: cited, not claimed).

proofs.title: The cheaper committed-history marker programs PKT-079 and PKT-143 allow are refused by the contract they would refine: the deferred marker leaves A <= M <= D, and an unfenced or in-place marker is refused by the byte model's discipline and its crash images
proofs.statement: Over the history model of books/store-history-required.lisp (the host-called decisions fn-hmr-open-verdict and fn-hmr-catch-up, host/native/io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker and fnn-recover's catch-up; the marker written by fnn-mark-committed at host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-prepared) and the byte programs of books/byte-store-marker-program.lisp (fnn-mark-committed's syscalls): fn-hmr-deferred-commit is the step in which a live process answers success for record COUNT while the marker still counts COUNT (the marker of commit n renamed under commit n+1's reservation, the brief's shared later barrier). fn-hmr-deferred-commit-leaves-the-invariant: from any state satisfying fn-hmr-invp with a live process, the step leaves a state that does not satisfy it (A = COUNT+1 > M = COUNT). fn-hmr-deferred-commit-admits-a-lost-answered-record: from the same state, K = COUNT is below the answered prefix and (fn-hmr-open-verdict profile marker K) is (:admitted :marked K): the negation of fn-hmr-open-refuses-below-every-answered-record's conclusion, so a lost newest record that a client holds a 240 for is admitted by the next open. fn-hmr-deferred-commit-is-not-caught-up: D31 case (2) does not cover it, the catch-up over the shortened history writes nothing. The byte candidates fn-bs-marker-unfenced-program (the stage's fsync folded into the record's staging barrier: a fence drains one inode, so the marker's stage is unfenced) and fn-bs-marker-in-place-program (one overwrite of committed-history.json and one fsync) are refused executably: the model's discipline D1 (fn-bs-links-only-fencedp) rejects the first and D2 (fn-bs-never-overwrites-authorityp) the second, and on the K5 fixture a crash image of each (a garbled unit of the pending write, fn-bs-tear-write) holds a marker that is neither the old nor the new one: the open of a store that lost nothing refuses it, :history-short-of-marker 23 or :marker-damaged, so fn-bs-marker-crash-after-barrier-is-new and fn-bs-marker-crash-open-stays-admitted are false of them. fn-bs-marker-program stays the served program; its cost is seven barriers per commit, measured in the record; the one sound sharing (the next reservation renamed under the marker's root barrier before the acknowledgement) is a file-kernel and K0 change, PKT-441.
proofs.progress_note: Lane publish-program (2026-09-26, dev 17ff24aa). Certified on persvati (ACL2 8.7 w25 acl2-literal, 2 jobs, 300 s): run-20260926T102908Z-0df7, manifest certify-20260926T102932Z-378295, the book passed and the test book failed on a wrong witness (one garble selector for an eleven-unit write: the fixture's unit is 4 octets); run-20260926T103449Z-fa4d, manifest certify-20260926T103516Z-444060, the repaired test book passed; no book over 10 s. Teeth: a reachable history (open, one acknowledged commit, the deferred commit) asserting every hypothesis and conclusion of the three theorems, beside the served step at the same point (invariant kept, the open refused); the live hypothesis removed (a state that is not live: the identity step, the invariant kept, K not below A, a marker behind the history caught up); the invariant removed as corrupted-state witnesses (a marker above the history: the deferred step lands on the invariant and the open at K refuses; a marker behind: caught up). The byte refutations are ground images on the K5 fixture (byte-store-k0-marker-tests' pair): admissible choices, the observation neither old nor new, the open's refusal by name, and the served program's image at the same cut for contrast. Not claimed: a general theorem over the unfenced program's crash images (the ground counterexample refutes the universal claims); any program of the served path changed; the sound sharing (PKT-441).

proofs.title: The operator's daily verbs decide starting, stale and the exit scale in ACL2: health's code never overlaps the seven outcome codes, a held lock where an owner would listen is starting, and an offline control verb runs offline exactly when the lock was seen free
proofs.statement: books/native-health.lisp: fn-nh-exit-code-is-zero-or-past-the-outcome-codes: for every V, (fn-nh-exit-code V) is 0 or at least 19, and it satisfies fn-outcome-codep (books/outcome-class.lisp, reading *fn-outcome-codes*) exactly when it equals (fn-outcome-code :accepted); host: fnn-operator-execute-health (host/native/operator.lisp) returns fn-native-health-host-exit of the rendered report, which is fn-nh-exit-code (fn-nh-report-exit-of-render). fn-nh-exit-code-cases (exported): with at most eight outcomes the code is in (0 19 20..27). fn-nh-fence-of-starting-iff: with no clone fence and a route that did not reach an owner, fn-nh-fence-of is :starting exactly when the lock is :held and an owner would listen, and a free or absent lock is never fenced; host: fn-native-health-host-fenced from fnn-operator-health-report. fn-nh-fence-of-route restated over the fourth observation. books/native-control.lisp fn-native-control-liveness-decides: the offline executor starts (fn-native-control-liveness-offlinep) exactly when the lock was observed :free or :absent, the decision is :stale exactly when a socket node is present and the lock is free or absent, and it is one of :live :stale :offline :held; host: fn-native-control-host-liveness from fnn-operator-execute-admin, which removes a :stale node under the control-path lease (fnn-control-remove-stale-offline) and refuses :held without starting the executor.
