proofs.title: Pull liveness: a peer's 430 for a listed id is an answer of the class unavailable; the round goes on, the id holds the cursor for at most BOUND consecutive complete rounds and is dropped, logged, exactly at the bound; the counts are durable in FNPL
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls (fn-pull-session-step through fn-pull-session-step-pair, fn-pull-session-close, fn-pull-session-close-effects; books/peer-pull-session.lisp) and fnn-pull-journal-open / fnn-pull-journal-append call (fn-pull-journal-scan with its committed offset, fn-pull-records-replay, fn-pull-cursor-envelope; books/peer-pull.lisp). A peer's 430 to the round's ARTICLE for a listed id is an answer of the class unavailable: the round records the id, reopens the local transit connection (:reopen-local) and goes on with the remaining ids. fn-pull-session-step-marks-unavailable-only-on-the-peers-reply: a host step that changes the unavailable ids is a (:remote . octets) event after the preamble, in phase :article, and adds exactly the article in hand. fn-pull-session-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round (PRF-100's keystone restated; its conclusion strengthened per id, not weakened): if the host's close moves the advance count, the round is :done, every listed id drew 235/435/437 from the local node OR was answered 430 by the peer in this round with its consecutive count reaching the bound, the new instant is the peer's DATE less the overlap, and PENDING is nil; fn-pull-close-advances-past-all-answered-when-nothing-is-unavailable keeps PRF-100's conclusion verbatim for a round with nothing unavailable, and the old form is a must-fail witness in tests/acl2/peer-pull-tests.lisp. fn-pull-session-unavailable-id-is-retried-below-the-bound: an id unavailable with 1 + its count below the bound leaves the instant and advance count where they were (so the peer lists it again: RFC 3977 7.4, not proved) and a complete round journals its count as exactly one more; fn-pull-session-complete-round-past-the-bound-advances: a complete round in which every unavailable id reached the bound advances and clears PENDING, the log naming each id whose count reached the bound in that round (dropped exactly at the bound, never before). fn-pull-records-replay-is-the-replay: the records the open scans back from a journal of cursor appends (one :pull-unavailable frame per PENDING entry, then the committing :pull-cursor frame) fold to exactly fn-pull-replay's cursor, so fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut (PRF-100, cited, its statement over the four-field cursor) holds of the on-disk journal; fn-pull-records-replay-ignores-an-uncommitted-tail: unavailable records whose cursor record never became durable change nothing (and the scan truncates them). BOUND is the peer row pull-unavailable-rounds (`peer pull NAME SECONDS ROUNDS`), else the local policy *fn-pull-default-unavailable-rounds* = 5: a work bound on re-listing, not a data cap. Trusted, not proved: that the peer lists again what it listed for the same instant (RFC 3977 7.4).

proofs.title: The two-node consumer exchange: the receiving node's stored event keeps the carrier's authored source and both signatures, and the served poll report is the event's exact encoding or a named :oversize refusal
proofs.statement: (a) The subject is fn-pa-authorized-event, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit's :ok arm calls through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carried-event for NNTP and BP transit and served POSTs. fn-osp-authorized-event-keeps-the-carried-source-and-signatures (books/owner-signed-post): whenever it forms an event, fn-pa-carrier-form of the received octets is :ok; the event's authored source is exactly the carrier's source (nth 1); its article record is exactly fn-record-encode of the record over the received octets (so the stored projection holds the carrier); and fn-hsig-authorize-at holds of the carrier's source version, principal, keys, source and signatures (nth 4) with the host's primitive observations: the two signatures the verdict authorized are the carrier's. The hop-local Path may differ between nodes; the source and signatures may not. (c) The subject is fn-col-poll-report (books/consumer-owner-local), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll serves. fn-col-poll-report-fits-or-refuses-by-name (books/consumer-owner-local-progress): a non-page or empty page is fn-col-poll's answer unchanged; a page whose encoded report satisfies fn-ncl-poll-event-bytesp is (:poll cursor report) with the event's exact encoding (fn-col-poll-report-octets: fn-stxa-encode, or fn-rcon-record-encode-impl for a legacy record); a page whose report is octets longer than *fn-stxa-max-octets* is (:refused :oversize). fn-col-poll-report-is-a-page-or-a-refusal: never a write, so an oversize article leaves the position unchanged. (b) PKT-256's CORRUPTED-state witness for fn-cp-ack-writes-only-a-forward-declaration-in-scope's frontier premise and (d) PKT-262's witness (a consumer registered after an article polls it first: intended) are teeth in tests/acl2/consumer-owner-local-progress-tests. Not claimed: that the :oversize antecedent is witnessed concretely (it needs a report above 4,294,966,940 octets, reachable only for a profile whose record bound R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets*; PKT-467); an explicit skip past an oversize article (PKT-466); anything about the Python consumer (an external client whose lock, resend and correlation are its own bookkeeping under CNS-003); BP carriage (PKT-333 phase 2).

proofs.title: A login's signing binding is a row of the configuration the owner publishes live: at start and on `principal bind|unbind' the configuration binds every login as the credential file does, an open session is decided under the table its connection pinned, a connection opened after the publication under the published table, and the verb says `applied' only after the owner published
proofs.statement: Subject fn-lb-ocfg-gate (books/login-binding-live.lisp), called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-gate from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-served; fn-lb-sync-plan, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-bindings-plan from host/native/auth.lisp fnn-native-auth-publish-bindings (at start in fnn-native-auth-install and on control request 14 in host/native/login-bindings.lisp), whose delta lists are staged by fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas and published by fn-owner-reconfigure-complete (fn-ocl-publish) through fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked. (1) By definition (fn-lb-ocfg-gate-unfolds, not cited) the host's verdict is fn-lb-owner-gate (PRF of books/login-binding.lisp; its keystones apply) with the policy of the live configuration and the binding table of the in-flight submission's connection pin. (2) The delta (books/config.lisp :login-binding, code 17, rows (LOGIN PRINCIPAL-HEX "" 2) of the accounts slot): fn-lb-binding-delta-binds-the-login binds exactly the given principal (nil unbinds), fn-lb-binding-delta-keeps-other-logins leaves every other login, fn-lb-binding-delta-is-admitted is admitted against every configuration for a bindable login and a 32-octet principal. (3) fn-lb-sync-binds-every-login-as-the-file-does: when the plan is :ok, applying its deltas binds every login as the credential file's table does; fn-lb-pairs-deltas-set-exactly-their-logins is the fold; fn-lb-pairs-deltas-ignore-the-record-coordinates lets the host's records of at most 64 deltas compose. (4) fn-lb-a-publication-keeps-every-open-connections-table (no hypotheses): staging and publishing any change leaves every connection's pinned table; fn-lb-an-open-session-is-decided-under-its-pinned-table: over any owner trace that does not re-pin the connection, the gate decides its submission under the table pinned before the trace. (5) fn-lb-a-connection-opened-after-a-publication-is-bound-anew: with nothing staged, a durable publication of the binding deltas (the owner's history relation before, fn-ocl-config-historyp; no stale pin at the fresh identifier after, which fn-ocfg-statep implies) and a connection opened next, that connection's table binds every login the deltas name as the file does and every other as before. (6) fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-applied-only-when-published (fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-restart-unless-no-owner, restated with the owner's answer, stays its PRF's): `applied' only when the lock was not seen free or absent and the owner answered :accepted. Teeth: tests/acl2/login-binding-live-tests.lisp (a witness per keystone asserting every antecedent; one must-fail per hypothesis; the gate witness is login-binding-tests' constructed owner, the publication witness config-owner-live-tests' replayed ground owner) and tests/acl2/native-auth-admin-tests.lisp. Not covered: that the owner's live configuration is its history's replay across every publication (the maintained relation; PRF-028's fn-ocl-no-reader-observes-a-half-change is listed uncertified at the current digest and is cited, not claimed); the host's reading of the credential file (bounded transport, as before).
